topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A research laboratory needs continuous real-time solution of differential equations that model fluid dynamics while simultaneously logging discrete digital sensor readings. Which computer architecture is fundamentally most appropriate?

options.A: Pure digital superscalar processor with high clock rate
options.B: Hybrid computer combining analog integrators with digital control and storage
options.C: Mainframe optimized for high concurrent transaction throughput
options.D: Vector supercomputer focused solely on floating-point peak performance

explanation: Hybrid systems uniquely combine continuous analog computation (ideal for differential equations) with digital logic for discrete data handling and storage. Pure digital or mainframe systems lack native continuous-time capability; pure supercomputers are optimized for discrete FLOPS, not continuous analog dynamics.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In terms of architectural philosophy, the primary reason a traditional mainframe remains preferred over a modern cluster of commodity servers for core banking OLTP workloads is:

options.A: Higher theoretical peak FLOPS
options.B: Superior I/O channel architecture, continuous availability features and transaction integrity under extreme concurrent load
options.C: Lower total cost of ownership for scientific simulations
options.D: Native support for analog signal processing

explanation: Mainframes are engineered around high-bandwidth I/O subsystems, hardware-assisted transaction reliability and near-continuous uptime. Commodity clusters excel at parallel compute but typically require additional software layers to match mainframe-grade transactional consistency and I/O scale.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: An analog computer represents numerical quantities using continuous physical variables. Which of the following is an inherent limitation of pure analog computation that digital systems overcome?

options.A: Inability to perform addition
options.B: Accumulation of noise and drift that degrades precision over long computations
options.C: Requirement for binary encoding of every value
options.D: Lack of any form of memory

explanation: Analog quantities are susceptible to thermal noise, component drift and measurement inaccuracy that compound over time. Digital systems quantize values and can maintain exact bit-level precision indefinitely (within word-length limits).

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A climate-modeling center requires sustained double-precision floating-point throughput on the order of tens of petaFLOPS with massive inter-node communication. Which classification of system is purpose-built for this workload?

options.A: Mainframe with high RAS features
options.B: Hybrid analog-digital computer
options.C: Supercomputer (massively parallel or vector architecture)
options.D: Network of ordinary desktop workstations without specialized interconnect

explanation: Supercomputers are designed for extreme floating-point performance and high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnects required by tightly coupled scientific simulations. Mainframes prioritize I/O and reliability for business transactions; hybrid systems target continuous-time problems of smaller scale.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In a hybrid computer used for real-time flight simulation, the analog subsystem is typically responsible for:

options.A: Storing the entire aircraft control software in non-volatile memory
options.B: Solving continuous differential equations that model aerodynamic forces in real time
options.C: Performing high-volume database lookups of passenger records

explanation: Analog sections excel at continuous-time integration and differentiation of physical quantities (forces, velocities). Digital sections handle discrete control logic, pilot interfaces and data logging.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a supercomputer from a mainframe with respect to their design goals?

options.A: Both are optimized for the same mix of high I/O and high FLOPS
options.B: Supercomputers maximize floating-point computational rate and interconnect bandwidth; mainframes maximize concurrent transaction throughput and continuous availability
options.C: Mainframes are always faster in peak FLOPS than any supercomputer
options.D: Supercomputers cannot run ordinary operating systems

explanation: The architectural trade-offs differ fundamentally: supercomputers sacrifice some RAS features for raw compute density and network performance; mainframes emphasize reliability, I/O scale and mixed commercial workloads.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A system that accepts continuous voltage signals from sensors, converts them via ADC, processes the discrete samples digitally, and can optionally drive analog actuators is best classified as:

options.A: Pure analog computer
options.B: Pure digital computer
options.C: Hybrid computer

explanation: The presence of both continuous (analog) and discrete (digital) processing paths with conversion interfaces defines a hybrid architecture.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Why are pure analog computers rarely used for general-purpose business data processing today?

options.A: They cannot perform multiplication
options.B: They lack the precision, programmability and large-scale storage required for discrete transactional and administrative workloads
options.C: They consume less power than digital systems
options.D: They are inherently faster for all classes of problems

explanation: Business processing demands exact discrete arithmetic, complex branching logic, large addressable memory and programmability—capabilities native to digital architectures but poorly matched to continuous analog techniques.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In the context of computer classification by purpose and scale, a system that must guarantee near-zero unplanned downtime while processing millions of concurrent short commercial transactions is most likely a:

options.A: Vector supercomputer
options.B: Mainframe
options.C: Analog differential analyzer

explanation: Mainframes are specifically engineered for extreme reliability (RAS), massive concurrent I/O and transaction integrity—characteristics demanded by core banking and airline reservation systems.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A key advantage of digital representation over analog representation of numbers is:

options.A: Digital values can be transmitted without any form of encoding
options.B: Noise margins allow reliable regeneration and exact reproduction of discrete states
options.C: Digital systems require no power
options.D: Analog systems can store infinite precision without quantization error

explanation: Once a signal is quantized into discrete levels, noise below the decision threshold can be rejected and the original discrete value restored—something continuous analog signals cannot guarantee.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: When evaluating architectural suitability, which workload is least appropriate for a classic mainframe?

options.A: High-volume credit-card authorization with strict ACID guarantees
options.B: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulation requiring sustained multi-petaFLOPS
options.C: Airline reservation system with continuous 24×7 availability
options.D: Batch processing of end-of-day banking settlements

explanation: Molecular dynamics is a tightly coupled floating-point intensive scientific workload classically assigned to supercomputers. Mainframes target transactional and commercial I/O-bound workloads.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In a hybrid computer, the role of the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is to:

options.A: Amplify continuous signals without quantization
options.B: Translate continuous physical quantities into discrete digital values that the digital subsystem can process
options.C: Store analog waveforms indefinitely
options.D: Perform floating-point division in the analog domain

explanation: ADC is the interface that samples and quantizes continuous signals so they can be handled by digital logic and memory.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following best characterizes the programming model difference between traditional analog computers and modern digital computers?

options.A: Analog computers are programmed by writing sequential instruction lists in a high-level language
options.B: Analog computers are typically configured by interconnecting computing elements (integrators, summers, multipliers) according to the equation being solved
options.C: Digital computers cannot solve differential equations

explanation: Classical analog computers are programmed by patching physical computing elements to realize the desired differential equation; digital computers use stored sequences of instructions.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A supercomputer’s interconnect fabric is optimized primarily for:

options.A: Low-cost commodity Ethernet with high latency tolerance
options.B: Extremely high bandwidth and low latency between compute nodes to support tightly coupled parallel algorithms
options.C: Connecting only storage devices

explanation: Scientific parallel codes frequently exchange large volumes of data with strict timing constraints; hence specialized low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnects are a defining feature of supercomputers.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In classification by signal type, a computer that processes only discrete binary values and uses Boolean algebra for its internal operations is:

options.A: Analog
options.B: Digital
options.C: Hybrid

explanation: Digital computers operate exclusively on discrete states (typically binary) and realize arithmetic and logic via Boolean operations and sequential circuits.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which performance metric is most relevant when comparing two supercomputers intended for climate simulation?

options.A: Number of concurrent OLTP transactions per second
options.B: Sustained floating-point operations per second on the actual application (or a representative benchmark such as HPL or HPCG)
options.C: Mean time between failures of a single disk drive

explanation: Scientific simulation performance is dominated by sustained floating-point throughput and memory/interconnect bandwidth under realistic application patterns, not transactional metrics.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A hybrid computer is particularly advantageous when the problem contains:

options.A: Only discrete logical decisions with no continuous variables
options.B: Both continuous dynamic behavior that is naturally expressed by differential equations and discrete control or data-logging requirements
options.C: Only high-volume commercial transactions

explanation: Hybrid architectures exploit analog speed and natural continuous representation for the differential parts while using digital precision and flexibility for control and discrete data.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In modern terminology, many so-called ‘hybrid’ systems in embedded and control domains actually implement the continuous dynamics digitally via high-speed sampling. The classical hybrid computer, however, used true analog computing elements because:

options.A: Digital processors did not exist
options.B: Analog integration can be performed with very low latency and without discrete-time approximation error for the continuous portion of the model
options.C: Analog elements consume more power
options.D: Digital systems cannot interface to sensors

explanation: True analog integrators operate in continuous time, avoiding sampling artifacts and offering potentially lower latency for certain classes of real-time simulation.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of mainframe architecture that is less emphasized in typical supercomputer design?

options.A: Massive aggregate floating-point peak performance
options.B: Extensive hardware and firmware support for continuous availability, dynamic workload partitioning and high-volume mixed I/O
options.C: Specialized vector pipelines
options.D: Use of commodity Ethernet as the primary interconnect

explanation: Mainframes invest heavily in RAS (Reliability, Availability, Serviceability) features and sophisticated I/O subsystems to keep commercial workloads running with minimal interruption.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A pure digital computer can approximate the behavior of an analog computer for continuous systems by:

options.A: Using only integer arithmetic
options.B: Employing numerical methods (e.g., Runge–Kutta, multistep integrators) on discrete time steps
options.C: Eliminating all floating-point units

explanation: Digital simulation of continuous dynamics relies on discretization in time and numerical integration algorithms that approximate the solution of differential equations.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In ranking computer classes by typical peak floating-point capability for scientific workloads, the usual order from highest to lowest is:

options.A: Mainframe > Supercomputer > Workstation
options.B: Supercomputer > High-end server / mainframe > Ordinary workstation
options.C: Analog computer > Supercomputer > Digital mainframe

explanation: Supercomputers are purpose-built for maximum floating-point throughput; mainframes and high-end servers follow; ordinary workstations trail significantly.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which statement about precision is correct?

options.A: Analog computers can represent any real number with infinite precision limited only by physical noise and component tolerances
options.B: Digital computers can represent any real number exactly with a finite number of bits
options.C: Both analog and digital systems have identical precision characteristics

explanation: In theory an analog quantity is continuous; in practice precision is limited by noise, drift and measurement. Digital systems have finite, exactly known precision determined by word length and format.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A data center that must simultaneously run large-scale weather models and high-volume online transaction processing would most likely deploy:

options.A: Only analog computers
options.B: A combination of supercomputers (or HPC clusters) for the scientific workload and mainframes or high-end transactional servers for the OLTP workload
options.C: Only mainframes for both workloads

explanation: The two workloads have fundamentally different architectural requirements; specialized platforms are chosen for each.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: The term ‘stored-program computer’ is most closely associated with which class?

options.A: Classical pure analog computers
options.B: Digital computers following the von Neumann (or Harvard) architecture
options.C: Mechanical differential analyzers only
options.D: Any system that uses vacuum tubes

explanation: The stored-program concept—instructions held in the same memory as data—is a defining feature of modern digital architectures originating with von Neumann and contemporaries.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In a hybrid computer used for process control, the digital portion typically handles:

options.A: Only the continuous integration of sensor voltages
options.B: Supervisory control logic, sequencing, data logging, operator interfaces and discrete decision making
options.C: Nothing; the analog section does all work

explanation: Digital subsystems provide the flexibility required for complex logic, user interaction and historical data storage that pure analog systems handle poorly.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following is least likely to be a design goal of a supercomputer?

options.A: Maximizing sustained application FLOPS
options.B: Minimizing interconnect latency and maximizing bandwidth
options.C: Providing the absolute highest level of continuous commercial transaction availability with mixed I/O workloads
options.D: Supporting efficient parallel programming models (MPI, OpenMP, etc.)

explanation: While supercomputers have good reliability, the extreme RAS and mixed commercial I/O features are the hallmark of mainframes rather than pure HPC systems.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: An analog computer solves a differential equation by:

options.A: Executing a sequence of binary instructions stored in memory
options.B: Physically interconnecting electronic (or mechanical) computing elements whose voltages or shaft positions continuously obey the same equations
options.C: Using only lookup tables
options.D: Compiling the equation into Java bytecode

explanation: Analog computation is performed by physical analogy: the circuit or mechanism is built so that its continuous behavior mirrors the mathematical model.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Modern high-performance computing systems sometimes incorporate specialized accelerators (GPUs, FPGAs, AI chips). These systems are still classified as digital computers because:

options.A: They use continuous voltage levels for all internal computation
options.B: All computation is performed on discrete binary representations, even if the functional units are highly parallel or application-specific
options.C: They contain no memory

explanation: Regardless of specialization, the underlying representation and arithmetic remain discrete (digital).

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A key reason digital computers displaced analog computers for most scientific work is:

options.A: Digital systems are always slower
options.B: Programmability, precision control, reproducibility and the ability to handle complex logic and large data sets favored digital approaches as technology advanced
options.C: Analog computers could not solve differential equations

explanation: Once digital hardware became fast enough and memory large enough, the advantages of exact arithmetic, flexible software and data handling outweighed the continuous-time elegance of analog machines for the majority of problems.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In the taxonomy of computers by size and capability, a system that occupies a large climate-controlled room, supports thousands of simultaneous users or transactions, and is managed by a specialized operations staff is typically a:

options.A: Microcomputer
options.B: Mainframe or large-scale server complex
options.C: Handheld calculator

explanation: Mainframes and their modern large-server descendants are characterized by physical scale, multi-user/transaction capacity and professional operational environments.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following statements about hybrid computers is most accurate in contemporary practice?

options.A: They have completely disappeared
options.B: True analog-digital hybrid systems still appear in specialized real-time simulation and certain control applications, while many ‘hybrid’ embedded systems are purely digital with high-speed sampling
options.C: They are the dominant architecture for web servers
options.D: They cannot interface to digital networks

explanation: Classical hybrid machines retain niches where continuous-time fidelity matters; most modern control systems approximate continuous behavior digitally.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A supercomputer node typically contains:

options.A: Only a single scalar processor with no vector or SIMD capability
options.B: Multiple high-performance cores or specialized floating-point units, large memory bandwidth and a high-speed network interface
options.C: Only analog computing elements

explanation: Modern supercomputer nodes are dense digital compute engines optimized for floating-point work and communication.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: When a problem is described by a set of ordinary differential equations with a modest number of state variables and requires real-time continuous solution, a classical hybrid or pure analog approach may still be considered because:

options.A: Digital computers cannot solve differential equations at all
options.B: Analog integration can offer very low latency and avoid discrete-time step-size constraints for that specific continuous dynamics
options.C: Analog systems have infinite digital storage
options.D: Mainframes are slower for all problems

explanation: For certain real-time continuous control or simulation tasks the latency and continuous nature of analog computation remain attractive.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which metric is more characteristic of mainframe evaluation than of supercomputer evaluation?

options.A: HPL (High-Performance Linpack) rating
options.B: Transactions per second under mixed commercial workload with strict response-time percentiles and continuous availability
options.C: Peak double-precision FLOPS

explanation: Mainframes are judged by transactional throughput, response-time distribution and uptime under realistic business mixes.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Digital computers achieve reliable long-term storage of numerical results primarily because:

options.A: They use continuous voltage levels that never change
options.B: Discrete states can be regenerated, error-corrected and copied without progressive degradation
options.C: They require no power to retain data
options.D: They store data only in analog capacitors

explanation: Binary (or multi-level discrete) representations allow perfect regeneration and the application of error-correcting codes, preventing the cumulative drift inherent in pure analog storage.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In classifying computers by the type of data they process, a system that accepts both continuous sensor voltages and discrete digital commands, processes them in their respective domains, and produces both analog actuator signals and digital status outputs is:

options.A: Purely digital
options.B: Purely analog
options.C: Hybrid

explanation: The coexistence of continuous and discrete processing paths defines the hybrid class.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A major historical limitation of large analog computers was:

options.A: They could not solve any differential equations
options.B: Setup (patching) time, limited precision, difficulty of storing programs and results, and poor suitability for discrete logic and large data sets
options.C: They were always faster than digital machines of the same era

explanation: Practical analog machines suffered from cumbersome programming, drift, and inability to handle the discrete and data-intensive aspects of many problems.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following workloads maps most naturally onto a supercomputer rather than a mainframe?

options.A: Processing millions of short debit/credit transactions per hour with full ACID semantics
options.B: Performing a global climate simulation that requires solving coupled partial differential equations on a fine spatial grid for decades of simulated time
options.C: Maintaining a 24×7 airline reservation database
options.D: Running a large corporate payroll batch job

explanation: Tightly coupled, floating-point-intensive, long-running scientific simulations are the classic supercomputer domain.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In a digital computer the fundamental unit of information is the bit. In a pure analog computer the corresponding notion is best described as:

options.A: A discrete binary digit
options.B: A continuous physical quantity (voltage, current, shaft angle, etc.) whose value represents a real number within the machine’s dynamic range
options.C: A fixed-size byte

explanation: Analog machines encode information directly in continuous physical variables.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Modern mainframes continue to be used in financial institutions primarily because of:

options.A: Their superior performance on LINPACK benchmarks
options.B: Extremely high reliability, massive I/O capacity, sophisticated workload management and the ability to run legacy transactional applications with minimal change
options.C: Native analog computing capabilities
options.D: Lower power consumption than any other class of computer

explanation: The combination of RAS features, I/O scale and software compatibility keeps mainframes central to core financial systems.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A system designer must choose an architecture for a real-time hardware-in-the-loop simulation of an aircraft that includes both continuous aerodynamic equations and discrete avionics logic. The most historically appropriate classical choice would be:

options.A: A pure digital mainframe of the 1970s
options.B: A hybrid computer with analog section for the continuous dynamics and digital section for the discrete logic and pilot interface
options.C: A pure analog computer with no digital components
options.D: A cluster of commodity PCs without real-time guarantees

explanation: Hybrid systems were developed precisely for this combination of continuous plant models and discrete control/logic.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the relationship between precision and dynamic range in analog versus digital systems?

options.A: Digital systems have infinite dynamic range with finite bits
options.B: In analog systems, noise and component tolerances limit both usable precision and dynamic range; in digital systems precision and range are determined by the chosen numeric format and word length
options.C: Analog systems always have higher precision than digital systems
options.D: Digital systems cannot represent numbers larger than 1

explanation: Analog precision is physically limited; digital precision and range are design parameters of the number system employed.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In terms of software compatibility and longevity of applications, mainframes are noted for:

options.A: Forcing complete rewrites of applications every few years
options.B: Supporting decades-old transactional applications with high binary or source compatibility while the underlying hardware evolves
options.C: Being unable to run any modern operating system

explanation: A hallmark of mainframe environments is extreme backward compatibility for mission-critical business software.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A pure digital computer approximates continuous functions by:

options.A: Using continuous voltage levels inside the ALU
options.B: Evaluating discrete samples or series expansions and employing numerical algorithms whose accuracy depends on step size, word length and method order
options.C: Avoiding all mathematical functions

explanation: Digital computation of continuous mathematics is performed via discrete numerical methods.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which class of computer is most likely to be evaluated using both LINPACK and a commercial transaction-processing benchmark such as TPC-C?

options.A: A pure analog differential analyzer
options.B: A large mainframe or high-end enterprise server that may also host some technical computing
options.C: A single-board microcontroller
options.D: A specialized ASIC with no general-purpose capability

explanation: Enterprise systems are sometimes measured on both scientific and commercial benchmarks, although pure supercomputers focus on the former and pure OLTP systems on the latter.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: The fundamental reason a digital computer can implement an arbitrary algorithm (subject to resource limits) while a classical analog computer is more restricted is:

options.A: Digital computers use continuous signals
options.B: Digital stored-program machines can execute sequences of conditional operations and can be reprogrammed by changing memory contents, whereas analog machines realize specific equations via fixed (or patchable) physical configurations
options.C: Analog computers have larger memories

explanation: The stored-program concept plus conditional branching gives digital computers universal algorithmic capability within their resource bounds.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: In a modern context, when engineers speak of a ‘hybrid’ embedded controller they most often mean:

options.A: A system containing both a true analog computer and a digital processor
options.B: A predominantly digital system that also contains analog signal-conditioning, ADC/DAC interfaces and perhaps analog control loops, while the complex logic remains digital
options.C: A pure mechanical computer
options.D: A system with no digital components

explanation: Contemporary usage of ‘hybrid’ in embedded systems usually refers to mixed-signal designs rather than classical analog-digital computing hybrids.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Which of the following best describes the role of a front-end computer in a traditional supercomputer installation?

options.A: It performs all of the floating-point intensive computation
options.B: It handles interactive user access, job submission, file management and other tasks that do not require the full capability of the compute nodes
options.C: It is an analog computer
options.D: It replaces the need for an interconnect

explanation: Front-end (or login) nodes provide the user interface and resource-management services while the bulk of the parallel computation occurs on the tightly coupled compute fabric.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: A critical advantage of digital representation when transmitting data over long distances or storing it for long periods is:

options.A: Digital signals cannot be amplified
options.B: Discrete levels can be detected and restored by regenerators, allowing essentially perfect recovery in the presence of moderate noise
options.C: Analog signals never suffer attenuation

explanation: Regeneration of discrete symbols is the foundation of reliable digital communication and storage.

topic: 1.1 Types of Computers: Analog, Digital, Hybrid, Mainframe, Super Computer
question: Considering the evolution of computing, the dominant reason digital architectures became universal for general-purpose work is the combination of:

options.A: Lower theoretical peak speed and higher power consumption
options.B: Scalable precision, programmability via stored programs, reliable storage and transmission, and the ability to implement arbitrary discrete algorithms
options.C: Exclusive use of continuous physical quantities
options.D: Inability to interface with human operators

explanation: These properties allowed digital systems to absorb virtually every computational task once the underlying technology reached sufficient speed and density.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In the email delivery path, the protocol that transfers a message from the originating MTA to the recipient’s MTA across the public Internet is primarily:

options.A: IMAP
options.B: POP3
options.C: SMTP

explanation: SMTP is the standard inter-server mail transfer protocol. IMAP and POP3 are retrieval protocols used by clients; HTTP is used for web traffic.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A user accesses the same mailbox from a laptop, a phone and a tablet and expects folders, read/unread status and message flags to remain synchronized. Which protocol is designed for this behavior?

options.A: POP3 in its classic delete-after-download mode
options.B: IMAP
options.C: SMTP submission only

explanation: IMAP keeps the authoritative copy on the server and synchronizes state across multiple clients. Classic POP3 downloads and typically removes messages from the server.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which CSS layout module is specifically intended for two-dimensional arrangements of rows and columns, allowing precise placement of items in both axes simultaneously?

options.A: Flexbox
options.B: CSS Grid
options.C: Float-based layout

explanation: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. Flexbox is primarily one-dimensional (row or column).

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A navigation bar that must distribute a variable number of menu items evenly along a single horizontal line, with flexible spacing, is most cleanly implemented using:

options.A: CSS Grid with explicit row and column tracks
options.B: CSS Flexbox on the main axis
options.C: Absolute positioning of every item

explanation: Flexbox is optimized for one-dimensional distribution and alignment. Grid is more powerful but heavier for pure 1-D navigation.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Port 587 is commonly used for:

options.A: Unencrypted HTTP
options.B: SMTP message submission, frequently with STARTTLS
options.C: IMAP over SSL only

explanation: Port 587 is the standardized submission port for authenticated SMTP clients, usually protected by STARTTLS.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In the traditional email architecture, the component that accepts mail from a user’s client and injects it into the SMTP relay network is called the:

options.A: MDA (Mail Delivery Agent) only
options.B: MUA (Mail User Agent) acting as a submission client
options.C: DNS resolver

explanation: The MUA (Outlook, Thunderbird, etc.) submits the message via SMTP to an MSA/MTA. The MDA later delivers into the user’s mailbox.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes POP3 from IMAP regarding server-side state?

options.A: Both keep identical permanent server-side state by default
options.B: IMAP maintains folders, flags and message state on the server; classic POP3 treats the server primarily as a temporary drop-box
options.C: POP3 never deletes messages

explanation: IMAP is a true remote mailbox protocol; POP3 was designed for download-and-delete scenarios.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A responsive web design technique that allows content to reflow and resize according to viewport width without separate mobile sites is primarily achieved through:

options.A: Fixed-pixel layouts only
options.B: CSS media queries combined with fluid grids and flexible images
options.C: Server-side user-agent sniffing exclusively

explanation: Media queries + fluid layout units form the core of responsive design.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: When an email client issues a RETR command after authenticating, it is most likely speaking:

options.A: SMTP
options.B: IMAP
options.C: POP3

explanation: RETR is a POP3 command used to retrieve a specific message. IMAP uses FETCH; SMTP uses DATA, etc.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS, the main axis of a flex container is determined by the value of:

options.A: align-items
options.B: flex-direction
options.C: grid-template-columns

explanation: flex-direction sets whether the main axis is horizontal (row) or vertical (column) and its direction.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A web developer needs a layout in which certain elements span multiple rows and columns while others occupy single cells. The most appropriate modern CSS module is:

options.A: Flexbox alone
options.B: CSS Grid
options.C: Floats with clearfix

explanation: CSS Grid natively supports row and column spanning via grid-row / grid-column properties.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which protocol is responsible for the final delivery of a message into a user’s mailbox on the destination server after the message has arrived via SMTP?

options.A: SMTP itself in all cases
options.B: The local Mail Delivery Agent (MDA) or LMTP
options.C: POP3

explanation: After SMTP acceptance, the MDA (or LMTP) writes the message into the user’s mailbox store.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In modern email security, STARTTLS is used to:

options.A: Encrypt the entire SMTP session after an initial plaintext handshake
options.B: Replace SMTP entirely with HTTPS
options.C: Authenticate only the client certificate without encrypting the channel

explanation: STARTTLS upgrades a plaintext SMTP (or IMAP/POP) connection to TLS after the EHLO/capability exchange.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A CSS rule that applies only when the viewport width is at most 600 px is written using:

options.A: @media (max-width: 600px) { ... }
options.B: @viewport max-width 600px
options.C: A fixed <meta> tag alone

explanation: Media queries with max-width (or min-width) are the standard mechanism for responsive breakpoints.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which of the following is a correct characterization of MIME in the email system?

options.A: MIME is a transport protocol that replaces SMTP
options.B: MIME defines how non-ASCII text, images, audio and multipart messages are encoded and structured inside the email body and headers
options.C: MIME is used only for encrypting messages
options.D: MIME is a client-side display language

explanation: MIME extends the original 7-bit ASCII email format to support multimedia and international text through content-type headers and transfer encodings.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS Flexbox, the property that controls how free space is distributed among flex items along the main axis is:

options.A: align-items
options.B: justify-content
options.C: flex-wrap

explanation: justify-content distributes space on the main axis; align-items works on the cross axis.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A mail administrator wants clients to leave messages on the server and manage them remotely with full folder support. The protocol that must be enabled on the server is:

options.A: POP3 only
options.B: IMAP
options.C: SMTP submission only

explanation: IMAP provides remote folder management and persistent server-side state.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which HTML5 element is semantically correct for the main navigation links of a website?

options.A: <div class="nav">
options.B: <nav>
options.C: <section id="menu">

explanation: The <nav> element is the semantic container for major navigation blocks.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In the email path, DKIM is used to:

options.A: Encrypt the message body end-to-end
options.B: Provide a cryptographic signature that allows receiving servers to verify that the message was authorized by the domain owner and was not altered in transit
options.C: Replace the need for SPF

explanation: DKIM adds a digital signature over selected headers and the body, enabling integrity and domain authentication checks.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A CSS Grid container has two columns defined as grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr. The second column will occupy:

options.A: Exactly twice the width of the first column of the free space
options.B: The same width as the first column
options.C: A fixed 2-pixel width
options.D: All remaining space after a 1-pixel first column

explanation: The fr unit distributes free space proportionally; 1fr : 2fr means the second track receives twice as much free space as the first.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which protocol is connection-oriented and used by a mail client to submit a new message to its outbound server, often on port 587?

options.A: UDP-based DNS
options.B: SMTP (submission)
options.C: IMAP FETCH

explanation: Message submission uses SMTP (or the SMTP submission service) on the designated submission port.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In responsive design, a common mobile-first approach means:

options.A: Designing only for desktop and ignoring mobile
options.B: Writing base styles for the smallest screens and then using min-width media queries to enhance for larger viewports
options.C: Using only JavaScript to detect screen size
options.D: Creating completely separate mobile and desktop HTML files

explanation: Mobile-first starts with the constrained case and progressively enhances.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: An email message that contains both a plain-text version and an HTML version is typically structured as a:

options.A: Single-part text/plain message
options.B: MIME multipart/alternative message
options.C: SMTP command

explanation: multipart/alternative allows the client to choose the best representation it can render.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which CSS property is used to change the stacking order of positioned elements?

options.A: order (in Flexbox)
options.B: z-index
options.C: flex-grow

explanation: z-index controls the painting order of positioned boxes along the z-axis.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: SPF records are published in DNS primarily to:

options.A: Encrypt outbound mail
options.B: Authorize which IP addresses or hosts are permitted to send mail for a given domain
options.C: Store the user’s password

explanation: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) lists authorized sending hosts, helping receiving servers detect forged From domains.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS, the difference between justify-content and align-items in a flex container is that:

options.A: They are identical
options.B: justify-content works on the main axis while align-items works on the cross axis
options.C: align-items works only on Grid
options.D: justify-content is used only for text

explanation: Main-axis vs cross-axis alignment is the fundamental distinction.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A web page must support both left-to-right and right-to-left languages. The CSS logical property that sets the inline starting margin independent of writing direction is:

options.A: margin-left
options.B: margin-inline-start
options.C: padding-top

explanation: Logical properties (margin-inline-start, etc.) adapt to writing mode and direction.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: When a mail server advertises the capability “STARTTLS” in response to EHLO, a client that wishes to protect the session should:

options.A: Ignore it and continue in plaintext
options.B: Issue the STARTTLS command and negotiate TLS before sending AUTH or MAIL commands
options.C: Switch to port 25 only

explanation: The proper sequence is EHLO → STARTTLS → TLS handshake → EHLO again → AUTH / MAIL.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS Grid, the fr unit represents:

options.A: A fixed number of pixels
options.B: A fraction of the available free space in the grid container
options.C: A percentage of the viewport only

explanation: fr distributes remaining free space after fixed-size tracks are accounted for.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Mail Transfer Agent (MTA)?

options.A: Accepting messages from other MTAs or from submission clients
options.B: Routing messages toward their final destination based on DNS MX records
options.C: Providing a graphical interface for end users to read mail
options.D: Queuing and retrying delivery when the destination is temporarily unavailable

explanation: The graphical user interface belongs to the MUA, not the MTA.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A CSS technique that prevents a flex item from shrinking below its content size is to set:

options.A: flex-shrink: 0
options.B: flex-grow: 0
options.C: align-self: stretch

explanation: flex-shrink: 0 disables shrinking; the item keeps at least its flex-basis / content size.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In the context of web performance and design, critical CSS refers to:

options.A: All CSS of the entire website inlined
options.B: The minimal set of CSS rules required to render the above-the-fold content of a page, often inlined to avoid render-blocking
options.C: CSS that is never used

explanation: Inlining critical CSS improves first-contentful paint by eliminating an extra network round-trip for above-the-fold styles.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which header field in an email is most directly used by DKIM to identify the signing domain?

options.A: Subject
options.B: DKIM-Signature (containing the d= tag)
options.C: Date

explanation: The d= tag inside the DKIM-Signature header names the domain asserting responsibility for the signature.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A layout that must place items into a strict matrix of rows and columns, with some items occupying multiple cells, is best served by:

options.A: Flexbox with nested containers only
options.B: CSS Grid
options.C: Absolute positioning of every element
options.D: The HTML <table> element for non-tabular content

explanation: CSS Grid was designed exactly for two-dimensional, cell-based layouts with spanning.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: When an IMAP client issues a SELECT command on a mailbox, the server responds with information that includes:

options.A: Only the SMTP banner
options.B: Flags, existence and recent message counts, and UIDs relevant to that mailbox
options.C: The user’s password

explanation: SELECT opens a mailbox and returns its current status and permanent flags.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In modern CSS, the gap property (or row-gap / column-gap) is used to:

options.A: Set the margin of the container itself
options.B: Insert consistent spacing between grid or flex items without using margins on the items
options.C: Define the width of the viewport

explanation: gap provides gutters between tracks or flex items cleanly.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A phishing email that forges the visible From address of a bank is most directly mitigated for the receiving server by checking:

options.A: Only the Subject line
options.B: SPF, DKIM and DMARC authentication results for the purported sending domain
options.C: The time of day the message arrived
options.D: The size of the attachment only

explanation: SPF/DKIM/DMARC together provide domain authentication that helps detect forged senders.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between HTML structure and CSS presentation?

options.A: CSS should contain the primary semantic structure of the document
options.B: HTML provides the structure and meaning; CSS controls visual presentation and layout
options.C: JavaScript is required for any layout
options.D: Tables must be used for all layout

explanation: Separation of structure (HTML) from presentation (CSS) is a foundational principle of modern web design.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS Flexbox, setting flex: 1 on an item is a shorthand that typically means:

options.A: flex-grow: 1; flex-shrink: 1; flex-basis: 0%
options.B: The item cannot grow or shrink
options.C: The item is absolutely positioned
options.D: The item is removed from the flex flow

explanation: The common flex: 1 shorthand makes the item grow and shrink equally from a zero basis, filling available space.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A mail server that accepts messages from the public Internet on port 25 and then forwards them according to MX records is acting as a:

options.A: Mail User Agent
options.B: Mail Transfer Agent (MTA) / SMTP relay
options.C: DNS authoritative server

explanation: Port 25 SMTP servers that route mail are MTAs.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which CSS feature allows a single stylesheet to adapt typography and spacing according to the user’s preferred color scheme (light/dark)?

options.A: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
options.B: A fixed background-color only
options.C: JavaScript-only detection

explanation: The prefers-color-scheme media feature enables automatic light/dark adaptation.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In IMAP, the difference between a message sequence number and a UID is that:

options.A: They are always identical
options.B: Sequence numbers can change when messages are expunged; UIDs are permanent within a mailbox for the lifetime of the message
options.C: UIDs are only used by POP3
options.D: Sequence numbers are globally unique across all mailboxes

explanation: UIDs provide stable references; sequence numbers are transient and renumber after deletions.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A web designer wants images to scale proportionally within their containers without overflow. A common modern approach is:

options.A: Fixed width and height attributes only
options.B: max-width: 100%; height: auto;
options.C: Using only background-image with no sizing

explanation: max-width: 100% prevents overflow while height: auto preserves aspect ratio.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: DMARC builds upon SPF and DKIM by adding:

options.A: A policy mechanism that tells receivers what to do with messages that fail authentication, plus reporting
options.B: End-to-end encryption of the message body
options.C: A new transport protocol

explanation: DMARC supplies the policy (reject/quarantine/none) and feedback reporting layer on top of SPF and DKIM results.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In CSS Grid, the property grid-template-areas allows:

options.A: Only numeric track sizing
options.B: Naming grid regions with ASCII art-like strings so that items can be placed by name
options.C: Setting the z-index of the grid

explanation: grid-template-areas creates named areas that items can reference via grid-area.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which of the following is a valid reason to prefer IMAP over POP3 for a user who travels frequently and uses multiple devices?

options.A: POP3 always keeps messages synchronized across devices by default
options.B: IMAP maintains server-side state (folders, flags, read status) so every device sees a consistent mailbox
options.C: IMAP cannot work over TLS
options.D: POP3 supports server-side search better than IMAP

explanation: Server-side state is the core advantage of IMAP for multi-device use.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A CSS rule that targets only the first child element of a container uses the pseudo-class:

options.A: :hover
options.B: :first-child
options.C: :nth-of-type(2)

explanation: :first-child matches an element that is the first child of its parent.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: In the SMTP dialogue, after the server responds 250 to the MAIL FROM command, the client next sends:

options.A: QUIT immediately
options.B: One or more RCPT TO commands
options.C: The message body without headers

explanation: The envelope continues with RCPT TO for each recipient before DATA.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: Which modern CSS layout method is most appropriate when the design requires both a flexible header/footer and a central content area that itself contains a complex two-dimensional card grid?

options.A: Only floats
options.B: Flexbox for the overall page structure and CSS Grid for the card layout inside the content area
options.C: Tables for everything

explanation: Combining Flexbox (1-D page shell) with Grid (2-D content) is a common and powerful pattern.

topic: 1.2 Basic Knowledge of Internet/Email System, Web Design
question: A receiving mail system that applies a DMARC policy of “reject” will typically:

options.A: Accept all messages regardless of authentication
options.B: Refuse messages that fail SPF/DKIM alignment according to the domain’s published policy
options.C: Convert the message into a tweet
options.D: Store the message without any authentication check

explanation: A DMARC reject policy instructs receivers to reject unauthenticated messages claiming to be from that domain.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A data-center operator needs to prevent an authenticated employee from being followed into a secure server room by an unauthorized person. The most effective physical control is:

options.A: A single card-reader door
options.B: A mantrap (interlocking doors) with weight or biometric verification
options.C: A privacy screen on monitors
options.D: A Faraday cage around the building

explanation: A mantrap forces sequential authentication and prevents tailgating by isolating the person between two doors until the second authentication succeeds.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which control specifically mitigates TEMPEST-style electromagnetic eavesdropping on sensitive computing equipment?

options.A: Mantrap
options.B: Faraday cage / RF shielding
options.C: UPS system

explanation: A Faraday cage attenuates electromagnetic radiation, preventing signal leakage that could be intercepted.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a data center housing live servers, the preferred fire-suppression agent is one that:

options.A: Leaves a conductive powder residue on circuit boards
options.B: Uses clean-agent gas (e.g., FM-200, Novec 1230) that extinguishes fire without damaging electronics or leaving residue
options.C: Floods the room with water from ordinary sprinklers while staff are present
options.D: Relies solely on portable CO₂ extinguishers in occupied spaces without automatic release controls

explanation: Clean-agent systems are designed for occupied electronic environments; they leave no residue and are safe for equipment.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A privacy screen filter on a financial terminal primarily protects against:

options.A: Electromagnetic emanation attacks
options.B: Shoulder-surfing / visual observation by bystanders
options.C: Power failures

explanation: Privacy filters limit the viewing angle so that only a person directly in front of the screen can read its contents.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a Tier-III or higher data center, the combination of UPS + diesel generator is intended to:

options.A: Provide permanent free electricity
options.B: Bridge utility power failures and maintain continuous operation until generator power stabilizes
options.C: Replace the need for any fire suppression
options.D: Act as a primary cooling system

explanation: UPS supplies instantaneous power; generators provide sustained backup once they reach stable output.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct ordering of physical security layers from outermost to innermost in a typical high-security facility?

options.A: Server rack lock → building perimeter fence → mantrap
options.B: Perimeter fencing / gates → building access control → server-room mantrap / biometric → rack-level locks
options.C: Biometric only at the parking lot

explanation: Defense-in-depth applies concentric physical controls of increasing strictness.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A raised-floor plenum in a data center is commonly used for:

options.A: Storing paper archives
options.B: Cold-air distribution and cable routing while maintaining separation from hot exhaust
options.C: Housing the primary diesel generators

explanation: Raised floors traditionally deliver cold air and conceal power/data cabling.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which physical control is most effective against an attacker who has already obtained a valid access card through social engineering?

options.A: A single card reader that only checks card validity
options.B: Multi-factor physical authentication (card + PIN or biometric) combined with anti-tailgating measures
options.C: A privacy filter on screens

explanation: Requiring a second factor and preventing piggybacking significantly raises the bar even if the card itself is compromised.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In the context of environmental controls, the primary purpose of maintaining positive air pressure in a data hall relative to adjacent spaces is to:

options.A: Increase noise levels
options.B: Prevent unfiltered outside air and contaminants from infiltrating the controlled environment
options.C: Reduce the need for UPS

explanation: Positive pressure helps keep dust and external air out of the conditioned space.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A dry-pipe or pre-action sprinkler system is preferred over a wet-pipe system in a server room because:

options.A: It is cheaper to install
options.B: Water is held back until a confirmed fire condition, reducing the risk of accidental water discharge onto live equipment
options.C: It uses no water at all
options.D: It eliminates the need for any detection

explanation: Pre-action systems require both a detection event and a sprinkler head activation before water is released, protecting against false discharges.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a ‘hot aisle / cold aisle’ arrangement?

options.A: To maximize mixing of hot and cold air for uniform temperature
options.B: To separate supply (cold) and return (hot) air paths, improving cooling efficiency and preventing recirculation
options.C: To eliminate the need for CRAC units

explanation: Segregating cold supply from hot exhaust reduces mixing and raises cooling efficiency.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A biometric access control that measures the unique pattern of blood vessels in the finger or hand is an example of:

options.A: Something you know
options.B: Something you have
options.C: Something you are (physiological biometric)

explanation: Vascular pattern recognition is a physiological biometric characteristic.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In physical security design, the concept of ‘defense in depth’ applied to a data center means:

options.A: Relying on a single strong lock
options.B: Implementing successive layers of controls so that failure of one layer does not immediately compromise the protected assets
options.C: Removing all cameras to save cost

explanation: Multiple complementary layers raise the cost and complexity of a successful physical attack.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which environmental sensor is most directly relevant to preventing early-stage electrical fires in a server room?

options.A: Only a humidity sensor
options.B: Very early smoke detection (VESDA / aspirating) or ionization/photoelectric smoke detectors integrated with the suppression system
options.C: A noise-level meter

explanation: Early smoke detection allows suppression or shutdown before a fire becomes large.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A Faraday cage around a critical computing enclosure primarily protects against:

options.A: Unauthorized visual observation
options.B: Electromagnetic interference and emanation (both inbound and outbound RF)
options.C: Water damage from sprinklers
options.D: Power surges on the AC line

explanation: The conductive enclosure attenuates electromagnetic fields in both directions.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In access-control terms, a mantrap enforces which security principle most directly?

options.A: Least privilege for data
options.B: Controlled entry of only one authenticated individual at a time, defeating tailgating
options.C: Encryption of data at rest

explanation: The physical design forces single-person, sequential authentication.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about clean-agent fire suppression systems?

options.A: They leave a sticky residue that must be cleaned from every board
options.B: They extinguish fire primarily by interrupting the chemical reaction or reducing heat, without leaving conductive residue
options.C: They are suitable only for outdoor use
options.D: They require the room to be fully occupied during discharge for safety

explanation: Clean agents are electrically non-conductive and leave no residue, making them suitable for electronics.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A data-center design that routes cold air under a raised floor and returns hot air through a ceiling plenum is an example of:

options.A: Uncontrolled free cooling only
options.B: A traditional raised-floor cooling architecture
options.C: Immersion cooling

explanation: This is the classic raised-floor cold-aisle supply design.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which physical security control is most appropriate for protecting the contents of a display from casual observation in an open office?

options.A: Faraday cage
options.B: Privacy screen filter
options.C: Mantrap

explanation: Privacy filters restrict the viewing cone of the display.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a high-security facility, the purpose of a ‘sally port’ or vehicle airlock is analogous to a mantrap but applied to:

options.A: Only pedestrian traffic
options.B: Vehicles, ensuring that a vehicle is fully inside and authenticated before the inner gate opens
options.C: Only network packets

explanation: Vehicle sally ports enforce controlled, sequential entry for cars and trucks.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of using biometric authentication at a data-center entrance compared with a simple proximity card?

options.A: Biometrics are always faster
options.B: Biometrics bind the authentication to a physiological characteristic that is harder to share or lose than a card
options.C: Biometrics require no enrollment

explanation: A card can be lent or stolen; a biometric factor is intrinsic to the individual.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In the context of power continuity, the term ‘N+1 redundancy’ for UPS modules means:

options.A: Exactly one UPS with no spare
options.B: Enough capacity to carry the full load plus one additional module so that any single module can fail without interrupting power
options.C: Twice the required capacity with no modular design

explanation: N+1 provides fault tolerance against the failure of any one unit.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A security policy that requires all visitors to be escorted at all times inside the data-center perimeter is an example of:

options.A: A technical control only
options.B: An administrative / procedural control that complements physical barriers
options.C: A cryptographic control

explanation: Escort requirements are procedural controls that reinforce physical access restrictions.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following environmental conditions is most likely to cause electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage to sensitive electronics if not controlled?

options.A: Very high humidity only
options.B: Very low relative humidity combined with synthetic flooring and lack of grounding
options.C: Moderate temperature with proper grounding
options.D: Presence of a clean-agent suppression system

explanation: Low humidity increases the risk of static buildup and discharge.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a multi-tenant data center, cage-level physical security is intended to:

options.A: Allow any tenant to access any other tenant’s equipment freely
options.B: Provide each tenant with a locked perimeter around their own racks so that other tenants and unauthorized staff cannot reach their hardware
options.C: Eliminate the need for any access logs
options.D: Replace the building’s outer perimeter controls

explanation: Cages create tenant-specific physical boundaries inside the shared facility.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the use of CCTV in a data center?

options.A: CCTV alone prevents all physical attacks
options.B: CCTV provides detection and retrospective evidence; it must be combined with barriers, access control and monitoring to be effective
options.C: Cameras should never be recorded
options.D: CCTV replaces the need for access logs

explanation: Surveillance is a detective control that supports but does not replace preventive physical controls.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A water-leak detection system under a raised floor is primarily intended to protect against:

options.A: Unauthorized network access
options.B: Damage from cooling-system leaks or accidental water ingress before equipment is affected
options.C: Electromagnetic interference

explanation: Early leak detection allows intervention before water reaches live equipment.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In physical security, the principle of ‘fail-safe’ versus ‘fail-secure’ for an electronic lock refers to:

options.A: Whether the lock opens or remains locked when power is lost
options.B: The color of the lock
options.C: Whether the lock uses a key or a card

explanation: Fail-safe (fail-open) unlocks on power loss (life-safety); fail-secure (fail-locked) stays locked (security).

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate physical control for a rack containing highly sensitive cryptographic hardware?

options.A: Leaving the rack unlocked for convenience
options.B: A lockable rack with continuous monitoring, access logging, and placement inside a further controlled room or cage
options.C: Only a privacy screen
options.D: No special measures beyond the building perimeter

explanation: Sensitive hardware warrants layered physical protection including rack-level locking and monitoring.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A data-center operator notices that the cold-aisle temperature is rising while the CRAC units are running at full capacity. A likely physical cause among the following is:

options.A: Perfect hot-aisle containment
options.B: Missing blanking panels allowing hot exhaust to recirculate into the cold aisle
options.C: Excessive humidity only

explanation: Missing blanking panels create bypass paths that mix hot and cold air, degrading cooling effectiveness.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In the context of physical security, ‘tailgating’ refers to:

options.A: A network protocol
options.B: An unauthorized person following an authorized person through a controlled door before it closes
options.C: A type of malware

explanation: Tailgating (or piggybacking) is a common physical social-engineering technique.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following power-related designs provides the highest availability for critical IT loads?

options.A: A single UPS with no generator
options.B: Dual utility feeds + redundant UPS systems (e.g., 2N) + redundant generators with automatic transfer
options.C: Only a portable generator wheeled in after a failure
options.D: No UPS, relying solely on utility power

explanation: 2N or similar fully redundant topologies eliminate single points of failure in the power path.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A security camera system that retains footage for a defined retention period and is regularly reviewed is primarily serving which security function?

options.A: Prevention only
options.B: Detection and deterrence, plus forensic/investigative support after an incident
options.C: Encryption of data

explanation: CCTV is mainly detective and supportive of investigation; its visible presence also deters.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a data center, the practice of installing blanking panels in unused rack units primarily improves:

options.A: Network latency
options.B: Cooling efficiency by preventing hot-air recirculation
options.C: The speed of the CPUs
options.D: The strength of the biometric readers

explanation: Blanking panels force cold air through equipment intakes rather than allowing bypass.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct characterization of a ‘cold aisle containment’ system?

options.A: Hot exhaust is captured and returned; cold supply is left open
options.B: The cold supply aisle is enclosed so that cold air is forced through the equipment, improving efficiency
options.C: No physical barriers are used

explanation: Cold-aisle containment encloses the supply aisle to reduce mixing and improve cooling predictability.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A physical security assessment that includes testing whether an unauthorized person can follow an employee through a controlled door is evaluating resistance to:

options.A: SQL injection
options.B: Tailgating / piggybacking
options.C: Buffer overflow

explanation: This is a classic physical penetration-test scenario for anti-tailgating controls.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In the design of a secure server room, the HVAC system should ideally:

options.A: Be completely independent of the building’s general HVAC and have its own redundant capacity
options.B: Share the same air handlers as the office floors with no separation
options.C: Have no temperature monitoring
options.D: Blow unfiltered outside air directly onto the servers

explanation: Dedicated, redundant environmental systems protect the IT load from office-side failures and contamination.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following best describes the role of an access-control vestibule (mantrap) that also incorporates a weight sensor?

options.A: It only checks the card
options.B: It verifies that only one person is present in the vestibule, helping to defeat both tailgating and the use of stolen credentials by multiple people
options.C: It measures the temperature of the person
options.D: It replaces the need for any logging

explanation: Weight sensors can detect whether more than one person occupies the space.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A data-center fire-safety design that uses early-warning aspirating smoke detection together with a clean-agent suppression system is intended to:

options.A: Allow a fire to grow large before any action
options.B: Detect a fire at the earliest stage and extinguish it with an agent safe for electronics while personnel can still evacuate
options.C: Eliminate all detection in favor of suppression only
options.D: Use only water mist with no detection

explanation: Early detection + clean agent provides both life safety and equipment protection.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In physical security terminology, a ‘mantrap’ is also sometimes called a:

options.A: Firewall
options.B: Access-control vestibule or interlock
options.C: VPN concentrator

explanation: These terms all refer to the same sequential, interlocking entry control concept.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct reason for locating diesel generators outside the main data-hall structure?

options.A: To make them harder to refuel
options.B: To reduce noise, vibration, exhaust and fire risk inside the IT space while still providing reliable backup power
options.C: Because generators cannot run outdoors
options.D: To eliminate the need for any fuel storage

explanation: Generators produce exhaust, heat, noise and constitute a fire load best kept separate from the IT equipment.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A physical security control that records every successful and failed door access attempt with timestamp and identity is primarily providing:

options.A: Only prevention
options.B: Accountability and forensic capability (detective control)
options.C: Encryption of the data on the servers

explanation: Access logs support investigation and accountability after the fact.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a secure facility, the practice of requiring two authorized persons to be present to open a critical safe or to access a highly sensitive area is known as:

options.A: Single-person integrity
options.B: Dual control / two-person rule
options.C: Least privilege only

explanation: Dual control reduces the risk of a single individual acting maliciously or making an undetected error.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following environmental parameters is typically monitored continuously in a production data center?

options.A: Only the number of visitors
options.B: Temperature, humidity, water presence, smoke, and sometimes air quality / particulate levels
options.C: Only the color of the walls
options.D: Only the brand of the servers

explanation: These parameters directly affect equipment reliability and safety.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A data-center design that places the most critical equipment in the center of the room, surrounded by successive rings of physical controls, is applying:

options.A: A flat security model with no layers
options.B: Concentric layered defense (defense in depth)
options.C: Only cryptographic controls

explanation: Concentric layers force an attacker to defeat multiple independent controls.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the relationship between physical security and cybersecurity?

options.A: Physical security is irrelevant once a firewall is installed
options.B: Compromise of physical access can bypass many logical controls; therefore physical and cyber controls must be designed together
options.C: Physical security only matters for paper documents
options.D: Cybersecurity can fully replace physical locks

explanation: Physical access often grants the ability to subvert logical protections (console access, hardware keyloggers, etc.).

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: In a data center, the use of color-coded conduits or trays for power and data cabling primarily aids:

options.A: Aesthetic design only
options.B: Correct identification, maintenance and separation of power versus data paths, reducing accidental disconnection or interference
options.C: Increasing the temperature of the room

explanation: Clear visual differentiation reduces human error during maintenance.

topic: 1.3 Basic Knowledge of Physical Security of IT Infrastructure
question: A physical security policy that prohibits photography inside the data hall is intended to:

options.A: Improve cooling efficiency
