explanation: Dynamic scheduling lets the processor exploit instruction-level parallelism that static scheduling cannot always expose.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A classic five-stage RISC pipeline consists of the stages:

options.A: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Write-back
options.B: Only Fetch and Execute
options.C: Compile, Link, Load, Run, Exit

explanation: The canonical IF-ID-EX-MEM-WB pipeline is the teaching model for simple RISC pipelines.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a pipeline, a data hazard of type RAW (Read-After-Write) occurs when:

options.A: An instruction tries to read a register before a previous instruction has finished writing it
options.B: Two instructions write the same register in the wrong order
options.C: An instruction tries to write a register before a previous instruction has read it
options.D: There is a resource conflict on the ALU

explanation: RAW is the true dependence; the consumer must wait for the producer.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: Branch prediction is employed to mitigate:

options.A: Structural hazards only
options.B: Control hazards by guessing the direction (and often the target) of a branch so that the pipeline can continue fetching
options.C: Cache misses

explanation: Accurate prediction keeps the pipeline full; misprediction requires a flush and restart.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A VLIW (Very Long Instruction Word) architecture relies primarily on:

options.A: Dynamic hardware scheduling of independent operations
options.B: The compiler to identify and package independent operations into a single long instruction word that the hardware executes in parallel
options.C: Complex microcode for every instruction

explanation: VLIW shifts the burden of discovering ILP onto the compiler; the hardware simply executes the bundled operations.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: Pipeline stalls (bubbles) are inserted when:

options.A: Every instruction completes in a single cycle
options.B: A hazard cannot be resolved by forwarding and the dependent instruction must wait
options.C: The cache always hits

explanation: Stalls freeze younger instructions until the hazard condition disappears.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a CISC processor the use of microcode typically serves to:

options.A: Force every instruction to be a single simple RISC-like operation
options.B: Implement complex, variable-length instructions by sequencing simpler micro-operations inside the control unit
options.C: Eliminate the need for any control unit

explanation: Microcode provides a flexible way to realize rich instruction semantics without hard-wired combinational control for every variant.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: Register renaming is a technique used in out-of-order processors to:

options.A: Increase the number of architectural registers visible to the programmer
options.B: Eliminate false dependences (WAR and WAW) by mapping architectural registers onto a larger set of physical registers
options.C: Replace the need for a register file entirely
options.D: Perform floating-point division in a single cycle

explanation: Renaming removes anti- and output dependences that would otherwise unnecessarily serialize independent instructions.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A precise exception in a pipelined processor means that:

options.A: The exception is ignored
options.B: The architectural state at the time the exception is reported is identical to the state that would exist if the instructions had been executed sequentially up to the excepting instruction
options.C: All instructions in the pipeline are allowed to complete regardless of the exception

explanation: Precise exceptions simplify restart and exception handling by preserving a clean sequential model.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a load/store (RISC) architecture, arithmetic and logical instructions:

options.A: May take memory operands directly
options.B: Operate only on register operands; memory is accessed exclusively by explicit load and store instructions
options.C: Require microcode for every operation
options.D: Cannot be executed in a pipeline

explanation: The load/store restriction simplifies the pipeline datapath and is a defining RISC characteristic.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A branch-target buffer (BTB) is used to:

options.A: Store the results of arithmetic operations
options.B: Cache the target addresses of previously executed branches so that the fetch stage can begin fetching from the predicted target immediately
options.C: Replace the program counter

explanation: The BTB supplies both a prediction and the corresponding target address early in the pipeline.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The term ‘instruction-level parallelism’ (ILP) refers to:

options.A: The ability of a multiprocessor to run many threads
options.B: The existence of independent instructions within a single thread that can be executed concurrently by a superscalar or VLIW processor
options.C: The number of cores on a chip
options.D: The size of the instruction cache

explanation: ILP is the parallelism available among instructions of one sequential program.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a pipeline, a WAW (Write-After-Write) hazard can occur when:

options.A: Two instructions write the same register and the later write must not be overtaken by the earlier write in an out-of-order machine
options.B: An instruction reads a register before it is written
options.C: Two instructions need the same memory port

explanation: WAW is an output dependence; register renaming is the usual hardware solution.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: Scoreboarding is a classic hardware technique for:

options.A: Static compile-time scheduling only
options.B: Dynamic scheduling that tracks operand availability and functional-unit status to issue instructions out of order while preserving true dependences
options.C: Eliminating the need for any registers

explanation: The CDC 6600 scoreboard is the historical example of a centralized dynamic scheduler.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A major disadvantage of a very deep pipeline is:

options.A: Always higher IPC under all conditions
options.B: Increased penalty for branch mispredictions and other pipeline flushes, and greater difficulty in balancing stage delays
options.C: The complete elimination of data hazards

explanation: Deeper pipelines raise the misprediction cost and can make the clock-cycle budget harder to meet.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In the classic RISC pipeline, the Memory stage is used primarily for:

options.A: All arithmetic operations
options.B: Load and store instructions that access data memory; ALU instructions typically pass through this stage without a memory operation
options.C: Instruction fetch only

explanation: The MEM stage is the data-cache access point for loads and stores.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: Speculative execution beyond a predicted branch requires that:

options.A: All results be immediately written to the architectural register file
options.B: Results be held in a reorder buffer or similar structure until the branch is resolved, so that incorrect speculation can be discarded
options.C: The pipeline be frozen until the branch outcome is known

explanation: Speculative state must be buffered so that a misprediction can be rolled back cleanly.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A hazard detection unit in a simple pipeline is responsible for:

options.A: Performing all floating-point arithmetic
options.B: Comparing register fields of instructions in different stages to detect data dependences that require a stall or that can be satisfied by forwarding
options.C: Predicting the outcome of every branch

explanation: The hazard unit examines source and destination registers across pipeline stages to decide when to stall or forward.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a Tomasulo-style algorithm the reservation stations serve to:

options.A: Store only the program counter
options.B: Buffer instructions that are waiting for operands, hold the operands once they arrive, and issue the operation to a functional unit when ready
options.C: Replace the register file completely

explanation: Reservation stations implement distributed scheduling and eliminate WAR/WAW hazards via renaming.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The CPI (cycles per instruction) of a pipeline is degraded by:

options.A: Perfect hit rates in all caches and perfect branch prediction
options.B: Stalls caused by data hazards, control hazards, structural hazards and cache misses
options.C: The complete absence of any hazards
options.D: An infinitely large register file alone

explanation: Ideal CPI approaches 1 (or less for superscalar); real CPI is inflated by all sources of stalls and bubbles.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A delayed branch is a software technique in which:

options.A: The compiler places an independent instruction in the branch-delay slot that is always executed, whether or not the branch is taken
options.B: The hardware never fetches the instruction after a branch
options.C: Branches are illegal
options.D: The pipeline is flushed on every branch

explanation: The delay slot hides the control hazard without hardware prediction; the compiler is responsible for filling it usefully.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a modern out-of-order CPU the reorder buffer (ROB) is used to:

options.A: Store only data-cache lines
options.B: Maintain the original program order of instructions so that results can be committed in order, supporting precise exceptions and correct speculation recovery
options.C: Replace the need for a register file

explanation: The ROB provides in-order retirement while allowing out-of-order execution.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A dual-issue superscalar processor that can issue at most one memory operation and one ALU operation per cycle is limited by:

options.A: No structural constraints
options.B: A structural constraint that prevents two memory operations (or two ALU operations) from issuing in the same cycle
options.C: The complete inability to execute any instruction
options.D: The size of the TLB only

explanation: Issue-width limitations of this kind are common structural constraints in moderately superscalar designs.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The principal advantage of a Harvard architecture over a pure von Neumann architecture in an embedded or DSP pipeline is:

options.A: A single shared memory bus
options.B: The ability to fetch an instruction and access data memory simultaneously without structural contention on a unified memory port
options.C: The absence of any registers
options.D: The requirement that all data reside in the instruction memory

explanation: Separate instruction and data memories (or at least separate caches) remove a common structural hazard.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a pipeline that uses forwarding, a load-use hazard still typically requires a stall because:

options.A: Forwarding is never possible
options.B: The data loaded from memory is not available until the end of the MEM stage, so an immediately following dependent instruction in EX cannot yet receive the value
options.C: Loads never produce a result
options.D: The register file cannot be read

explanation: Even with forwarding from MEM/WB, a load’s result arrives one cycle too late for an immediately dependent ALU instruction.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A static multiple-issue processor differs from a dynamic superscalar processor mainly in that:

options.A: The hardware reorders instructions at run time
options.B: The compiler is responsible for grouping independent instructions into issue packets; the hardware executes the packet with little or no run-time reordering
options.C: No parallelism is exploited
options.D: Only one instruction is ever issued

explanation: Static issue (as in many VLIW and some EPIC designs) relies on the compiler for ILP packaging.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The term ‘pipeline bubble’ refers to:

options.A: A stage that is actively executing a useful instruction
options.B: A cycle in which a pipeline stage is forced to do no useful work because of a stall
options.C: A cache line that is being filled
options.D: A branch that is correctly predicted

explanation: Bubbles are the visible manifestation of stalls in the pipeline diagram.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a processor that supports simultaneous multithreading (SMT), the principal goal is to:

options.A: Increase the clock frequency without limit
options.B: Improve utilization of execution resources by allowing instructions from multiple threads to share the pipeline and functional units in the same cycle
options.C: Eliminate the need for caches
options.D: Make every thread run on a dedicated core

explanation: SMT fills otherwise idle issue slots and functional units with work from other threads.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A major reason that classic CISC instruction sets were attractive in the era of limited memory was:

options.A: They always executed in a single cycle
options.B: Dense, powerful instructions reduced the number of bits that had to be fetched from a slow and expensive memory hierarchy
options.C: They required no microcode

explanation: Code density mattered when memory capacity and bandwidth were severe constraints.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a pipeline with forwarding, the earliest stage from which an ALU result can typically be forwarded to a dependent instruction is:

options.A: The write-back stage only
options.B: The execute stage (after the ALU has produced the result)
options.C: The fetch stage

explanation: Forwarding from the EX/MEM pipeline register supplies the result to the next instruction’s EX stage.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A control hazard can be completely eliminated (in the absence of exceptions) by:

options.A: Never using any branch or jump instructions
options.B: Using a branch-delay slot that is always filled with a useful independent instruction, or by perfect branch prediction together with a mechanism to cancel incorrect speculation
options.C: Increasing the number of ALU units

explanation: Either the compiler guarantees a useful delay-slot instruction or the hardware predicts perfectly and recovers from any residual misprediction.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The principal performance advantage of a superscalar design over a scalar pipeline of the same depth is:

options.A: A higher clock frequency in all cases
options.B: The ability to achieve a CPI lower than 1 by executing multiple instructions per cycle when sufficient ILP is present
options.C: The complete elimination of all hazards

explanation: Issue width greater than one is what allows IPC (instructions per cycle) to exceed 1.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a processor that uses a reorder buffer, an instruction is allowed to update the architectural register file only when:

options.A: It has finished execution, regardless of older instructions
options.B: It reaches the head of the reorder buffer (i.e., all older instructions have already committed) and it is ready to retire
options.C: A cache miss occurs

explanation: In-order retirement from the ROB guarantees precise state and correct handling of exceptions and mispredictions.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A structural hazard that arises because a single memory port is used for both instruction fetch and data access is most directly solved by:

options.A: Ignoring the hazard
options.B: Using separate instruction and data caches (or a dual-ported memory), i.e., a Harvard-style split
options.C: Eliminating all load and store instructions

explanation: Split caches remove the structural contention between IF and MEM stages.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The concept of ‘issue width’ in a superscalar processor refers to:

options.A: The number of bits in the data bus
options.B: The maximum number of instructions that the issue logic can dispatch to execution units in a single cycle
options.C: The size of the instruction cache line

explanation: Issue width is a key determinant of the peak IPC the machine can achieve.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a pipeline, the term ‘flush’ most commonly means:

options.A: Writing all registers to memory
options.B: Discarding the instructions that were fetched after a mispredicted branch (or after an exception) so that the pipeline can restart from the correct address
options.C: Increasing the clock frequency

explanation: A pipeline flush is the recovery action taken after incorrect speculation or an exception.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A key advantage of dynamic scheduling over static (compiler) scheduling is that:

options.A: The compiler never needs to know about dependences
options.B: The hardware can adapt to dependences and latencies that are not known at compile time (for example cache misses or variable-latency operations)
options.C: No hardware is required

explanation: Run-time information lets the processor keep functional units busy even when the compiler’s static schedule would stall.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In the classic five-stage pipeline, forwarding from the MEM/WB stage to the EX stage is needed when:

options.A: An ALU instruction is followed immediately by another ALU instruction that uses its result (the EX/MEM → EX path is also used)
options.B: A load is followed two instructions later by a dependent ALU instruction
options.C: No forwarding is ever required

explanation: The MEM/WB → EX path covers the case where the producer is a load (or an ALU result that has already moved past EX/MEM).

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A processor that can execute instructions from more than one thread in the same cycle is said to support:

options.A: Only coarse-grained multithreading
options.B: Simultaneous multithreading (SMT) or fine-grained multithreading that interleaves threads at the issue level
options.C: No form of multithreading

explanation: SMT issues instructions from multiple threads concurrently; fine-grained MT switches every cycle.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The main reason that a pure interlocked pipeline (no forwarding) has lower performance than a pipeline with forwarding is that:

options.A: Forwarding increases the clock period dramatically in all designs
options.B: Many data hazards that could be resolved by a simple bypass path instead cause multi-cycle stalls
options.C: Interlocks eliminate all control hazards

explanation: Without forwarding, even a simple RAW dependence between consecutive ALU instructions forces a stall.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In a VLIW processor a ‘no-op’ (or explicit stop bit) is often required because:

options.A: The hardware dynamically reorders operations
options.B: The compiler must indicate the end of an independent operation group or fill unused slots when insufficient parallelism is available
options.C: The register file is too small

explanation: VLIW packets have a fixed format; unused issue slots are filled with no-ops or marked by stop bits.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A pipeline that supports precise exceptions must ensure that:

options.A: All instructions after the excepting instruction have already updated architectural state
options.B: When an exception is recognized, all instructions older than the excepting instruction have committed and no younger instruction has modified architectural state
options.C: Exceptions are never reported

explanation: Precise state is required for correct restart and for the OS to see a consistent sequential machine.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: The term ‘issue queue’ (or reservation-station pool) in an out-of-order processor holds:

options.A: Only completed instructions waiting to retire
options.B: Decoded instructions that are waiting for their source operands to become available and for a free functional unit
options.C: Only branch instructions
options.D: The entire contents of main memory

explanation: The issue queue is the central structure from which ready instructions are dispatched to execution units.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: A major challenge in designing a high-frequency, deeply pipelined processor is:

options.A: The complete absence of any timing constraints
options.B: Balancing the amount of work in each pipeline stage so that the clock period is determined by the slowest stage, while still keeping the misprediction and forwarding penalties acceptable
options.C: Eliminating the need for any cache
options.D: Making every instruction take a single cycle with no hazards

explanation: Stage balancing, hazard resolution latency and clock-period targets are tightly coupled design constraints.

topic: 2.3 CPU Architecture
question: In the presence of a perfect branch predictor and perfect caches, the remaining performance limiters for a superscalar processor are primarily:

options.A: Only the number of pins on the package
options.B: True data dependences (RAW), limited issue width, limited functional-unit resources, and the amount of instruction-level parallelism actually present in the program
options.C: The complete lack of any parallelism in any program
options.D: The size of the hard disk

explanation: Even with ideal prediction and memory, ILP is bounded by true dependences and by the machine’s issue and execution resources.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Direct Memory Access (DMA) is characterized by the ability of a device controller to:

options.A: Transfer data only one byte at a time under continuous CPU polling
options.B: Move blocks of data between a device and main memory with minimal CPU intervention after the transfer is initiated
options.C: Execute arbitrary user-level programs
options.D: Replace the need for any interrupt mechanism

explanation: DMA allows the controller to become bus master and perform bulk transfers, freeing the CPU from per-byte involvement.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Programmed I/O (polling) forces the CPU to:

options.A: Remain idle until an interrupt arrives
options.B: Continuously test a device status register in a tight loop until the device is ready
options.C: Hand over the entire transfer to a DMA controller

explanation: Polling is busy-wait; the CPU wastes cycles repeatedly checking readiness flags.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Interrupt-driven I/O differs from programmed I/O mainly in that:

options.A: The CPU never learns that a device needs attention
options.B: The device signals the CPU via an interrupt when it is ready, allowing the CPU to perform other work in the meantime
options.C: All data movement is performed solely by the DMA controller with no CPU involvement at any stage

explanation: Interrupts free the CPU from continuous polling; the device notifies the processor only when service is required.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Memory-mapped I/O means that:

options.A: Device registers occupy a separate address space accessed only by special IN/OUT instructions
options.B: Device control and data registers are mapped into the same address space as main memory and are accessed with ordinary load/store instructions
options.C: Devices can never be accessed by the CPU
options.D: All I/O must be performed by DMA exclusively

explanation: In memory-mapped I/O the CPU treats device registers as ordinary memory locations.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Port-mapped (isolated) I/O is characterized by:

options.A: Using the same address space and ordinary load/store instructions for both memory and devices
options.B: A distinct I/O address space and special processor instructions (e.g., IN/OUT) dedicated to device communication
options.C: The complete absence of any device registers
options.D: Mandatory use of DMA for every transfer

explanation: Isolated I/O keeps device addresses separate from memory addresses and requires dedicated I/O instructions.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A device driver is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Compiling source code into machine code
options.B: Providing a device-specific software interface that translates generic OS I/O requests into the low-level commands understood by a particular hardware device
options.C: Managing the file-system journal exclusively

explanation: Drivers encapsulate hardware details so that the rest of the kernel can issue uniform I/O requests.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the context of I/O, a blocking system call means that:

options.A: The calling process continues to run while the I/O proceeds asynchronously
options.B: The calling process is put to sleep (or otherwise suspended) until the requested I/O operation completes
options.C: The device is permanently disabled
options.D: Only DMA is used and the process never waits

explanation: Blocking I/O suspends the process until the data are available or the transfer finishes.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: An interrupt service routine (ISR) is executed when:

options.A: The CPU decides to poll a device on its own schedule
options.B: A hardware or software event asserts an interrupt request and the processor vectors to the corresponding handler
options.C: A user process terminates normally without any external event
options.D: The scheduler runs a new process in the absence of any interrupt

explanation: Interrupts are asynchronous signals that cause a controlled transfer to an ISR.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Cycle stealing in a DMA transfer refers to:

options.A: The DMA controller permanently locking the CPU out of the bus
options.B: The DMA controller temporarily becoming bus master for one or a few bus cycles, transferring a word, then releasing the bus so the CPU can continue
options.C: The complete suspension of all CPU activity for the entire duration of a large block transfer
options.D: A method of increasing the CPU clock frequency

explanation: Cycle stealing interleaves DMA bus usage with CPU bus usage, minimizing disruption to the processor.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a vectored interrupt system the interrupting device:

options.A: Always forces the CPU to jump to a single fixed address
options.B: Supplies an identifier (vector) that the CPU uses to locate the appropriate interrupt handler
options.C: Never identifies itself
options.D: Requires the CPU to poll every device after every interrupt

explanation: Vectored interrupts allow direct dispatch to the correct ISR without exhaustive polling.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A major advantage of DMA over interrupt-driven byte-by-byte transfers for large blocks is:

options.A: Higher CPU utilization for the transfer itself
options.B: Far lower CPU overhead because the processor is involved only at the start and end of the block transfer
options.C: The complete elimination of any need for device drivers
options.D: Guaranteed real-time response for every single byte

explanation: DMA amortizes setup cost over an entire block, freeing the CPU for useful work during the transfer.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the I/O software stack, the layer that is most closely tied to the peculiarities of a specific hardware device is:

options.A: The user-level library
options.B: The device-independent I/O software of the kernel
options.C: The device driver

explanation: Drivers contain the device-specific knowledge; higher layers present a uniform interface.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A non-blocking (asynchronous) I/O operation allows the calling process to:

options.A: Be suspended until the operation finishes
options.B: Continue execution immediately after initiating the request, later learning of completion via a callback, signal or explicit wait
options.C: Ignore the device forever
options.D: Force the device to complete in zero time

explanation: Asynchronous I/O returns control at once; completion is notified separately.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Bus mastering is a capability that allows a device to:

options.A: Only respond to CPU-initiated transactions
options.B: Initiate its own bus transactions, becoming temporary owner of the system bus (as required for DMA)
options.C: Disable the CPU permanently
options.D: Execute user programs in place of the CPU

explanation: Bus-master devices can drive address and control lines themselves, enabling DMA.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a system that uses memory-mapped I/O, protection of device registers from user-mode programs is typically achieved by:

options.A: Making the registers completely inaccessible even to the kernel
options.B: Mapping the device registers only into kernel address space (or using page-protection bits so that user mode cannot access them)
options.C: Relying solely on the fact that users do not know the addresses

explanation: The MMU and page tables enforce that user processes cannot touch privileged device registers.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A daisy-chain interrupt priority scheme works by:

options.A: Giving every device the identical priority
options.B: Propagating the interrupt-acknowledge signal along a chain so that the electrically closest requesting device is serviced first
options.C: Requiring the CPU to poll every device on every interrupt
options.D: Eliminating the need for any interrupt controller

explanation: Daisy-chaining encodes priority in the physical wiring order of the acknowledge line.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The primary purpose of a device controller (or adapter) is to:

options.A: Replace the operating system
options.B: Convert between the software-visible interface expected by the driver and the electrical signalling and protocol required by the physical device
options.C: Store the entire contents of main memory

explanation: Controllers abstract the raw hardware, presenting registers and status bits that drivers understand.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the presence of a DMA controller, the CPU is typically interrupted:

options.A: After every single byte transferred
options.B: Only at the beginning and/or the end of a block transfer (or on error), not for each word
options.C: Never, because DMA eliminates all interrupts
options.D: Only when the user presses a key

explanation: DMA completion (or error) generates a single interrupt after the whole block has been moved.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A character-oriented device differs from a block-oriented device mainly in that:

options.A: It always transfers data in fixed-size blocks of 512 bytes or more
options.B: It delivers or accepts a stream of individual bytes (or small records) without an underlying block structure visible to the driver
options.C: It cannot generate interrupts
options.D: It never requires a device driver

explanation: Keyboards, mice and serial ports are classic character devices; disks are block devices.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Buffering of I/O data in kernel memory is performed primarily to:

options.A: Increase the number of page faults
options.B: Decouple the speed and timing of the device from the speed and timing of the user process, and to allow data to be staged safely across protection domains
options.C: Eliminate the need for any DMA
options.D: Force every transfer to be synchronous

explanation: Kernel buffers absorb speed mismatches and provide a safe intermediate storage area.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a system that supports both programmed I/O and DMA, a typical criterion for choosing DMA is:

options.A: The transfer size is a single byte
options.B: The transfer size is large enough that the setup cost of DMA is amortized and the CPU savings become significant
options.C: The device is a keyboard

explanation: DMA has non-trivial setup overhead; it becomes advantageous for bulk transfers.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: An interrupt vector table (or interrupt descriptor table) contains:

options.A: Only the current program counter of the running process
options.B: Addresses (or descriptors) of the interrupt service routines, indexed by interrupt type or vector number
options.C: The entire contents of main memory

explanation: The vector table maps each interrupt source to its handler entry point.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Spooling is a technique that:

options.A: Forces every process to wait until a slow device finishes before it can continue
options.B: Temporarily stores data destined for a slow device (e.g., a printer) on a faster medium so that the producing process can proceed without waiting for the device
options.C: Eliminates the need for any device drivers
options.D: Is used only for network packet routing

explanation: Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line) decouples producers from slow consumers via intermediate storage.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a memory-mapped I/O system a read from a device status register is performed by:

options.A: A special IN instruction that cannot be used for memory
options.B: An ordinary load instruction whose address falls within the region assigned to that device
options.C: A DMA request only
options.D: A system call that is never translated into a memory access

explanation: Memory-mapped registers are accessed with the same load/store instructions used for RAM.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A major disadvantage of pure programmed I/O for high-speed devices is:

options.A: It always uses DMA automatically
options.B: The CPU can spend a large fraction of its time spinning in a status-check loop, unable to perform useful computation
options.C: It requires no software at all
options.D: It eliminates all interrupts by design

explanation: Busy-waiting wastes CPU cycles that could be used by other processes or by the same process for useful work.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the I/O request life-cycle, the step that occurs after a user process issues a read system call and before the device is actually programmed is typically:

options.A: The process is immediately resumed with the data
options.B: The kernel validates the request, locates the appropriate driver, and may place the request on a queue if the device is busy
options.C: The CPU is halted permanently

explanation: Kernel I/O handling includes validation, queuing and driver invocation before hardware is touched.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A polled interrupt (or software interrupt) differs from a hardware interrupt in that it is:

options.A: Generated by an external device asserting a pin
options.B: Caused by the execution of a special instruction (or a trap condition) inside the CPU itself
options.C: Never serviced by an ISR
options.D: Always of higher priority than any hardware interrupt

explanation: Software interrupts / traps are synchronous with instruction execution; hardware interrupts are asynchronous external events.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: Double buffering is a technique that:

options.A: Uses only a single buffer that is shared by CPU and device without synchronization
options.B: Employs two buffers so that the CPU can process one buffer while the device fills or empties the other, improving throughput and reducing waiting
options.C: Eliminates the need for any synchronization
options.D: Is used only for network routing tables

explanation: Two buffers allow concurrent operation of producer and consumer sides of the transfer.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a system with a single shared interrupt request line, identification of the interrupting device is typically performed by:

options.A: Ignoring the interrupt
options.B: Polling the status registers of candidate devices (or using a daisy-chain / vectored scheme layered on top of the shared line)
options.C: Assuming only one device exists

explanation: When multiple devices share a line, the ISR (or interrupt controller) must determine which device asserted the request.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A scatter-gather DMA operation is useful when:

options.A: The data to be transferred occupy a single contiguous physical region
options.B: The data occupy multiple non-contiguous physical buffers; the DMA engine is given a list of address/length pairs and transfers them without CPU intervention between segments
options.C: Only one byte needs to be moved

explanation: Scatter-gather lists allow a single DMA transaction to handle fragmented buffers, common with virtual-memory systems.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The term ‘I/O-bound process’ refers to a process that:

options.A: Spends most of its time performing CPU-intensive calculations
options.B: Spends a large fraction of its time waiting for I/O operations to complete
options.C: Never performs any I/O

explanation: I/O-bound processes are limited by device speed rather than by processor speed.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a modern operating system the uniform I/O interface presented to user programs is typically realized through:

options.A: Direct manipulation of device registers from user mode
options.B: System calls such as open, read, write, ioctl and close that are independent of the underlying device type
options.C: A requirement that every program contain its own device driver
options.D: The complete absence of any abstraction

explanation: The system-call interface hides device diversity behind a small set of generic operations.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A level-triggered interrupt remains asserted until:

options.A: The CPU acknowledges it by reading a status register or otherwise clearing the condition
options.B: A fixed number of clock cycles elapse, after which it disappears automatically
options.C: The power supply is removed

explanation: Level-triggered interrupts stay active as long as the requesting condition is true, requiring explicit clearance.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: An edge-triggered interrupt is recognized when:

options.A: The interrupt line remains continuously high
options.B: A transition (rising or falling edge) occurs on the interrupt line; the condition need not remain asserted
options.C: The CPU is in user mode only

explanation: Edge triggering latches the event at the moment of transition, which is useful for transient conditions.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the design of a device driver, the ‘top half’ versus ‘bottom half’ (or deferred work) distinction is used to:

options.A: Make every interrupt handler run for an unbounded time
options.B: Keep the interrupt-context work as short as possible and defer longer processing to a less critical context
options.C: Eliminate all synchronization
options.D: Force all work to be performed by user processes

explanation: Short top-half handlers preserve system responsiveness; bottom halves run later with interrupts re-enabled.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A cycle-stealing DMA controller that transfers one word at a time will typically:

options.A: Hold the bus for the entire duration of a multi-kilobyte block
options.B: Acquire the bus, move a single word, release the bus, and repeat until the whole block is transferred, interleaving with CPU memory accesses
options.C: Never release the bus once it has acquired it
options.D: Require the CPU to move every word itself

explanation: Cycle stealing interleaves DMA and CPU bus usage at a fine granularity.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a system that uses I/O ports, the instruction that reads a byte from an I/O port address is typically called:

options.A: LOAD or MOV (ordinary memory read)
options.B: IN (or an equivalent special I/O read instruction)
options.C: JMP

explanation: Isolated I/O uses dedicated instructions such as IN and OUT on many architectures.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The principal reason that modern high-performance I/O devices prefer DMA (or similar bus-master transfers) is:

options.A: DMA always increases the number of interrupts
options.B: The CPU cannot keep up with the data rates of contemporary disks, network interfaces and GPUs if it must handle every word itself
options.C: DMA eliminates the need for any device driver

explanation: Modern device bandwidths far exceed what a CPU can sustain with programmed I/O.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A device-independent I/O software layer in the kernel is responsible for:

options.A: Programming the exact bit patterns required by a particular disk controller
options.B: Providing uniform naming, protection, blocking/non-blocking semantics, buffering and allocation of devices, independent of the underlying hardware
options.C: Replacing the file system entirely

explanation: Device-independent code supplies the common services that all drivers and user requests share.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the presence of a DMA controller that can address the full physical memory, a potential protection problem is that:

options.A: DMA cannot transfer any data
options.B: A malicious or buggy device could overwrite arbitrary kernel or user memory unless an IOMMU (or similar protection mechanism) restricts the addresses the device may touch
options.C: The CPU is always faster than DMA

explanation: An IOMMU provides the analogue of virtual-memory protection for device-initiated transfers.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A synchronous I/O operation is one in which:

options.A: The calling thread continues immediately and learns of completion later
options.B: The calling thread does not proceed past the call until the I/O has completed (or failed)
options.C: No data are ever transferred
options.D: Only DMA is used and the thread never waits

explanation: Synchronous (blocking) I/O waits for completion before returning to the caller.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The interrupt priority level (or IRQ priority) mechanism is used to:

options.A: Make every interrupt equal in urgency
options.B: Allow a higher-priority interrupt to preempt the handler of a lower-priority interrupt, while preventing lower-priority interrupts from interfering with critical higher-priority handlers
options.C: Disable all interrupts permanently
options.D: Replace the need for any device drivers

explanation: Priority schemes ensure that time-critical devices are serviced ahead of less urgent ones.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a Unix-like system the ‘major’ and ‘minor’ device numbers are used to:

options.A: Identify the CPU model
options.B: Select the device driver (major) and the specific unit or partition handled by that driver (minor)
options.C: Store file sizes

explanation: Major number indexes the driver; minor number distinguishes instances or subdivisions of the device.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A burst-mode DMA transfer differs from cycle-stealing DMA in that:

options.A: The DMA controller never uses the bus
options.B: The DMA controller seizes the bus for the entire duration of a multi-word block, transferring data continuously until the block is finished, then releases the bus
options.C: Only one word is ever transferred
options.D: The CPU must move every word

explanation: Burst mode maximizes bus efficiency for large contiguous transfers at the cost of longer periods of CPU bus starvation.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The principal function of an interrupt controller (e.g., PIC or APIC) is to:

options.A: Execute user programs
options.B: Accept interrupt requests from multiple devices, prioritize them, and present a single interrupt signal together with a vector to the CPU
options.C: Replace the need for any device drivers

explanation: Interrupt controllers multiplex many device IRQs onto the limited interrupt pins of the processor and supply vector information.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In the I/O software hierarchy, the layer that is responsible for naming devices, protection, and providing a uniform block or character interface is best described as:

options.A: The user process itself
options.B: Device-independent OS software
options.C: The raw hardware

explanation: Device-independent code sits above the drivers and below the system-call interface, supplying common services.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A potential problem with allowing user processes to perform programmed I/O directly on device registers is:

options.A: It always improves performance with no drawbacks
options.B: A buggy or malicious process could corrupt device state, monopolize the device, or interfere with other processes that share the device
options.C: Devices become faster

explanation: Direct user-mode access to devices violates protection and resource-sharing principles; hence I/O is mediated by the kernel.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: In a system that uses both interrupts and DMA, the typical sequence for a large disk read is:

options.A: CPU polls the disk for every sector until the whole request is satisfied
options.B: Driver programs the DMA controller and the disk, sleeps; DMA moves the data; an interrupt signals completion; the driver awakens the waiting process
options.C: The user process itself programs the DMA engine from user mode

explanation: Modern bulk I/O combines DMA for the data path with a single completion interrupt.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: The term ‘memory-mapped file’ refers to a technique in which:

options.A: A file is copied entirely into a kernel buffer before any user access
options.B: Portions of a file are mapped directly into a process’s virtual address space so that ordinary loads and stores access file data, with the OS handling page faults by reading from the file
options.C: The file is stored only in CPU registers
options.D: DMA is disabled for that file

explanation: Memory-mapped I/O of files unifies the file and memory abstractions and can improve performance via demand paging.

topic: 2.4 I/O Management, I/O Interface, I/O Requests Handling, I/O Devices
question: A fundamental reason that I/O software is organized in layers (user libraries, device-independent kernel code, device drivers, interrupt handlers) is to:

options.A: Increase the number of lines of code without benefit
options.B: Separate concerns so that device-specific details are confined to drivers while higher layers present stable, uniform abstractions to applications and to the rest of the kernel
options.C: Force every application to know the register layout of every device
options.D: Eliminate the need for any hardware controllers

explanation: Layering achieves modularity, portability and maintainability in the face of diverse and evolving hardware.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A Layer-2 switch creates separate collision domains for each of its ports while still forming a single broadcast domain (unless VLANs are configured). This statement is:

options.A: False – switches never segment collision domains
options.B: True
options.C: True only for hubs

explanation: Each switch port is its own collision domain; the default VLAN remains one broadcast domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router is required when traffic must be forwarded between:

options.A: Two devices on the same LAN that share the same IP subnet
options.B: Different IP networks or subnets that constitute distinct Layer-3 broadcast domains
options.C: Two ports of the same Layer-2 switch with no VLAN separation
options.D: Devices that need only signal regeneration

explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 and interconnect separate IP networks.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A pure repeater operates at which OSI layer and performs what primary function?

options.A: Layer 3 – routes IP packets
options.B: Layer 2 – filters frames by MAC address
options.C: Layer 1 – regenerates or amplifies the electrical or optical signal without interpreting frames

explanation: Repeaters are Physical-layer devices that extend the reach of a segment by restoring signal quality.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A hub is best described as:

options.A: A multiport Layer-2 switch that learns MAC addresses
options.B: A multiport Layer-1 repeater that floods every incoming frame out all other ports, creating a single shared collision domain
options.C: A Layer-3 device that routes between subnets

explanation: Hubs are shared-media devices; every port belongs to the same collision domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A multilayer (Layer-3) switch can make forwarding decisions based on:

options.A: Only MAC addresses
options.B: Both MAC addresses (Layer 2) and IP addresses (Layer 3)
options.C: Only TCP port numbers

explanation: Multilayer switches combine traditional switching with routing capabilities.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When a pure Layer-2 switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not yet in its MAC address table, it:

options.A: Drops the frame silently
options.B: Floods the frame out all ports except the one on which it arrived
options.C: Sends an ARP request for the MAC address
options.D: Forwards the frame only to the router

explanation: Unknown unicast frames are flooded; the switch learns the source MAC from the incoming frame.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A gateway in the classic networking sense is a device that:

options.A: Operates only at Layer 1
options.B: Connects networks that use dissimilar protocol stacks, often performing translation at higher layers (up to Layer 7)
options.C: Is identical to a simple repeater

explanation: Gateways can interconnect heterogeneous architectures by translating protocols at multiple layers.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which statement correctly ranks the devices by the OSI layer at which they make forwarding decisions (from lowest to highest)?

options.A: Router → Switch → Hub → Repeater
options.B: Repeater / Hub → Switch → Router
options.C: Switch → Router → Hub

explanation: Repeaters/hubs = Layer 1, switches = Layer 2, routers = Layer 3.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A cut-through switch begins forwarding a frame:

options.A: Only after the entire frame has been received and the FCS verified
options.B: As soon as the destination MAC address has been read, before the rest of the frame arrives
options.C: Only after consulting a routing table
options.D: Never; it always stores the frame first

explanation: Cut-through switching reduces latency by starting transmission before the frame is complete (at the cost of possibly forwarding errored frames).

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Store-and-forward switching is characterized by:

options.A: Forwarding the frame as soon as the destination MAC is known
options.B: Receiving the entire frame, checking the FCS, and only then forwarding it if it is error-free
options.C: Ignoring the FCS completely

explanation: Store-and-forward prioritizes error detection over minimum latency.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router maintains a routing table that is consulted to determine:

options.A: The MAC address of every host on the local LAN only
options.B: The next-hop interface (and next-hop address) for packets destined to remote networks
options.C: The physical signal strength on each port
options.D: The TCP port numbers of all connections

explanation: Routing tables map destination network prefixes to outgoing interfaces and next hops.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When two hosts on different VLANs attached to the same Layer-2 switch need to communicate, the traffic must normally:

options.A: Be switched directly by the Layer-2 switch using only MAC addresses
options.B: Pass through a Layer-3 device (router or multilayer switch) that performs inter-VLAN routing
options.C: Be flooded to every port regardless of VLAN membership

explanation: VLANs are separate broadcast domains; Layer-3 forwarding is required to move traffic between them.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A bridge is historically most similar in function to a modern:

options.A: Router
options.B: Layer-2 switch (especially an early two-port switch)
options.C: Repeater

explanation: Classic transparent bridges performed MAC learning and selective forwarding—the core of Layer-2 switching.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A hub creates how many collision domains for an 8-port hub?

options.A: 8 separate collision domains
options.B: 1 single collision domain shared by all ports
options.C: 4 collision domains

explanation: All ports of a hub share one collision domain because the device simply repeats bits to every port.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: An 8-port Layer-2 switch (with no VLANs) creates how many collision domains and how many broadcast domains?

options.A: 1 collision domain, 8 broadcast domains
options.B: 8 collision domains, 1 broadcast domain
options.C: 8 collision domains, 8 broadcast domains

explanation: Each port is a collision domain; the default VLAN is still one broadcast domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router creates separate broadcast domains for each of its interfaces (or sub-interfaces). This statement is:

options.A: False
options.B: True
options.C: True only for Layer-2 switches

explanation: Routers do not forward broadcasts between interfaces; each interface is its own broadcast domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which device can reduce the size of a broadcast domain?

options.A: Hub
options.B: Repeater
options.C: Router (or a multilayer switch performing inter-VLAN routing)

explanation: Only Layer-3 devices stop broadcasts from propagating between networks.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: In a switched Ethernet network the MAC address table (CAM table) of a switch is populated by:

options.A: Static configuration only
options.B: Observing the source MAC address of frames arriving on each port (transparent learning)
options.C: ARP replies exclusively

explanation: Switches learn by inspecting source addresses of incoming frames and associating them with the ingress port.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A frame whose destination MAC is a broadcast address (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) will be:

options.A: Dropped by every switch
options.B: Flooded out all ports of a Layer-2 switch (within the VLAN) except the incoming port
options.C: Forwarded only to the router

explanation: Broadcasts are flooded within the broadcast domain (VLAN).

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which of the following devices does not examine MAC addresses when forwarding traffic?

options.A: Layer-2 switch
options.B: Bridge
options.C: Hub / repeater
options.D: Multilayer switch operating in Layer-2 mode

explanation: Hubs and pure repeaters are Layer-1 devices and simply regenerate bits without frame inspection.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router that receives a packet whose destination network is not present in its routing table will typically:

options.A: Flood the packet out all interfaces
options.B: Drop the packet and may send an ICMP Destination Unreachable message back to the source
options.C: Convert the packet into a Layer-2 broadcast

explanation: Without a matching route (or default route) the packet cannot be forwarded.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: The primary purpose of a default gateway configured on a host is to:

options.A: Serve as the DNS server
options.B: Provide the next-hop address for packets whose destination lies outside the host’s local subnet
options.C: Act as a Layer-1 repeater
options.D: Replace the need for any switch

explanation: The default gateway is the router interface that leads out of the local network.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A switch that supports VLANs can create multiple broadcast domains on the same physical device by:

options.A: Ignoring MAC addresses
options.B: Assigning ports (or frames via tags) to different VLAN identifiers so that frames are only flooded within the same VLAN
options.C: Operating exclusively at Layer 1

explanation: VLAN membership partitions the switch into independent broadcast domains.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which device is most appropriate for interconnecting two geographically distant Ethernet LANs while preserving a single IP subnet (i.e., extending a Layer-2 domain)?

options.A: A router performing inter-subnet routing
options.B: A pair of bridges or Layer-2 switches connected by a suitable long-distance link (or a modern L2VPN / dark-fiber extension)
options.C: A pure Layer-1 hub spanning the distance without regeneration
options.D: A device that only performs NAT

explanation: Extending a single broadcast domain requires Layer-2 transparency, not routing.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A collision domain is defined as the set of network segments in which:

options.A: Broadcasts are confined
options.B: Only one device may transmit at a time without risk of collision; simultaneous transmissions from multiple devices will produce a collision
options.C: IP addresses must be unique

explanation: Collision domains are a Layer-1/Layer-2 shared-medium concept; switches micro-segment them.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A broadcast domain is the set of devices that:

options.A: Share the same collision domain
options.B: Will receive a Layer-2 broadcast frame transmitted by any member of the set
options.C: Must all have the same MAC address

explanation: Broadcasts are flooded to every port within the same VLAN / broadcast domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When a switch port is configured as an access port belonging to VLAN 10, frames arriving on that port from the attached host are:

options.A: Always tagged with VLAN 10 before entering the switch fabric
options.B: Treated as belonging to VLAN 10; the switch adds the VLAN tag internally if needed for trunk transport
options.C: Ignored unless they already carry a VLAN tag

explanation: Access ports accept untagged frames and associate them with the configured VLAN.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A trunk port on a switch is used to:

options.A: Connect a single end host that belongs to one VLAN
options.B: Carry frames of multiple VLANs between switches (or between a switch and a router), normally using 802.1Q tags to identify the VLAN of each frame
options.C: Disable all VLANs

explanation: Trunks multiplex many VLANs onto a single physical link.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the relationship between a collision domain and a broadcast domain on a modern switched network?

options.A: They are always identical
options.B: Each switch port is typically its own collision domain, while a VLAN (or the entire switch if no VLANs) constitutes a broadcast domain
options.C: Routers create collision domains but not broadcast domains

explanation: Switching micro-segments collision domains; VLANs (or lack thereof) define broadcast domains.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A pure Layer-3 router does not forward frames based on MAC addresses; instead it:

options.A: Ignores the IP header completely
options.B: Examines the IP destination address, consults its routing table, and rewrites the Layer-2 header for the next hop
options.C: Floods every packet out all interfaces

explanation: Routing is a Layer-3 decision followed by a new Layer-2 encapsulation for the outgoing interface.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: In a network that still contains hubs, placing a switch between two hubs has the effect of:

options.A: Merging the two hubs into one larger collision domain
options.B: Separating the two hubs into distinct collision domains while still allowing them to exchange frames
options.C: Eliminating all broadcast traffic

explanation: The switch port connected to each hub becomes the boundary of that hub’s collision domain.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A switch that implements 802.1Q tagging adds a VLAN identifier to frames so that:

options.A: The frames become Layer-3 packets
options.B: Receiving switches (or routers) can determine which VLAN the frame belongs to when it arrives on a trunk
options.C: MAC addresses are no longer needed
options.D: Collisions are completely eliminated on shared media

explanation: The 802.1Q tag carries the VLAN ID across trunk links.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which device can enforce different security or QoS policies on a per-subnet basis most naturally?

options.A: A pure Layer-1 hub
options.B: A Layer-2 switch with no Layer-3 capability
options.C: A router (or multilayer switch) that sees IP headers and can apply access lists or policy maps per interface/subnet

explanation: Layer-3 devices have visibility into IP addresses and can implement policy at network boundaries.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A transparent bridge (and by extension a modern Layer-2 switch) is called ‘transparent’ because:

options.A: It is invisible to the end hosts; hosts do not need to be reconfigured when a bridge is inserted into the network
options.B: It has no MAC address table
options.C: It operates only at Layer 3

explanation: End stations continue to use the same MAC addresses and framing; the bridge learns and filters silently.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When a Layer-2 switch receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC is present in its MAC address table, it:

options.A: Floods the frame out every port
options.B: Forwards the frame only out the port associated with that MAC address
options.C: Drops the frame
options.D: Sends it to the default gateway only

explanation: Known unicast frames are forwarded selectively, which is the main efficiency gain of switching over hubs.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router interface that is configured with an IP address and is in the ‘up/up’ state forms the boundary of:

options.A: Only a collision domain
options.B: Both a collision domain (if the media is shared) and a broadcast domain
options.C: Neither a collision nor a broadcast domain

explanation: Each router interface is a separate broadcast domain and, on multi-access media, also defines collision-domain boundaries.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: In a network design, the device that is normally placed at the boundary between a LAN and a WAN (or between two administrative IP domains) is a:

options.A: Hub
options.B: Pure Layer-2 switch with no routing capability
options.C: Router

explanation: Routers interconnect different Layer-3 networks and are the classic edge device for WANs.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A switch that runs the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) does so primarily to:

options.A: Increase the number of active loops in the topology
options.B: Detect and block redundant paths so that a loop-free logical topology is maintained while still providing physical redundancy
options.C: Eliminate the need for MAC address learning
options.D: Convert the switch into a router

explanation: STP prevents broadcast storms and forwarding loops by selectively blocking ports.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which of the following statements about a hub is correct?

options.A: It examines MAC addresses and forwards selectively
options.B: It creates a single shared collision domain and a single broadcast domain for all connected devices
options.C: It routes IP packets between subnets

explanation: Hubs are shared-medium devices at Layer 1; every transmission is seen by every station.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A multilayer switch that performs inter-VLAN routing is sometimes called a:

options.A: Layer-1 repeater
options.B: Layer-3 switch or routing switch
options.C: Pure hub

explanation: The combination of hardware switching and Layer-3 forwarding earns the name ‘Layer-3 switch’.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When a frame arrives on a switch port and the source MAC is already present in the MAC address table but associated with a different port, the switch typically:

options.A: Ignores the discrepancy
options.B: Updates the table entry to reflect the new port (MAC move), which can occur when a host is relocated or in certain attack scenarios
options.C: Permanently locks the original entry
options.D: Deletes the entire MAC address table

explanation: MAC address tables are dynamic; moves are learned by observing new source addresses on different ports.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router’s primary criterion for deciding whether two hosts can communicate without its involvement is:

options.A: Whether they share the same MAC address
options.B: Whether their IP addresses belong to the same subnet (as determined by the subnet mask)
options.C: Whether they are connected to the same physical hub
options.D: Whether they use the same transport-layer port numbers

explanation: Hosts on the same IP subnet communicate directly at Layer 2; different subnets require a router.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: In a classic three-tier campus design the device that most commonly performs inter-VLAN routing for the access layer is located at the:

options.A: Access-layer pure Layer-2 switch
options.B: Distribution layer (often multilayer switches or routers)
options.C: Core layer only as a pure repeater

explanation: Distribution-layer devices traditionally aggregate access switches and provide Layer-3 services including inter-VLAN routing.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A device that regenerates a digital signal without examining any protocol headers is operating as a:

options.A: Router
options.B: Layer-2 switch
options.C: Repeater (or hub)

explanation: Pure regeneration is a Physical-layer function.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: Which of the following correctly describes the flooding behavior of a Layer-2 switch?

options.A: It never floods any frame
options.B: It floods unknown unicasts, broadcasts and multicasts (within the VLAN) out all ports belonging to that VLAN except the ingress port
options.C: It floods only to the router
options.D: It floods every frame to every port regardless of VLAN

explanation: Flooding is limited to the broadcast domain (VLAN) and never back out the arrival port.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A router that is configured with a static default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to a next hop will:

options.A: Drop every packet that does not match a more specific route
options.B: Forward packets for which no longer-matching route exists toward that next hop
options.C: Ignore the default route when a more specific route is present (longest-prefix match still applies)
options.D: Both B and C are correct

explanation: A default route is a last-resort entry; longer prefixes always take precedence.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: In Ethernet, the device that historically allowed two collision domains to be interconnected while still filtering traffic based on MAC addresses was the:

options.A: Hub
options.B: Repeater
options.C: Bridge

explanation: Bridges were the first devices to segment collision domains intelligently at Layer 2.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: A modern data-center leaf-spine fabric typically uses:

options.A: Only Layer-1 hubs
options.B: Layer-3 routing (often with ECMP) between leaf and spine switches, treating the underlay as a routed network
options.C: A single large Layer-2 domain with no routing

explanation: Contemporary leaf-spine designs favour Layer-3 fabrics for scalability and equal-cost multipath.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: When a host sends an ARP request for a target that lies on a different IP subnet, the ARP request is:

options.A: Answered directly by the remote host
options.B: Answered by the local router (proxy ARP in some designs) or, more commonly, the host does not ARP for remote addresses; it ARPs for its default gateway instead
options.C: Flooded by every router in the Internet

explanation: Hosts ARP only for addresses on their own subnet; remote destinations are reached via the default gateway.

topic: 3.1 Networking Devices: Repeater, Hub, Switch, Router
question: The fundamental reason a pure Layer-2 network cannot scale indefinitely without routers or multilayer switches is that:

options.A: MAC addresses run out after a few hundred hosts
options.B: Broadcasts, unknown unicasts and the size of MAC address tables grow with the diameter of the Layer-2 domain, eventually overwhelming links and switch resources
options.C: IP addresses cannot be used inside a Layer-2 domain
options.D: Spanning Tree always blocks every port

explanation: Large flat Layer-2 domains suffer from broadcast overhead, slow convergence and table-size limitations; Layer-3 segmentation restores scalability.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Circuit switching is characterized by the establishment of a dedicated end-to-end path that remains allocated for the entire duration of a communication session. This statement is:

options.A: False – circuit switching never reserves resources
options.B: True
options.C: True only for packet switching

explanation: Circuit switching (classic telephony) reserves a continuous path for the call; bandwidth is dedicated whether or not data are flowing.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Packet switching differs from circuit switching mainly in that:

options.A: A dedicated physical circuit is always established for the whole session
options.B: Data are divided into packets that are routed independently and may take different paths; no dedicated end-to-end circuit is reserved
options.C: It can be used only for voice
options.D: It requires the same path for every packet of a conversation

explanation: Packet switching is connectionless (or uses virtual circuits) and statistical multiplexing.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A modem’s fundamental role is to:

options.A: Route IP packets between autonomous systems
options.B: Modulate digital bitstreams onto an analog carrier for transmission over analog media and demodulate the received analog signal back into digital form
options.C: Switch frames based solely on MAC addresses

explanation: Modem = modulator-demodulator; it bridges the digital and analog domains.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) is preferred over simple parity for many data-link protocols because:

options.A: It requires no extra bits
options.B: It has strong burst-error detection capability through polynomial division
options.C: It can correct any number of errors automatically
options.D: It is used only for encryption

explanation: CRC detects a wide class of burst errors with high probability using a small number of redundant bits.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Hamming codes are primarily used for:

options.A: Compressing data
options.B: Detecting and correcting single-bit errors (and detecting double-bit errors in the extended form)
options.C: Encrypting messages

explanation: Hamming distance properties allow single-error correction and double-error detection.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In circuit switching the three classic phases of a connection are:

options.A: Modulation, demodulation, and termination
options.B: Connection establishment, data transfer, and connection release
options.C: Packetization, routing, and reassembly only

explanation: A circuit must be set up before data can flow and is torn down afterwards.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Message switching (store-and-forward of entire messages) differs from packet switching in that:

options.A: Messages are never stored at intermediate nodes
options.B: An entire message is received, stored, and then forwarded as a unit, whereas packet switching divides the message into smaller packets that can be interleaved
options.C: It is identical to circuit switching
options.D: It requires a dedicated end-to-end circuit

explanation: Message switching treats the whole message as the unit of transfer; packet switching uses smaller, independent packets.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The Hamming distance between two equal-length binary strings is:

options.A: The sum of their numeric values
options.B: The number of bit positions in which they differ
options.C: Always equal to 1
options.D: The length of the longer string

explanation: Hamming distance counts differing positions and underpins error-detection/correction capability.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A parity bit can detect:

options.A: Any number of bit errors
options.B: An odd number of bit flips (single parity) but cannot correct errors
options.C: Only even numbers of errors

explanation: A single parity bit changes when an odd number of bits flip; it provides detection, not correction.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a virtual-circuit packet-switched network a connection is first established so that:

options.A: Every packet is routed completely independently with no state at intermediate nodes
options.B: A path is chosen and connection state (or labels) is installed at the switches; subsequent packets of the flow follow the same path
options.C: A dedicated physical circuit is reserved for the lifetime of the call
options.D: No packets can ever be lost

explanation: Virtual circuits combine connection-oriented signalling with packet multiplexing.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Datagram packet switching is characterized by:

options.A: A permanent dedicated circuit for each conversation
options.B: Each packet carrying full addressing information and being routed independently; intermediate nodes need not maintain per-flow state
options.C: The requirement that all packets of a message take the identical path

explanation: Classic IP is a datagram service; each packet is self-contained.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The generator polynomial of a CRC is used to:

options.A: Encrypt the payload
options.B: Perform polynomial division (modulo-2) of the message so that the remainder becomes the CRC check bits
options.C: Compress the frame

explanation: CRC computation is polynomial arithmetic over GF(2); the remainder is appended as the FCS.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A modem that implements V.90 or a similar standard is typically used to:

options.A: Route packets at Layer 3
options.B: Carry digital data over the analog Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) local loop
options.C: Switch Ethernet frames

explanation: Dial-up modems convert between the digital computer interface and the analog telephone line.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Forward Error Correction (FEC) differs from Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ) in that:

options.A: FEC requires a return channel for acknowledgements
