options.B: FEC adds redundant information so that the receiver can correct errors without retransmission, whereas ARQ relies on detection and retransmission
options.C: ARQ never retransmits
options.D: FEC is used only for encryption

explanation: FEC is open-loop correction; ARQ is closed-loop retransmission.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a stop-and-wait ARQ protocol the sender:

options.A: Continuously transmits packets without waiting for any acknowledgement
options.B: Transmits one frame and then waits for an acknowledgement (or timeout) before sending the next frame
options.C: Never retransmits lost frames
options.D: Uses only FEC with no acknowledgements

explanation: Stop-and-wait is the simplest ARQ; efficiency is limited by the round-trip time.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Go-Back-N ARQ improves on stop-and-wait by:

options.A: Allowing the sender to transmit up to N frames before needing an acknowledgement, but forcing retransmission of all frames from the point of the first loss
options.B: Never retransmitting any frame
options.C: Using only a single frame buffer at the receiver

explanation: Go-Back-N pipelines frames but retransmits the entire window after an error.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Selective-Repeat ARQ differs from Go-Back-N in that:

options.A: It retransmits every frame after any loss
options.B: Only the lost or errored frames are retransmitted; correctly received frames are buffered by the receiver
options.C: It requires no sequence numbers

explanation: Selective Repeat minimizes retransmissions at the cost of more receiver complexity and buffering.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The minimum Hamming distance of a code determines:

options.A: Only the data rate
options.B: The maximum number of errors that can be detected or corrected by the code
options.C: The physical length of the cable

explanation: A code with minimum distance d can detect up to d−1 errors and correct up to ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a circuit-switched telephone network the resource that is reserved during the call setup phase is typically:

options.A: Only a logical label with no bandwidth guarantee
options.B: A dedicated portion of bandwidth (or a time slot / frequency channel) along the entire path
options.C: A single shared packet queue
options.D: Nothing; resources are allocated on demand per packet

explanation: Circuit switching guarantees capacity by reserving it for the lifetime of the call.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A checksum that simply sums all the bytes of a message modulo 256 can detect:

options.A: All possible error patterns
options.B: Many (but not all) error patterns; it is weaker than a well-chosen CRC for burst errors
options.C: No errors at all
options.D: Only errors that change the length of the message

explanation: Simple checksums are computationally cheap but have poorer detection properties than CRC polynomials.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In the context of remote access, a dial-up connection using a modem typically involves:

options.A: A permanent digital leased line
options.B: Establishing a temporary circuit through the PSTN and then exchanging digital data via modulation
options.C: Only optical switching

explanation: Classic dial-up sets up a telephone circuit and then runs a modem protocol over it.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A two-dimensional parity scheme (parity on rows and columns) can:

options.A: Detect and correct a single-bit error and detect many double-bit errors
options.B: Correct any number of errors
options.C: Detect no errors

explanation: The intersection of a failing row and column parity identifies the erroneous bit; additional patterns can still be detected.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In packet switching statistical multiplexing means that:

options.A: Each flow receives a permanently dedicated time slot
options.B: Bandwidth is shared dynamically among active flows; a flow obtains capacity only when it has packets to send
options.C: No multiplexing occurs
options.D: All flows are blocked when any one flow is active

explanation: Statistical multiplexing exploits the fact that not all sources are active simultaneously.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The Frame Check Sequence (FCS) field in an Ethernet frame is typically a:

options.A: Simple parity bit
options.B: 32-bit CRC computed over the frame contents
options.C: Hamming code of length 7
options.D: Cryptographic hash used for authentication only

explanation: Ethernet uses CRC-32 as its FCS for strong error detection.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A major advantage of packet switching over circuit switching for bursty data traffic is:

options.A: Guaranteed constant bandwidth for every flow regardless of activity
options.B: More efficient use of transmission capacity because idle periods of one flow can be used by other flows
options.C: The complete absence of any queuing delay
options.D: The elimination of all routing decisions

explanation: Statistical sharing of capacity is the key efficiency gain for data.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a sliding-window protocol the window size primarily limits:

options.A: The physical length of the cable
options.B: The number of unacknowledged frames the sender may have outstanding
options.C: The IP version
options.D: The number of routers in the path

explanation: The window controls how far ahead the sender may get before needing feedback.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A modem that supports ADSL technology is designed to:

options.A: Provide symmetric high-speed service over fiber only
options.B: Deliver asymmetric digital service over the existing copper telephone local loop, with higher downstream than upstream rates
options.C: Replace all routers in the Internet
options.D: Operate only as a pure optical repeater

explanation: ADSL exploits the copper loop with discrete multitone modulation and asymmetric rate allocation.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Even parity means that:

options.A: The total number of 1-bits in the data plus parity bit is odd
options.B: The total number of 1-bits in the data plus parity bit is even
options.C: No parity bit is used

explanation: Even parity forces the overall count of 1s to be even.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a network that uses both FEC and ARQ, the typical division of labour is:

options.A: FEC handles all residual errors so that ARQ is never needed
options.B: FEC corrects the most common error patterns; ARQ recovers from the remaining uncorrectable errors by retransmission
options.C: ARQ is used only for encryption
options.D: FEC is used only on the reverse channel

explanation: Hybrid schemes combine the low latency of FEC with the reliability of ARQ.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A virtual circuit identifier (VCI) or label in a connection-oriented packet network is used to:

options.A: Carry the full global destination address in every packet
options.B: Index the forwarding state that was installed during connection setup, allowing short labels instead of full addresses
options.C: Encrypt the payload
options.D: Replace the need for any switching

explanation: Labels enable efficient table lookup once the path has been established.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The principal disadvantage of pure stop-and-wait ARQ on a long-fat pipe (high bandwidth-delay product) is:

options.A: It never retransmits
options.B: Channel utilization becomes very low because the sender spends most of its time waiting for acknowledgements
options.C: It requires an infinite window

explanation: Utilization ≈ packet transmission time / round-trip time, which is tiny on high-BDP paths.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A CRC that uses a generator polynomial of degree r produces a check field of length:

options.A: r bits (the remainder of the polynomial division)
options.B: Always 1 bit
options.C: The same length as the message

explanation: The remainder has degree less than the generator, hence at most r bits.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In the context of switching, a ‘store-and-forward’ node:

options.A: Begins transmitting a packet toward the next hop before the entire packet has been received
options.B: Receives the complete packet (or frame), checks it, and only then forwards it
options.C: Never stores any data
options.D: Is used only in circuit switching

explanation: Store-and-forward is the classic behaviour of packet switches and of store-and-forward message switches.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A cut-through packet switch (or frame switch) reduces latency by:

options.A: Waiting for the entire packet and its CRC before forwarding
options.B: Beginning to forward the packet as soon as the destination address (or label) has been read, before the whole packet arrives
options.C: Dropping every packet
options.D: Converting every packet into a circuit

explanation: Cut-through trading error detection for lower latency is common in high-speed switches.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The purpose of a longitudinal redundancy check (LRC) or block parity is to:

options.A: Replace CRC entirely in all modern protocols
options.B: Provide an additional parity dimension across a block of characters, improving detection of certain error patterns
options.C: Encrypt the block

explanation: LRC is a simple two-dimensional parity scheme used historically in character-oriented protocols.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a telephone modem negotiation the phase that determines the highest mutually supported modulation parameters is called:

options.A: IP routing
options.B: Training / handshaking (or modem negotiation)
options.C: Spanning-tree calculation

explanation: Modems exchange capabilities and probe the channel before settling on a data rate and constellation.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A code with minimum Hamming distance 3 can:

options.A: Correct 2 errors and detect 3 errors
options.B: Correct 1 error and detect (at least) 2 errors
options.C: Correct 3 errors

explanation: In general, d_min = 3 → t = 1 correction, detection of up to 2 errors.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a packet-switched network the intermediate nodes are primarily responsible for:

options.A: Establishing a dedicated physical circuit for each conversation
options.B: Receiving packets, performing a forwarding decision, and transmitting them on the appropriate outgoing link (store-and-forward or cut-through)
options.C: Modulating analog signals only

explanation: Packet switches forward self-contained packets according to their headers and local state.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A major reason that CRC is computed in hardware on most network interfaces is:

options.A: CRC is too simple for software
options.B: Line-rate generation and checking of CRC requires only a small linear-feedback shift register and must not consume significant CPU cycles
options.C: Software cannot perform polynomial division
options.D: CRC is used only for encryption

explanation: Hardware CRC engines are cheap and operate at wire speed.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In the context of remote access, PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) is commonly used to:

options.A: Route between autonomous systems with full BGP
options.B: Carry network-layer packets (IP, etc.) over a serial point-to-point link, providing framing, authentication and optional compression/encryption
options.C: Replace Ethernet completely on LANs

explanation: PPP is the standard data-link protocol for dial-up, DSL and many serial WAN links.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A burst error of length L is an error pattern in which:

options.A: At most one bit is inverted
options.B: All errors are confined to a span of L consecutive bits (the first and last of which are in error)
options.C: Every bit of the message is inverted

explanation: Burst-error models capture the clustered nature of many physical-channel impairments.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the relationship between circuit switching and quality of service for constant-bit-rate traffic?

options.A: Circuit switching cannot provide any delay guarantees
options.B: Once a circuit is established, the reserved capacity yields predictable delay and no congestion for that flow
options.C: Packet switching always provides stricter guarantees than circuit switching
options.D: Circuit switching is identical to best-effort datagram service

explanation: Dedicated resources give circuit switching natural QoS properties for CBR streams.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a Go-Back-N sender window of size N, the maximum number of frames that may be unacknowledged is:

options.B: N
options.C: Unlimited

explanation: The window size N is exactly the limit on outstanding frames.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A modem’s ‘training sequence’ is used primarily to:

options.A: Assign IP addresses
options.B: Allow the receiver to estimate channel characteristics and to adapt equalizer and constellation parameters before user data are sent
options.C: Encrypt the subsequent payload

explanation: Training symbols probe the channel so that the demodulator can converge.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: The efficiency of stop-and-wait ARQ on a channel with negligible error rate is approximately:

options.A: 100 % regardless of propagation delay
options.B: Transmission time of the frame divided by (transmission time + round-trip propagation delay + processing)
options.C: Always greater than 1

explanation: Utilization collapses when propagation delay dominates transmission time.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a network that uses pure datagram switching, intermediate routers:

options.A: Maintain soft or hard state for every end-to-end flow
options.B: Forward each packet independently according to its destination address and the current routing table; no per-flow state is required
options.C: Establish a dedicated circuit before any packet may be sent

explanation: Stateless forwarding is a defining property of classic datagram networks such as IP.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A single-bit error in a received codeword of a Hamming code can be corrected by:

options.A: Ignoring the syndrome
options.B: Computing the syndrome (which equals the binary representation of the error position) and flipping the indicated bit
options.C: Retransmitting the entire message without using the code
options.D: Adding a parity bit after the fact

explanation: The syndrome of a Hamming code directly identifies the errored bit position.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between modulation and demodulation in a modem?

options.A: Modulation converts analog signals into digital form; demodulation does the reverse
options.B: Modulation impresses digital information onto an analog carrier; demodulation recovers the digital information from the received analog waveform
options.C: Both are identical processes
options.D: Neither is required for digital transmission over analog media

explanation: Modulation is the forward conversion; demodulation is the inverse at the receiver.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: In a selective-repeat receiver the principal additional complexity compared with Go-Back-N is:

options.A: The complete absence of sequence numbers
options.B: The need to buffer out-of-order frames and to maintain a more sophisticated acknowledgement / retransmission map
options.C: The requirement to retransmit every frame after any loss
options.D: The elimination of the sender window

explanation: Selective Repeat keeps correctly received frames and requests only the missing ones.

topic: 3.2 Switching Technologies, Modems and Remote Access, Error Detection & Correction
question: A fundamental trade-off in the design of error-control schemes for high-speed links is:

options.A: Between the strength of the code (detection/correction capability) and the overhead in bandwidth and processing, versus the latency and bandwidth cost of retransmissions
options.B: Between using only parity and using no redundancy at all
options.C: Between circuit switching and having no switching
options.D: Between modulation and the complete absence of a physical layer

explanation: Stronger codes cost more overhead; weaker codes force more ARQ activity. The optimum depends on the channel and the delay constraints.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An IPv4 address is composed of how many bits?

options.A: 16 bits
options.B: 32 bits
options.C: 64 bits

explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: DNS is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Encrypting web traffic
options.B: Translating human-readable domain names into IP addresses
options.C: Assigning MAC addresses to network interfaces
options.D: Routing packets based solely on AS numbers

explanation: The Domain Name System is the Internet’s distributed name-to-address resolution service.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: Which protocol provides reliable, ordered, connection-oriented byte-stream delivery between applications?

options.A: UDP
options.B: TCP
options.C: IP

explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; UDP is connectionless and unreliable.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) is used to:

options.A: Map an IP address to a MAC address on a local network
options.B: Translate domain names to IP addresses
options.C: Assign IP addresses dynamically
options.D: Route packets between different autonomous systems

explanation: ARP resolves Layer-3 addresses to Layer-2 addresses within a broadcast domain.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A /27 IPv4 subnet mask (255.255.255.224) leaves how many host bits, and therefore how many usable host addresses (after subtracting network and broadcast)?

options.A: 5 host bits → 30 usable hosts
options.B: 3 host bits → 6 usable hosts
options.C: 7 host bits → 126 usable hosts

explanation: 32−27 = 5 host bits; 2^5 − 2 = 30 usable addresses.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: NAPT / PAT (Network Address Port Translation) allows:

options.A: Only a one-to-one permanent mapping of private to public addresses
options.B: Multiple private hosts to share a single public IP address by translating both the address and the transport-layer port numbers
options.C: No translation of any addresses
options.D: Only the translation of MAC addresses

explanation: PAT multiplexes many internal sessions onto one external address using port numbers.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: DHCP is used to:

options.A: Resolve domain names to IP addresses
options.B: Dynamically assign IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways and other configuration parameters to hosts
options.C: Map IP addresses to MAC addresses

explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automates host network configuration.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An IPv6 address is composed of how many bits?

options.A: 32 bits
options.B: 64 bits
options.C: 128 bits

explanation: IPv6 expands the address space to 128 bits.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: UDP is preferred over TCP for applications that:

options.A: Require strict in-order reliable delivery of every byte
options.B: Can tolerate occasional loss and need low latency or simple request-reply semantics (e.g., DNS, real-time media, some gaming)
options.C: Must establish a connection before any data can be sent

explanation: UDP’s lack of connection setup and retransmission makes it suitable for latency-sensitive or simple transactions.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The private IPv4 address ranges defined by RFC 1918 include:
explanation: These three blocks are reserved for private use and are not globally routable.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A DNS recursive resolver is responsible for:

options.A: Only storing the authoritative zone data for a single domain
options.B: Accepting queries from clients and performing the iterative lookups necessary to obtain the final answer, then returning it to the client
options.C: Assigning IP addresses via DHCP
options.D: Encrypting every DNS packet with IPsec by default

explanation: Recursive resolvers hide the complexity of the DNS hierarchy from end hosts.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In IPv4 classful addressing, a Class B network originally used a default mask of:
explanation: Class B addresses begin with 10 in binary and traditionally used a /16 mask.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) allows:

options.A: Only the original Class A/B/C boundaries
options.B: Arbitrary-length network prefixes, enabling more efficient allocation and aggregation of address blocks
options.C: Only 8-bit prefixes

explanation: CIDR replaced rigid classful boundaries with flexible prefix lengths.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: ICMP is used primarily for:

options.A: Reliable byte-stream transport between applications
options.B: Network-layer diagnostic and error-reporting messages (echo, destination unreachable, time exceeded, etc.)
options.C: Resolving domain names

explanation: ICMP is the companion protocol to IP for control and error messages.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A /24 IPv4 network can contain how many usable host addresses?
explanation: 2^8 − 2 = 254 (network and broadcast addresses are reserved).

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The well-known port number traditionally associated with HTTP is:
explanation: Port 80 is the default for unencrypted HTTP; 443 is used for HTTPS.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An anycast address is characterized by the property that:

options.A: It identifies a single unique interface worldwide
options.B: The same address is assigned to multiple interfaces (usually in different locations); a packet is delivered to the ‘nearest’ one according to routing metrics
options.C: It is used only for broadcast within a LAN
options.D: It can never appear in a routing table

explanation: Anycast is used for services such as DNS root servers and CDNs to direct clients to a nearby instance.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In the DNS hierarchy the root name servers are responsible for:

options.A: Storing the A records of every host on the Internet
options.B: Providing referrals to the authoritative servers of the top-level domains (TLDs)
options.C: Assigning IP addresses via DHCP

explanation: Root servers know the TLD name servers; they do not hold the final host records.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A TCP connection is uniquely identified by the 4-tuple consisting of:

options.A: Only the two IP addresses
options.B: Source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port
options.C: Only the two port numbers
options.D: The MAC addresses of the endpoints

explanation: The 4-tuple distinguishes concurrent connections between the same pair of hosts.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: RARP (Reverse Address Resolution Protocol) was historically used to:

options.A: Map a known MAC address to an IP address (the opposite of ARP)
options.B: Translate domain names to IP addresses
options.C: Encrypt IP packets

explanation: RARP allowed diskless hosts to discover their own IP address from their MAC address; it has largely been superseded by DHCP/BOOTP.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In IPv6 the interface identifier portion of a unicast address is typically:

options.A: 16 bits long
options.B: 64 bits long (often derived from the MAC address via EUI-64 or generated randomly for privacy)
options.C: 32 bits long

explanation: The standard /64 subnet leaves 64 bits for the interface identifier.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A DNS MX record is used to:

options.A: Map a hostname to an IPv4 address
options.B: Specify the mail servers responsible for accepting email for a domain
options.C: Indicate the authoritative name servers for a zone

explanation: Mail eXchanger records direct SMTP traffic to the appropriate servers.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: When a host needs to send a packet to a destination on a different subnet, it:

options.A: ARPs directly for the destination’s MAC address
options.B: ARPs for the MAC address of its configured default gateway and sends the packet to that gateway
options.C: Broadcasts the IP packet to the entire Internet

explanation: Remote destinations are reached via the default gateway; ARP is performed only for on-link addresses.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The loopback address range in IPv4 is:
explanation: 127.0.0.0/8 is reserved for loopback; 127.0.0.1 is the common address used by a host to refer to itself.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A TCP three-way handshake consists of the exchange of which segments (in order)?

options.A: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK
options.B: ACK, SYN, FIN
options.C: FIN, ACK, SYN

explanation: The classic three-way handshake establishes sequence numbers and confirms reachability in both directions.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An authoritative DNS name server for a zone is the server that:

options.A: Only caches answers obtained from other servers
options.B: Holds the definitive, administrator-configured data for that zone and answers queries from that data
options.C: Assigns IP addresses via DHCP

explanation: Authoritative servers are the source of truth for their zones; recursive resolvers cache their answers.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In IPv4, the directed broadcast address of a subnet is formed by:

options.A: Setting all host bits to 0
options.B: Setting all host bits to 1
options.C: Using the address 255.255.255.255 exclusively
options.D: Using the first address of the subnet

explanation: All-ones in the host portion is the subnet-directed broadcast address.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: NAT (Network Address Translation) in its basic form allows a private network to:

options.A: Use globally unique addresses for every internal host without any translation
options.B: Share a smaller number of public addresses among a larger number of private hosts by rewriting address (and possibly port) fields
options.C: Eliminate the need for any routing

explanation: NAT conserves public address space by multiplexing internal hosts onto fewer external addresses.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A PTR record in DNS is used for:

options.A: Mapping a hostname to an IPv4 address
options.B: Mapping an IP address back to a hostname (reverse lookup)
options.C: Indicating mail servers

explanation: Pointer records enable reverse DNS resolution.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The IPv4 header field that limits the lifetime of a packet and is decremented by each router is the:

options.A: Source Address
options.B: Time-to-Live (TTL) / Hop Limit
options.C: Protocol field

explanation: TTL prevents packets from circulating indefinitely; when it reaches zero the packet is discarded.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In a /30 point-to-point IPv4 link the number of usable host addresses is:
explanation: 2 host bits → 4 addresses total − network − broadcast = 2 usable addresses, ideal for a point-to-point link.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A DNS CNAME record is used to:

options.A: Map a name directly to an IP address
options.B: Create an alias that points to another domain name (canonical name)
options.C: Indicate the primary mail server

explanation: CNAME provides a level of indirection so that one hostname can be an alias for another.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The transport-layer port numbers occupy how many bits in the TCP and UDP headers?

options.A: 8 bits
options.B: 16 bits
options.C: 32 bits

explanation: Source and destination ports are each 16-bit fields, allowing 65 536 possible ports.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An IPv6 link-local address is characterized by the prefix:
explanation: fe80::/10 addresses are valid only on the local link and are used for neighbour discovery, etc.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: When a TCP receiver advertises a window of zero it is telling the sender that:

options.A: The connection must be closed immediately
options.B: The receiver currently has no buffer space and the sender must stop transmitting data until a non-zero window is advertised
options.C: The sender should increase its congestion window
options.D: All previous data have been lost

explanation: A zero window is flow-control feedback; the sender probes later to discover when space becomes available.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A public IP address is distinguished from a private IP address by the fact that:

options.A: Private addresses are globally unique and routable on the public Internet
options.B: Public addresses are globally unique and can be routed on the public Internet, whereas private addresses are not globally routable
options.C: There is no difference
options.D: Private addresses are longer than public addresses

explanation: RFC 1918 private addresses must be translated (NAT) before they can appear on the public Internet.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The process by which a DNS resolver obtains the IP address of a name by querying a sequence of servers starting from the root is called:

options.A: A recursive query only
options.B: An iterative (or non-recursive) resolution process
options.C: A DHCP discovery

explanation: Iterative resolution is the step-by-step referral process; a recursive resolver performs it on behalf of the client.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In IPv4 the limited broadcast address that is never forwarded by routers is:
explanation: 255.255.255.255 is the local-network broadcast; routers do not forward it.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A TCP segment that carries the FIN flag indicates that:

options.A: The sender has no more data to send and wishes to close its side of the connection
options.B: The connection must be reset immediately
options.C: The window size is zero
options.D: The segment contains only an acknowledgement

explanation: FIN is the graceful-close signal; each side must send its own FIN to fully terminate the connection.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An IPv6 multicast address begins with the prefix:
explanation: All IPv6 multicast addresses share the leading octet 0xff.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The purpose of the TCP checksum is to:

options.A: Encrypt the payload
options.B: Detect (with high probability) corruption of the TCP header, payload and a pseudo-header that includes IP addresses
options.C: Guarantee delivery of every segment

explanation: The checksum provides end-to-end error detection across the TCP segment and critical IP fields.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A subnet mask of 255.255.255.248 corresponds to a prefix length of:
explanation: 255.255.255.248 = /29 (3 host bits, 6 usable addresses).

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: In the DNS, a zone transfer is the mechanism by which:

options.A: A client obtains the IP address of a single host
options.B: A secondary (slave) name server obtains a complete copy of the zone data from the primary (master) server
options.C: DHCP assigns addresses

explanation: Zone transfers keep secondary servers synchronized with the primary.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A TCP socket in the LISTEN state is waiting for:

options.A: A FIN from the remote peer
options.B: An incoming SYN that will begin a new connection
options.C: An ARP reply

explanation: LISTEN is the passive-open state of a server socket.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The IPv4 address 224.0.0.1 is a well-known:

options.A: Private unicast address
options.B: Multicast address meaning ‘all hosts on this subnet’
options.C: Loopback address

explanation: 224.0.0.1 is the all-hosts multicast address on the local link.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: When a host’s ARP cache contains no entry for a needed next-hop IP address, the host:

options.A: Drops the packet silently
options.B: Broadcasts an ARP request and, while waiting for the reply, may queue the original packet
options.C: Sends the packet to the limited broadcast address 255.255.255.255 as a substitute

explanation: ARP resolution is performed on demand; the packet is held until the MAC address is known.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: An IPv6 Unique Local Address (ULA) is intended for:

options.A: Global Internet routing without any restriction
options.B: Addressing within a site or organisation, analogous to IPv4 private addresses, and is not expected to be globally routable
options.C: Only loopback communication

explanation: ULAs (fc00::/7) provide private addressing in IPv6.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The TCP congestion-control algorithm that treats packet loss as a signal of congestion and halves the congestion window is historically known as:

options.A: Stop-and-wait
options.B: TCP Tahoe / Reno (additive increase / multiplicative decrease and slow-start)
options.C: Selective Repeat ARQ only

explanation: Classic TCP congestion control reacts to loss by reducing the sending rate.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: A DNS SOA (Start of Authority) record contains, among other fields:

options.A: Only an IP address
options.B: The primary name server for the zone, the responsible party’s email, serial number and timer values that control zone transfers and caching
options.C: A list of all hosts in the zone

explanation: The SOA record defines administrative and timing parameters for the zone.

topic: 3.3 Internet Services, Internet Protocol/addressing
question: The fundamental reason that IPv6 was developed is that:

options.A: IPv4 addresses were becoming exhausted and a larger address space together with improved features was required
options.B: TCP was no longer needed
options.C: Ethernet frames had become too small

explanation: Address exhaustion of the 32-bit IPv4 space was the primary driver; IPv6 also introduced other architectural improvements.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A digital signature is created by:

options.A: Encrypting the entire message with the recipient’s public key
options.B: Computing a hash of the message and encrypting that hash with the signer’s private key
options.C: Encrypting the message with a symmetric key that is never shared
options.D: Appending a CRC to the message

explanation: The private-key encryption of the hash proves both integrity and origin; anyone can verify with the public key.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: Symmetric-key cryptography is distinguished from public-key cryptography by the fact that:

options.A: The same secret key is used for both encryption and decryption
options.B: A different key is used for encryption and decryption and the encryption key can be published
options.C: No keys are required at all

explanation: Symmetric algorithms (AES, ChaCha20, etc.) share a single secret; asymmetric algorithms use a key pair.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A firewall that examines the state of TCP connections (e.g., whether a packet belongs to an established session) is called a:

options.A: Packet-filter firewall that looks only at individual packets in isolation
options.B: Stateful (or stateful-inspection) firewall
options.C: Application-layer proxy only

explanation: Stateful firewalls keep a connection table and permit return traffic that matches existing sessions.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The Diffie–Hellman key-exchange protocol allows two parties to:

options.A: Authenticate each other with certificates
options.B: Agree on a shared secret over an insecure channel without having previously shared any secret
options.C: Encrypt messages with RSA directly

explanation: Diffie–Hellman produces a shared secret; it does not by itself provide authentication.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A one-way hash function is designed so that:

options.A: It is easy to invert and find a pre-image for any hash value
options.B: It is computationally infeasible to find any input that maps to a given hash value (pre-image resistance) and infeasible to find two inputs that collide
options.C: It expands a short key into a long keystream
options.D: It is identical to a block cipher

explanation: Cryptographic hashes provide compression, one-wayness and collision resistance.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A man-in-the-middle attack on an unauthenticated Diffie–Hellman exchange succeeds because:

options.A: Diffie–Hellman is broken by modern computers
options.B: An attacker can establish separate shared secrets with each party and relay messages, since neither party verifies the identity of the other
options.C: Public keys cannot be used

explanation: Without authentication, each party has no way to know whether it is talking to the intended peer or to an intermediary.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: AES is an example of a:

options.A: Public-key encryption algorithm
options.B: Symmetric block cipher that operates on fixed-size blocks (128 bits) with key sizes of 128, 192 or 256 bits
options.C: Stream cipher only

explanation: AES (Rijndael) is the current NIST standard symmetric block cipher.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A certificate authority (CA) in a public-key infrastructure is trusted to:

options.A: Generate every user’s private key
options.B: Issue digital certificates that bind a public key to an identity after verifying that identity
options.C: Decrypt all traffic on the Internet
options.D: Replace the need for any private keys

explanation: CAs are the trust anchors of the X.509 certificate system used by TLS and many other protocols.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A network intrusion detection system (NIDS) that examines packet payloads for known attack signatures is classified as:

options.A: Anomaly-based only
options.B: Signature-based (or misuse-based) detection
options.C: A pure firewall that never inspects payloads

explanation: Signature-based NIDS match observed traffic against a database of known malicious patterns.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The primary purpose of a nonce (or challenge) in an authentication protocol is to:

options.A: Encrypt the password permanently
options.B: Ensure freshness and prevent replay of previously captured authentication messages
options.C: Replace the need for any cryptographic keys

explanation: A nonce that is used only once forces the authenticating party to prove possession of the secret for the current session.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: RSA encryption of a message m under a public key (n, e) is performed by computing:

options.A: m XOR e
options.B: m^e mod n
options.C: m + e mod n
options.D: The hash of m encrypted with a symmetric key

explanation: The core RSA operation is modular exponentiation with the public exponent.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A VPN that encapsulates original IP packets inside new IP packets (often with encryption) is an example of:

options.A: A pure Layer-2 switch
options.B: An IP-in-IP or IPsec tunnel that provides a virtual private overlay across a public network
options.C: A simple Ethernet hub

explanation: Tunnel-mode IPsec or similar encapsulation creates a secure virtual link between sites or users.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: Perfect forward secrecy (PFS) in a key-exchange protocol means that:

options.A: Compromise of a long-term private key allows decryption of all past sessions
options.B: Compromise of a long-term private key does not allow an attacker to decrypt past session keys that were derived from ephemeral Diffie–Hellman exchanges
options.C: No encryption is used
options.D: All keys are static and never change

explanation: Ephemeral key agreement ensures that past session keys remain safe even if the long-term key is later compromised.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A buffer-overflow attack typically exploits:

options.A: A correctly bounds-checked input routine
options.B: A programming error that allows more data to be written into a fixed-size buffer than it can hold, potentially overwriting adjacent control data such as return addresses
options.C: The absence of any network connection

explanation: Classic stack- or heap-based overflows let an attacker seize control of program execution.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A message authentication code (MAC) provides:

options.A: Confidentiality of the message contents
options.B: Integrity and authenticity of a message under a shared secret key, without providing confidentiality by itself
options.C: Non-repudiation against the key holder in the same way a digital signature does
options.D: A one-way hash that requires no key

explanation: A MAC is a keyed integrity check; anyone holding the key can both generate and verify it.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In the TLS handshake the server proves possession of its private key by:

options.A: Sending its private key to the client
options.B: Signing a transcript of the handshake (or performing a key-exchange operation that requires the private key) so that the client can verify the signature with the public key from the certificate
options.C: Encrypting the entire handshake with a symmetric key known only to the CA
options.D: Using only Diffie–Hellman without any certificates

explanation: The CertificateVerify (or equivalent) message demonstrates that the server holds the private key corresponding to the presented certificate.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack aims to:

options.A: Steal confidential data without being noticed
options.B: Make a service or resource unavailable to legitimate users by exhausting bandwidth, CPU, memory or other critical resources
options.C: Install a permanent back-door for later use

explanation: Availability is the target of DoS/DDoS attacks.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: Salt is added to a password before hashing primarily to:

options.A: Make the hash shorter
options.B: Ensure that two users with the same password produce different stored hashes and to frustrate pre-computed rainbow-table attacks
options.C: Encrypt the password with AES
options.D: Replace the need for any hash function

explanation: A unique salt per password forces an attacker to compute hashes individually rather than using pre-computed tables.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A stateful packet-inspection firewall maintains:

options.A: No information about previous packets
options.B: A table of active connections / sessions so that return traffic and related packets can be permitted automatically
options.C: Only a static list of allowed IP addresses with no dynamic state
options.D: The private keys of all users

explanation: Connection tracking is the defining feature of stateful inspection.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: Cross-site scripting (XSS) is an attack that:

options.A: Exploits a buffer overflow in the operating-system kernel
options.B: Injects malicious script into a web page that is then executed in the browsers of other users who view that page
options.C: Floods a network with ICMP packets
options.D: Cracks a symmetric key by brute force

explanation: XSS abuses the trust a browser places in content received from a legitimate web site.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A public-key certificate (X.509) typically contains:

options.A: Only the subject’s private key
options.B: The subject’s public key, identity information, validity period, and a digital signature of the issuing CA
options.C: A symmetric session key only

explanation: The CA’s signature binds the public key to the claimed identity for a stated period.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A chosen-plaintext attack is one in which the adversary:

options.A: Only observes ciphertext
options.B: Can obtain the ciphertext corresponding to plaintexts of the adversary’s own choosing
options.C: Has no access to any encryption oracle

explanation: Chosen-plaintext capability is a standard attack model used to evaluate cipher strength.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: SQL injection succeeds when:

options.A: All user input is properly parameterized or escaped
options.B: An application concatenates unsanitized user input directly into a SQL query string, allowing the attacker to alter the query’s logic
options.C: The database is offline
options.D: HTTPS is used for the connection

explanation: Injection occurs when data are treated as code; prepared statements prevent it.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A stream cipher generates:

options.A: A fixed-size block of ciphertext for each fixed-size block of plaintext
options.B: A continuous keystream that is combined (usually by XOR) with the plaintext bit by bit or byte by byte
options.C: Only a message authentication code

explanation: Stream ciphers (e.g., ChaCha20, classic RC4) produce a running keystream.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The principle of least privilege requires that:

options.A: Every user and process be given the maximum possible rights
options.B: A subject be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform its authorized tasks
options.C: All users share a single administrator account

explanation: Least privilege limits the damage that can result from error or compromise.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A honeypot is a security mechanism whose primary purpose is to:

options.A: Replace the production firewall
options.B: Attract and observe attackers in a controlled environment so that their techniques can be studied and production systems protected
options.C: Store all user passwords in cleartext

explanation: Honeypots are decoy systems that yield intelligence about adversary behaviour.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In public-key cryptography the confidentiality of a message sent to Alice is achieved by:

options.A: Encrypting with Alice’s private key
options.B: Encrypting with Alice’s public key so that only Alice’s private key can decrypt it
options.C: Encrypting with a publicly known symmetric key
options.D: Hashing the message without any key

explanation: Anyone can encrypt to Alice with her public key; only she can decrypt.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A zero-day vulnerability is one that:

options.A: Has been publicly known and patched for many years
options.B: Is unknown to the vendor and for which no patch is yet available at the time it is exploited
options.C: Can never be exploited

explanation: Zero-day refers to the absence of prior public knowledge and of a vendor fix.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A cryptographic nonce must be:

options.A: Predictable and reused across many sessions
options.B: Unpredictable (or at least non-repeating) for the lifetime of the key with which it is used
options.C: Identical for every message
options.D: Derived only from the current time in a coarse granularity

explanation: Reuse of a nonce under the same key can completely break many constructions (e.g., CTR mode, GCM).

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A DMZ (demilitarized zone) in network architecture is typically used to:

options.A: Host only internal user workstations
options.B: Place publicly accessible services (web, mail, DNS) on a network segment that is isolated from the internal network by firewalls
options.C: Store all private keys in cleartext
options.D: Eliminate the need for any firewall

explanation: The DMZ limits the exposure of the internal network if a public-facing server is compromised.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The security property that a digital signature provides against the signer later denying having signed a message is called:

options.A: Confidentiality
options.B: Non-repudiation
options.C: Availability

explanation: Because only the holder of the private key could have produced the signature, the signer cannot credibly deny it.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A side-channel attack extracts secret information by observing:

options.A: Only the mathematical description of the algorithm
options.B: Physical phenomena such as timing, power consumption, electromagnetic radiation or acoustic emanations that depend on the secret data
options.C: Only the ciphertext

explanation: Side channels exploit implementation characteristics rather than pure mathematical weaknesses.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In the context of IPsec, the Authentication Header (AH) protocol provides:

options.A: Confidentiality of the payload
options.B: Integrity and origin authentication of the IP packet (including parts of the header) but not confidentiality
options.C: Only key exchange

explanation: AH authenticates; ESP can provide both confidentiality and authentication.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A rainbow table is a pre-computed data structure used to:

options.A: Speed up encryption of large files
options.B: Accelerate the cracking of unsalted (or poorly salted) password hashes by trading storage for computation
options.C: Generate digital certificates

explanation: Rainbow tables store chains of hash reductions; salting defeats them.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A mutual authentication protocol guarantees that:

options.A: Only the client authenticates to the server
options.B: Both parties prove their identities to each other
options.C: No authentication occurs
options.D: Only the server authenticates to the client

explanation: Mutual authentication prevents both client and server impersonation.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The AES key sizes of 128, 192 and 256 bits refer to:

options.A: The size of the plaintext blocks
options.B: The length of the secret key used by the cipher
options.C: The size of the IV only

explanation: AES always uses 128-bit blocks; the three standard key lengths give different security levels and round counts.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A replay attack is thwarted by:

options.A: Using the same ciphertext every time
options.B: Including a nonce, timestamp or sequence number that the receiver can check for freshness
options.C: Never using any cryptography

explanation: Freshness indicators make a captured message invalid for later use.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In a public-key infrastructure the revocation of a compromised certificate is commonly published via:

options.A: Only a verbal announcement
options.B: Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) or Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responders
options.C: Changing the CA’s private key without notice
options.D: Deleting the certificate from the holder’s machine only

explanation: CRLs and OCSP allow relying parties to learn that a previously valid certificate should no longer be trusted.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A polymorphic virus is characterized by:

options.A: Always having exactly the same binary representation
options.B: Changing its appearance (encryption, code rearrangement, etc.) on each infection while preserving its functional payload, thereby complicating signature-based detection
options.C: Never replicating

explanation: Polymorphism is a classic evasion technique against static antivirus signatures.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The security goal of integrity is violated when:

options.A: An unauthorized party merely reads a message
options.B: An unauthorized party modifies a message (or a stored datum) without detection
options.C: A service becomes temporarily unavailable

explanation: Integrity concerns the detection (and ideally prevention) of unauthorized alteration.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A keyed-hash message authentication code (HMAC) is constructed by:

options.A: Simply hashing the message with no key
options.B: Combining a secret key with the message in a carefully designed way and then applying a cryptographic hash function
options.C: Encrypting the message with AES and discarding the key

explanation: HMAC nests the key and the message inside the hash to produce a secure MAC.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In the Bell–LaPadula confidentiality model the ‘no-read-up’ rule states that:

options.A: A subject may read any object regardless of classification
options.B: A subject may not read an object whose security level is higher than the subject’s clearance
options.C: A subject may write to any higher level
options.D: There are no restrictions on reading

explanation: Simple Security Property (no-read-up) and the *-property (no-write-down) protect confidentiality.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A padding-oracle attack exploits:

options.A: A correct implementation of authenticated encryption
options.B: An implementation that reveals whether the padding of a decrypted ciphertext is valid, thereby leaking information that can be used to decrypt arbitrary ciphertexts
options.C: The complete absence of any padding
options.D: Only the public key of the server

explanation: Error messages or timing differences that disclose padding validity turn a decryption oracle into a decryption engine.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The purpose of an initialization vector (IV) or nonce in a block-cipher mode such as CBC or CTR is to:

options.A: Make the key longer
options.B: Ensure that identical plaintexts encrypt to different ciphertexts under the same key and to prevent certain attacks that arise from reuse
options.C: Replace the block cipher entirely

explanation: IVs/nonces provide semantic security under a fixed key when used correctly.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A security policy that requires two distinct individuals to authorize a critical action is an example of:

options.A: Least privilege only
options.B: Separation of duties (or dual control)
options.C: Complete mediation solely

explanation: Separation of duties reduces the risk that a single compromised or malicious actor can complete a sensitive operation.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: In TLS 1.3 the handshake was redesigned primarily to:

options.A: Increase the number of round trips
options.B: Reduce latency (1-RTT or 0-RTT), remove obsolete algorithms and improve privacy of the handshake
options.C: Eliminate all authentication
options.D: Use only static RSA key transport

explanation: TLS 1.3 simplifies the handshake, mandates modern AEAD ciphers and provides better forward secrecy.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A rootkit is malware that:

options.A: Only displays advertisements
options.B: Conceals its presence and the presence of other malicious components by subverting the operating system’s own reporting mechanisms
options.C: Is always easy to detect with a simple file scan
options.D: Exists only as a browser extension

explanation: Rootkits operate at a privilege level that allows them to hide from ordinary inspection tools.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The concept of ‘defence in depth’ advocates:

options.A: Relying on a single perfect security control
options.B: Layering multiple independent security mechanisms so that the failure of one does not lead to complete compromise
options.C: Removing all security controls to improve performance

explanation: Multiple overlapping layers increase the attacker’s cost and the defender’s chance of detection.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: A cryptographic hash function that is only collision-resistant but not pre-image resistant would still be unsuitable for:

options.A: Digital signatures that rely on the inability to find a pre-image of a given hash
options.B: Only checksums of public data
options.C: Nothing; collision resistance alone is always sufficient

explanation: Many applications (password hashing, commitment schemes, certain signature constructions) also require pre-image resistance.

topic: 3.4 Network Security, Cryptography
question: The fundamental reason that public-key cryptography is computationally more expensive than symmetric cryptography for bulk data is that:

options.A: Public-key operations rely on hard mathematical problems (modular exponentiation, elliptic-curve point multiplication, etc.) whose best algorithms are far slower than the substitutions and permutations of a block cipher
options.B: Symmetric ciphers cannot be implemented in hardware
options.C: Public-key algorithms use shorter keys
options.D: There is no difference in speed

explanation: Asymmetric operations are typically three to four orders of magnitude slower; hence hybrid systems use public-key methods only to protect symmetric session keys.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A system call is the mechanism by which:

options.A: A user process directly executes privileged hardware instructions without kernel involvement
options.B: A user process requests a service from the operating-system kernel, typically causing a controlled transition from user mode to kernel mode
options.C: The kernel permanently disables interrupts
options.D: Two user processes exchange data without any kernel mediation

explanation: System calls form the controlled interface between unprivileged user code and privileged kernel services.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The Process Control Block (PCB) is a kernel data structure that stores:

options.A: Only the executable code of the process
options.B: The essential state of a process (registers, program counter, memory-management information, open-file list, scheduling data, etc.) needed to suspend and later resume it
options.C: The entire contents of main memory

explanation: The PCB is the kernel’s permanent record of a process; context switches save and restore its contents.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A context switch occurs when:

options.A: A process terminates and never runs again
options.B: The CPU stops executing one process and begins executing another, saving the state of the outgoing process and loading the state of the incoming process
options.C: A page fault is never generated
options.D: The kernel disables all interrupts permanently

explanation: Context switching is the fundamental mechanism that multiplexes a single CPU among multiple processes.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a system that supports multithreading within a single process, the threads of that process typically share:

options.A: Nothing; each thread has a completely private address space
options.B: The same address space, open-file table and other process-level resources, while each thread has its own stack, registers and program counter
options.C: Only the program counter
options.D: Separate copies of the entire operating system

explanation: Threads are lightweight units of execution that share the process’s resources.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A page fault is raised when:

options.A: The referenced page is already resident in physical memory and the TLB hits
options.B: The MMU determines that the required virtual page is not currently mapped to a physical frame (or the access violates protection), forcing the OS to handle the missing page
options.C: A process terminates normally

explanation: Page faults are the hardware signal that demand-paging must bring a page into memory or handle a protection violation.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The kernel mode (or supervisor mode) of a processor is characterized by the ability to:

options.A: Execute only a restricted subset of instructions and to access only user memory
options.B: Execute privileged instructions and to access the entire address space, including kernel data structures
options.C: Never be interrupted
options.D: Run only one process for the lifetime of the machine

explanation: Privilege levels protect the kernel from untrusted user code.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A process in the blocked (or waiting) state is one that:

options.A: Is currently executing on a CPU
options.B: Is waiting for an event (I/O completion, lock acquisition, message arrival, etc.) and cannot proceed until that event occurs
options.C: Has been permanently terminated
options.D: Is ready to run but has not yet been created

explanation: Blocked processes do not compete for the CPU until the awaited event is signalled.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The dual-mode operation of a CPU (user mode vs. kernel mode) is fundamental to operating-system protection because:

options.A: It allows every user program to execute any instruction
options.B: It prevents user programs from executing privileged instructions or directly accessing kernel memory, forcing them to request services via system calls
options.C: It eliminates the need for any memory protection

explanation: Hardware mode bits enforce the boundary between trusted and untrusted code.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A zombie process is a process that:

options.A: Is still running and consuming CPU time
options.B: Has terminated but whose exit status has not yet been collected by its parent via a wait-family system call, so a residual PCB entry remains
options.C: Has never been scheduled
options.D: Is waiting for I/O in the blocked state

explanation: Zombies occupy a slot in the process table until the parent reaps them.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a demand-paging system the working set of a process is best described as:

options.A: The entire virtual address space of the process
options.B: The set of pages that the process has referenced in the most recent time window and that should therefore be kept resident for efficient execution
options.C: Only the pages that are currently dirty
options.D: The contents of the TLB alone

explanation: Working-set theory formalizes the locality that page-replacement algorithms attempt to capture.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A trap (or software interrupt) differs from a hardware interrupt in that a trap is:

options.A: Generated by an external device asynchronously
options.B: Caused by the execution of an instruction (system call, division by zero, page fault, etc.) and is therefore synchronous with the running program
options.C: Never handled by the kernel
options.D: Always of lower priority than any hardware interrupt

explanation: Traps are synchronous; hardware interrupts are asynchronous external events.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The primary purpose of the mode bit (or current privilege level) in a modern CPU is to:

options.A: Select the clock frequency
options.B: Indicate whether the processor is currently executing in user mode or kernel mode, thereby controlling which instructions and memory regions are accessible
options.C: Store the process ID of the running process
options.D: Count the number of page faults

explanation: The mode bit is the hardware foundation of dual-mode operation.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: When a process performs a blocking system call, the operating system typically:

options.A: Keeps the process in the running state and busy-waits
options.B: Moves the process to the blocked state, selects another ready process to run, and later moves the original process back to the ready state when the event completes
options.C: Terminates the process immediately
options.D: Disables all interrupts until the call finishes

explanation: Blocking I/O yields the CPU so that other work can proceed.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A process image (or address space) in a typical modern OS contains at least:

options.A: Only the executable code
options.B: Text (code), data, heap and stack segments, together with memory-mapping structures maintained by the kernel
options.C: Only the PCB

explanation: The classic layout comprises code, static data, dynamically allocated heap and the call stack.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The kernel is said to be non-preemptible (in a traditional monolithic design) when:

options.A: A user process can be switched out at any time
options.B: Once the CPU has entered kernel mode to handle a system call or interrupt, that kernel code runs to completion (or to a voluntary blocking point) before another process may be scheduled
options.C: Interrupts are never enabled
options.D: All processes run in kernel mode permanently

explanation: Classic Unix kernels were largely non-preemptible; modern kernels support kernel preemption.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A thread that is managed entirely by a user-level library without kernel awareness is called a:

options.A: Kernel thread
options.B: User-level thread (or green thread)
options.C: Process

explanation: User-level threads are scheduled by a library; the kernel sees only a single process.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The fork system call (in Unix-like systems) creates a new process by:

options.A: Loading a completely new program image immediately
options.B: Duplicating the calling process; the child receives a copy (often copy-on-write) of the parent’s address space and continues from the instruction after the fork
options.C: Terminating the parent
options.D: Creating only a new thread inside the same process

explanation: fork is the classic process-creation primitive; exec is used later to load a new image.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A ready queue (or run queue) in an operating system holds:

options.A: Processes that are waiting for I/O completion
options.B: Processes that are prepared to run and are waiting only for allocation of a CPU
options.C: Processes that have terminated

explanation: The scheduler selects the next process to run from the ready queue.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a system that uses pure demand paging, a newly created process:

options.A: Has all of its pages loaded into physical memory before it begins execution
options.B: Starts with no pages resident; pages are brought in only when they are first referenced, generating page faults
options.C: Never generates page faults
options.D: Is allocated a fixed set of frames that never change

explanation: Demand paging loads pages lazily on first reference.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The term ‘thrashing’ describes a situation in which:

options.A: A process spends most of its time executing useful instructions
options.B: The system spends an excessive fraction of time swapping pages in and out, so that useful CPU utilization drops dramatically
options.C: No page faults ever occur
options.D: All processes run in kernel mode

explanation: Thrashing occurs when the total working set of runnable processes exceeds available physical memory.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A process that has been swapped out to secondary storage is typically in which state?

options.A: Running
options.B: Ready or blocked, but its memory image resides on disk rather than in RAM
options.C: Terminated

explanation: Swapped processes retain their logical state but occupy no physical frames until swapped back in.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The exec family of system calls is used to:

options.A: Create a duplicate of the current process
options.B: Replace the current process’s memory image with a new program, retaining the same process ID
options.C: Terminate the process

explanation: exec loads a new executable into the already-existing process structure.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a multilevel feedback queue scheduler, a process that uses up its time quantum is typically:

options.A: Moved to a higher-priority queue
options.B: Moved to a lower-priority queue, giving preference to interactive or short jobs
options.C: Terminated
options.D: Left in the same queue forever

explanation: Feedback queues penalize CPU-bound jobs by demoting them, while I/O-bound jobs stay at higher priority.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A critical section is a portion of code that:

options.A: May be executed by any number of processes simultaneously without restriction
options.B: Accesses shared data and must be executed by at most one process (or thread) at a time to avoid race conditions
options.C: Is executed only by the idle process

explanation: Mutual exclusion for critical sections is the central problem of concurrent programming.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The idle process (or idle thread) in an operating system is scheduled when:

options.A: There are many ready processes competing for the CPU
options.B: No other runnable process exists; it typically executes a low-power wait or halt instruction
options.C: A page fault occurs

explanation: The idle process ensures the scheduler always has something to run and often enables power-saving modes.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A microkernel architecture differs from a monolithic kernel mainly in that:

options.A: All operating-system services run inside a single large kernel address space
options.B: Only a minimal set of functions (IPC, basic scheduling, low-level hardware control) run in privileged mode; most services run as user-level servers
options.C: There is no kernel at all
options.D: User processes execute privileged instructions directly

explanation: Microkernels push traditional kernel functionality into user-space servers for modularity and robustness.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The short-term scheduler (CPU scheduler) is responsible for:

options.A: Deciding which processes should be admitted into the system (long-term scheduling)
options.B: Selecting which ready process will next be allocated the CPU
options.C: Swapping processes between main memory and disk

explanation: Short-term scheduling is the frequent decision of which ready process runs next.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A race condition arises when:

options.A: Two processes never access shared data
options.B: The correctness of a concurrent program depends on the unpredictable interleaving of operations on shared state performed by multiple processes or threads
options.C: All processes run sequentially

explanation: Race conditions are the classic symptom of inadequate synchronization.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a system that uses copy-on-write after fork, a page is actually duplicated only when:

options.A: The child is created
options.B: Either the parent or the child attempts to write to a page that is still shared and marked read-only
options.C: The process terminates

explanation: Copy-on-write defers the cost of copying until a write actually occurs.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The long-term scheduler (job scheduler) controls:

options.A: Which ready process runs next on the CPU
options.B: The degree of multiprogramming by deciding which jobs are admitted into the system and become processes
options.C: Only the order of disk I/O requests
options.D: The mapping of virtual to physical addresses

explanation: Long-term scheduling regulates how many processes compete for memory and CPU.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A process that is CPU-bound spends most of its time:

options.A: Waiting for I/O operations to complete
options.B: Executing instructions on the processor
options.C: Blocked on a lock held by another process

explanation: CPU-bound processes have long CPU bursts relative to their I/O bursts.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The medium-term scheduler is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Selecting the next process to run on the CPU
options.B: Swapping processes into and out of main memory, thereby adjusting the degree of multiprogramming in response to memory pressure
options.C: Allocating file-system blocks

explanation: Medium-term scheduling manages the swap-in / swap-out decisions.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a pure user-level threading model, a blocking system call made by one thread typically:

options.A: Blocks only that thread while other user-level threads of the same process continue to run
options.B: Blocks the entire process because the kernel is unaware of the user-level threads
options.C: Has no effect on any thread

explanation: The kernel sees a single process; a blocking call suspends that process and therefore all of its user-level threads.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The purpose of a mode bit transition that occurs on a system call is to:

options.A: Increase the process’s priority permanently
options.B: Raise the processor’s privilege level so that the kernel can execute privileged instructions and access protected data structures on behalf of the user process
options.C: Disable the MMU
options.D: Clear the entire TLB without any other effect

explanation: The transition into kernel mode is the controlled entry point for privileged services.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A process’s state is completely defined by the contents of its:

options.A: Only the program counter
options.B: PCB together with the memory image that the PCB describes
options.C: Only the open-file table

explanation: The PCB plus the address-space contents capture everything needed to resume the process later.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: In a system that supports both processes and kernel threads, a context switch between two threads of different processes is generally more expensive than a switch between two threads of the same process because:

options.A: No address-space change is required for same-process threads
options.B: Different processes possess distinct address spaces, so the memory-management hardware (page tables, ASID/TLB) must be switched as well
options.C: Threads never share any resources

explanation: Cross-process switches incur TLB flushes or ASID changes and page-table base-register reloads.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A signal in a Unix-like operating system is a limited form of:

options.A: A system call that always blocks
options.B: Software interrupt that can be sent to a process to notify it of an event (or to force it to terminate, stop, continue, etc.)
options.C: A page-fault handler only

explanation: Signals provide asynchronous notification and control of processes.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: The degree of multiprogramming is defined as:

options.A: The number of CPUs in the system
options.B: The number of processes that reside in main memory and therefore compete for the CPU
options.C: The size of the ready queue only

explanation: Higher multiprogramming improves utilization but increases memory pressure.

topic: 4.1 Operating System Fundamentals
question: A kernel thread is a thread that:

options.A: Is invisible to the kernel and is scheduled only by a user-level library
options.B: Is a schedulable entity known to and managed by the kernel; the kernel can run different kernel threads of the same process concurrently on multiple CPUs
options.C: Cannot be blocked independently
options.D: Exists only inside the idle process
