options.B: Regularly (table-top exercises, functional tests, full interruption tests) so that deficiencies are discovered before a real disaster occurs
options.C: Never, because testing is too disruptive
options.D: Only after a real disaster has already happened

explanation: Untested plans frequently fail; regular exercises keep the plan and the team ready.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) or maximum acceptable outage (MAO) is:

options.A: Always shorter than the RTO
options.B: The absolute limit beyond which the organisation’s survival or mission is threatened; RTO must be set well inside this limit
options.C: Identical to the RPO
options.D: The time required to perform a differential backup

explanation: MTD/MAO is a business-derived ceiling; RTO is the operational target that must fit under it.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A backup that is stored on a different media type (e.g., disk-to-tape) and transported to an off-site vault is an example of satisfying which part of the 3-2-1 rule?

options.A: Only the “3” (three copies)
options.B: Both the “2” (two media types) and the “1” (one off-site copy)
options.C: None of the rule’s requirements
options.D: Only the requirement for daily full backups

explanation: Different media plus geographic separation addresses two of the three legs of the rule.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a multi-site active-active architecture:

options.A: Only one site processes production traffic; the other is pure standby
options.B: Two or more sites simultaneously serve production traffic and can absorb the load of a failed site, typically providing the lowest RTOs at the highest cost and complexity
options.C: No data replication occurs between sites
options.D: Both sites are cold and require manual hardware installation after a disaster

explanation: Active-active designs eliminate the notion of a passive standby, but demand continuous synchronisation and traffic-management logic.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A recovery-time actual (RTA) that consistently exceeds the documented RTO indicates that:

options.A: The DR plan is performing better than required
options.B: The organisation is missing its recovery objective and must improve procedures, technology or both
options.C: RPO is the only metric that matters

explanation: RTA is the measured result; persistent breaches of RTO require corrective action.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: Snapshot-based backup technologies typically provide:

options.A: A full bit-for-bit copy of every changed block with no relationship to prior snapshots
options.B: Point-in-time, space-efficient images of a volume that can be created rapidly and used for near-instant recovery or as the source of subsequent backups
options.C: Only tape-based sequential archives
options.D: No ability to restore individual files

explanation: Snapshots (especially copy-on-write or redirect-on-write) enable low-RPO, low-impact recovery points.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A single point of failure (SPOF) in a DR architecture is:

options.A: A component whose failure can be tolerated without any service impact
options.B: A component whose failure would cause the entire recovery capability (or the production service) to become unavailable
options.C: Always a desirable design feature

explanation: Eliminating SPOFs is a primary goal of resilient design.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a classic tape-rotation scheme such as Grandfather-Father-Son, the “grandfather” tapes typically represent:

options.A: The most recent incremental backups
options.B: The oldest retained full backups, kept for long-term archival purposes
options.C: Only the daily differential sets
options.D: Backups that are never taken off-site

explanation: The scheme provides a hierarchy of retention periods: daily (son), weekly (father), monthly/yearly (grandfather).

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A failover test that deliberately powers off the primary site and attempts to run production from the secondary site is classified as:

options.A: A table-top exercise only
options.B: A full-interruption (or full-scale) test
options.C: A pure documentation review
options.D: An optional activity that never needs to be performed

explanation: Full-interruption tests are the most realistic and the most risky; they validate the entire recovery path.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The term “RPO = 0” implies that:

options.A: Some data loss is always acceptable
options.B: No committed data may be lost; the recovery point must be identical to the moment of failure (typically requiring synchronous replication or equivalent)
options.C: The system may be down for an unlimited time
options.D: Only weekly full backups are needed

explanation: Zero RPO is the strongest data-loss requirement and is expensive to achieve over distance.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A backup repository that supports immutability (WORM or object-lock) is especially valuable against:

options.A: Ordinary hardware failure only
options.B: Ransomware that attempts to encrypt or delete the organisation’s own backups
options.C: Network congestion
options.D: The need for any off-site copy

explanation: Immutable backups cannot be altered or erased by an attacker who has compromised production credentials.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a cloud context, a multi-region deployment that keeps a standby environment in a second region is most closely analogous to a traditional:

options.A: Cold site that requires hardware purchase after disaster
options.B: Warm or hot site, depending on how much of the stack is kept running and how current the data are
options.C: Single on-premises data centre with no redundancy

explanation: Cloud regions function as geographically separated sites; the degree of readiness determines hot versus warm behaviour.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A recovery-point actual (RPA) that is larger than the stated RPO means that:

options.A: The organisation recovered more data than required
options.B: More data were lost than the business had declared acceptable; the protection scheme failed to meet its objective
options.C: RTO was automatically satisfied

explanation: RPA is the measured data-loss interval; exceeding RPO is a missed objective.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The primary purpose of an off-site backup vault is to:

options.A: Provide a second copy of data that survives a disaster affecting the primary site (fire, flood, regional outage, etc.)
options.B: Increase the speed of local restores only
options.C: Replace the need for any on-site backup
options.D: Store only obsolete data that will never be needed

explanation: Geographic separation is the classic defence against site-level disasters.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A “bare-metal restore” capability allows an organisation to:

options.A: Recover only individual user files
options.B: Rebuild an entire system (operating system, applications, configuration and data) onto dissimilar or new hardware from a backup image
options.C: Restore data only to the original physical machine with identical disks
options.D: Avoid the need for any recovery documentation

explanation: Bare-metal recovery is essential when the original hardware is destroyed or unavailable.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a DR context the term “failback” refers to:

options.A: The initial move of production from the primary site to the recovery site
options.B: The planned return of production operations from the recovery site back to the restored primary site once it is ready
options.C: The permanent abandonment of the primary site
options.D: A pure test that never affects production

explanation: Failback completes the recovery cycle by restoring normal operations at the original location.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A network-attached storage (NAS) device used for backup is most vulnerable as a single point of failure when:

options.A: It is replicated to a second NAS in another building and both are monitored
options.B: It is the sole repository for all backups and is located in the same facility as the production systems it protects
options.C: It stores only non-critical archival data
options.D: It is offline and powered off at all times

explanation: Co-locating the only backup copy with production defeats the purpose of protection against site disasters.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The frequency of backups is driven primarily by:

options.A: The colour of the backup media
options.B: The organisation’s RPO: more frequent backups (or continuous replication) are required when less data loss is tolerable
options.C: The RTO alone, independent of data-loss tolerance
options.D: A fixed regulatory requirement that every organisation must back up once per year

explanation: RPO sets the maximum gap between the last good copy and the moment of failure.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A disaster-recovery site that is kept in a “pilot-light” state will typically incur:

options.A: The same running cost as a fully scaled hot site
options.B: Lower continuous cost than a hot site, while still permitting relatively rapid scale-out when needed
options.C: Zero cost because no resources are reserved
options.D: Higher cost than an active-active multi-region deployment

explanation: Pilot-light keeps only the critical core running; additional capacity is started on demand.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a synchronous replication topology the primary factor that limits geographic distance is:

options.A: The colour of the fibre optic cable
options.B: The propagation delay (latency) that the application can tolerate while waiting for the remote write acknowledgement
options.C: The number of backup tapes available
options.D: The version of the operating system only

explanation: Speed-of-light delay makes true synchronous replication impractical beyond a few tens or hundreds of kilometres for latency-sensitive applications.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A table-top DR exercise is characterised by:

options.A: Actually failing over production systems to the recovery site
options.B: A discussion-based walkthrough of the recovery procedures by the responsible personnel, without touching live systems
options.C: A full restoration of every database from tape
options.D: The permanent decommissioning of the primary site

explanation: Table-top exercises are low-risk, low-cost ways to validate understanding and uncover procedural gaps.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The combination of a low RTO and a low RPO generally implies:

options.A: Infrequent tape backups and a cold site
options.B: Continuous or near-continuous replication to a hot (or warm) site, with automated or rapidly executable failover procedures
options.C: No need for any secondary site
options.D: Reliance solely on monthly full backups

explanation: Stringent objectives demand both frequent (or continuous) data protection and a ready-to-run recovery environment.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A backup set that has been encrypted and whose encryption keys are stored only at the primary site creates a risk that:

options.A: The backups are automatically more secure in all circumstances
options.B: After a site disaster the organisation may possess the encrypted data but be unable to decrypt them, rendering the backups useless
options.C: Encryption is never useful for backups

explanation: Key management must itself be resilient; keys or key-recovery material must be available at the recovery site.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In an active-passive DR configuration the passive site:

options.A: Simultaneously processes an equal share of production traffic
options.B: Remains on standby (with data replication) until a failover decision brings it into production service
options.C: Contains no data and no compute resources
options.D: Is used only for development and never for recovery

explanation: Active-passive keeps a ready standby that is activated when the primary fails.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A recovery procedure that has never been tested is best regarded as:

options.A: Guaranteed to work under all conditions
options.B: An unverified assumption that may contain fatal gaps; testing is required to convert documentation into a reliable capability
options.C: Sufficient for regulatory compliance in every jurisdiction
options.D: More reliable than a regularly tested procedure

explanation: Experience shows that untested plans frequently fail when first exercised under pressure.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The term “journal” or “change log” in a continuous-replication system refers to:

options.A: A pure paper record of administrator actions
options.B: A sequential record of data modifications that is shipped to the secondary site and applied to keep the replica current
options.C: The list of all full backups ever taken
options.D: A configuration file that is never updated

explanation: Journals (or transaction logs, write-ahead logs, etc.) are the vehicle for efficient, ordered replication.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A DR site located in the same seismic or flood zone as the primary site fails to provide protection against:

options.A: A single disk failure inside one server
options.B: A regional natural disaster that affects both locations simultaneously
options.C: A software bug that can be fixed by a patch

explanation: Geographic diversity must take into account correlated risks such as earthquakes, hurricanes and large-scale power events.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a backup strategy that alternates full and incremental backups, the restore sequence for a given day typically requires:

options.A: Only the most recent incremental backup
options.B: The last full backup plus every incremental backup taken after that full backup up to the desired recovery point
options.C: Only the first full backup ever taken

explanation: Incremental chains are cumulative; missing any link in the chain prevents a complete restore.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A service-level agreement (SLA) for a cloud DR service that quotes an RTO of 4 hours means that:

options.A: The provider guarantees that data loss will never exceed 4 hours
options.B: The provider commits to restoring the covered service to a usable state within 4 hours after a declared disaster (subject to the precise contractual definitions)
options.C: Backups are taken only every 4 hours
options.D: The service is unavailable for exactly 4 hours every day

explanation: RTO in an SLA is a contractual recovery-time commitment; RPO would be a separate data-loss commitment.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The practice of storing backup media in a fireproof, waterproof safe that remains inside the primary data centre protects against:

options.A: A complete site disaster such as a building fire or regional flood that destroys the safe along with the facility
options.B: Localised risks such as a small fire or sprinkler activation inside the data centre, but not against total site loss
options.C: All possible disasters without any need for off-site copies

explanation: On-site protective storage is valuable but insufficient for true site-level disasters; off-site copies remain essential.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A “dependency map” or “application dependency diagram” is critical in DR planning because:

options.A: It is required only for software licensing audits
options.B: It reveals the order in which systems must be recovered and the external services they rely upon, preventing incomplete or out-of-sequence restores
options.C: It replaces the need for any RTO or RPO targets
options.D: It is used solely for network bandwidth calculations

explanation: Modern applications form complex webs of dependencies; recovering a leaf system before its dependencies yields a non-functional service.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: In a replication topology the term “last-mile” or “split-brain” risk refers to:

options.A: The possibility that both sites believe they are primary after a network partition, potentially leading to divergent data sets
options.B: The cost of the final network hop to the end user
options.C: The time required to perform a full backup
options.D: A pure hardware failure of a single disk

explanation: Split-brain is a classic distributed-systems hazard that quorum or fencing mechanisms are designed to prevent.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: A graduated recovery approach that restores the most critical services first, then progressively less critical ones, is driven by:

options.A: A random ordering of systems
options.B: The prioritisation established in the business impact analysis and the associated RTO tiers
options.C: The alphabetical order of server names
options.D: The preference of the on-call technician alone

explanation: BIA-derived criticality tiers determine the sequence and resource allocation of recovery.

topic: 7.1 Disaster Recovery
question: The fundamental reason that a documented, tested disaster-recovery capability is required even when an organisation already possesses high-availability clusters inside a single data centre is that:

options.A: High availability inside one site already protects against every conceivable disaster
options.B: Site-level disasters (fire, flood, regional power loss, large-scale network failure, etc.) can overcome local HA mechanisms; only a geographically separated, recoverable capability addresses those risks
options.C: HA clusters never fail
options.D: Documentation is required only for insurance purposes and has no operational value

explanation: HA and DR are complementary: HA masks component failures within a site; DR survives the loss of the entire site.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) grants permissions according to:

options.A: The individual identity of each user without any grouping
options.B: The role (job function) assigned to a user; users acquire permissions only through the roles they hold
options.C: The physical location of the user’s workstation only
options.D: A purely discretionary decision made by the resource owner for every request

explanation: RBAC associates permissions with roles and users with roles, simplifying administration and supporting least privilege.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A phishing attack is best described as:

options.A: A purely technical exploit of a buffer overflow
options.B: A social-engineering technique that attempts to obtain sensitive information by masquerading as a trustworthy entity, typically via email or messaging
options.C: A denial-of-service flood of network packets
options.D: An insider’s accidental deletion of files

explanation: Phishing relies on deception rather than pure technical vulnerability exploitation.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) is characterised by the property that:

options.A: Resource owners may freely grant or revoke access to any other user
options.B: Access decisions are enforced by the system according to security labels (classifications and clearances) that ordinary users cannot override
options.C: No access controls exist at all
options.D: Permissions are derived solely from group membership decided by users

explanation: MAC is the model used in high-assurance systems (e.g., SELinux, military multilevel security); users cannot alter the policy.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A ransomware attack typically aims to:

options.A: Steal credentials and remain undetected indefinitely
options.B: Encrypt the victim’s data and demand payment (usually in cryptocurrency) for the decryption key
options.C: Only display unwanted advertisements
options.D: Improve the performance of the victim’s system

explanation: Ransomware is a form of malware whose business model is extortion via encryption.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) requires a user to present:

options.A: Only a password
options.B: At least two independent authentication factors from different categories (something you know, something you have, something you are)
options.C: Only a biometric sample
options.D: A single shared secret known to the entire organisation

explanation: MFA dramatically raises the cost of credential-based attacks by combining independent factors.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack is successful when the attacker:

options.A: Only reads publicly available documentation
options.B: Positions himself between two communicating parties so that he can intercept, and possibly alter, the traffic while both parties believe they are talking directly to each other
options.C: Sends a single malformed packet that crashes a server
options.D: Guesses a password by pure brute force without any network position

explanation: MitM attacks exploit the lack of authenticated, encrypted channels or the compromise of trust anchors.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Discretionary Access Control (DAC) is characterised by:

options.A: System-enforced labels that users cannot change
options.B: The ability of a resource owner (or a process acting on the owner’s behalf) to decide who else may access the resource
options.C: A pure role hierarchy with no individual ownership
options.D: The complete absence of any access decisions

explanation: Classic Unix file permissions are a form of DAC; the owner can chmod and chown.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A zero-day exploit is one that:

options.A: Targets a vulnerability for which a patch has been publicly available for years
options.B: Targets a vulnerability that is unknown to the vendor (and therefore has no available patch) at the time of the attack
options.C: Can never succeed against a properly configured firewall
options.D: Requires physical access to the target hardware in every case

explanation: “Zero-day” refers to the absence of prior public knowledge and of a vendor fix.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Spear phishing differs from ordinary phishing in that it:

options.A: Uses only generic messages sent to millions of addresses
options.B: Is carefully targeted at a specific individual or organisation, often incorporating personal or contextual information to increase credibility
options.C: Never involves email
options.D: Is exclusively a form of denial-of-service

explanation: Spear phishing is personalised; whaling is spear phishing aimed at high-value executives.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A principle of least privilege requires that:

options.A: Every user and process be given the maximum possible rights “just in case”
options.B: A subject be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform its authorised tasks, and for the minimum time required
options.C: All users share a single administrator account
options.D: Permissions never be reviewed after initial assignment

explanation: Least privilege limits the damage that can result from error, compromise or insider misuse.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A rootkit is malware that:

options.A: Only displays advertisements on web pages
options.B: Conceals its presence (and often the presence of other malicious components) by subverting the operating system’s own reporting and inspection mechanisms
options.C: Is always easy to detect with a simple file-name scan
options.D: Exists only as a browser extension and never touches the kernel

explanation: Rootkits operate at a privilege level that allows them to hide from ordinary tools.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Defence in depth advocates:

options.A: Relying on a single perfect security control
options.B: Layering multiple independent security mechanisms so that the failure of one does not lead to complete compromise
options.C: Removing all security controls to improve performance
options.D: Using only physical locks and no technical controls

explanation: Multiple overlapping layers increase an attacker’s cost and the defender’s chance of detection.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A SQL-injection vulnerability arises when:

options.A: All user input is properly parameterised or escaped before being placed in a query
options.B: An application concatenates unsanitised user input directly into a SQL statement, allowing the attacker to alter the query’s logic
options.C: The database is offline
options.D: HTTPS is used for the connection

explanation: Injection occurs when data are treated as code; prepared statements prevent it.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Cross-site scripting (XSS) is an attack that:

options.A: Exploits a buffer overflow in the operating-system kernel
options.B: Injects malicious script into a web page that is then executed in the browsers of other users who view that page
options.C: Floods a network with ICMP packets
options.D: Cracks a symmetric key by brute force

explanation: XSS abuses the trust a browser places in content received from a legitimate origin.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A botnet is a collection of:

options.A: Legitimate, well-administered servers under a single administrative domain
options.B: Compromised devices (bots) that are remotely controlled by an attacker and can be used for distributed attacks, spam or other malicious activity
options.C: Only physical network switches
options.D: Air-gapped machines that can never communicate

explanation: Botnets are the infrastructure behind many large-scale DDoS, spam and credential-stuffing campaigns.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The CIA triad of information security consists of:

options.A: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
options.B: Cryptography, Integrity, Authentication
options.C: Confidentiality, Identity, Authorisation

explanation: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability are the three classic security objectives.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A buffer-overflow attack typically exploits:

options.A: A correctly bounds-checked input routine
options.B: A programming error that allows more data to be written into a fixed-size buffer than it can hold, potentially overwriting adjacent control data such as return addresses
options.C: The absence of any network connection
options.D: A correctly configured firewall that drops all packets

explanation: Classic stack- or heap-based overflows let an attacker seize control of program execution.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes authorisation decisions on the basis of:

options.A: Only the user’s role name
options.B: Attributes of the subject, the resource, the action and the environment, evaluated against policies
options.C: A pure identity list with no additional context

explanation: ABAC is a flexible, policy-driven model that can express fine-grained, context-aware rules.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A Trojan horse is malware that:

options.A: Self-replicates by attaching to other files or by exploiting network services
options.B: Masquerades as a legitimate program while performing hidden malicious actions
options.C: Is always a pure denial-of-service tool with no payload
options.D: Requires no user interaction and spreads solely by network worms

explanation: Trojans rely on social engineering or deception to be executed; they do not self-propagate like worms.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A security policy that requires two distinct individuals to authorise a critical action implements:

options.A: Least privilege only
options.B: Separation of duties (or dual control)
options.C: Complete mediation solely

explanation: Separation of duties reduces the risk that a single compromised or malicious actor can complete a sensitive operation.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attack is characterised by:

options.A: A single source sending a modest volume of traffic
options.B: A large number of coordinated sources overwhelming a target’s bandwidth, CPU or application resources so that legitimate users cannot be served
options.C: An insider quietly copying confidential files

explanation: The distributed nature makes simple IP blocking ineffective and amplifies the volume of traffic.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The principle of complete mediation requires that:

options.A: Access checks be performed only at login time and never again
options.B: Every access to every object be checked against the current access-control policy, with no reliance on cached decisions that may have become stale
options.C: No access checks ever be performed
options.D: Only the first access in a session be verified

explanation: Complete mediation is one of Saltzer and Schroeder’s classic design principles.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A watering-hole attack is one in which the attacker:

options.A: Sends generic phishing email to millions of addresses
options.B: Compromises a website that is known to be frequented by the target group, so that visitors’ browsers or plugins are exploited
options.C: Only performs a physical break-in
options.D: Relies solely on guessing weak passwords

explanation: Watering-hole attacks exploit the trust users place in sites they regularly visit.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: In the context of authentication, a “something you are” factor refers to:

options.A: A password or PIN
options.B: A physical token or smart card
options.C: A biometric characteristic (fingerprint, iris, face, etc.)
options.D: A one-time code sent by SMS

explanation: The three classic factors are knowledge, possession and inherence (biometrics).

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A polymorphic virus is characterised by:

options.A: Always having exactly the same binary representation on disk
options.B: Changing its appearance (encryption, code rearrangement, etc.) on each infection while preserving its functional payload, thereby complicating signature-based detection
options.C: Never replicating

explanation: Polymorphism is a classic evasion technique against static antivirus signatures.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The security property of non-repudiation ensures that:

options.A: A message remains confidential from all third parties
options.B: A party that performed an action (e.g., signed a document or sent a message) cannot later convincingly deny having done so
options.C: A system is always available
options.D: Data are never modified in transit

explanation: Non-repudiation is typically achieved with digital signatures and trusted time-stamping.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A privilege-escalation attack aims to:

options.A: Reduce a user’s rights to the minimum necessary
options.B: Obtain higher privileges than those originally granted to the attacker’s account or process (e.g., from ordinary user to administrator or SYSTEM)
options.C: Only read public documentation
options.D: Improve the performance of the target system

explanation: Vertical privilege escalation moves to a more powerful role; horizontal escalation assumes another user’s identity at the same level.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A security audit log that records failed login attempts is primarily useful for:

options.A: Improving the graphical appearance of the login page
options.B: Detecting brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks and supporting forensic investigation after an incident
options.C: Automatically granting administrator rights to any user who fails three times
options.D: Replacing the need for any password policy

explanation: Logs are a cornerstone of detection, response and accountability.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A drive-by download attack typically occurs when:

options.A: A user deliberately installs software from a trusted vendor
options.B: A user merely visits a compromised or malicious web page and malware is installed without further interaction, often via an exploit of the browser or a plugin
options.C: A user inserts a USB stick that has been scanned and found clean
options.D: An administrator applies a signed operating-system patch

explanation: Drive-by downloads exploit client-side vulnerabilities; no explicit “download and run” step is required of the user.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The principle of fail-safe defaults states that:

options.A: Access should be allowed unless explicitly denied
options.B: Access should be denied unless explicitly granted; the default posture is restrictive
options.C: All permissions should be granted at system start-up
options.D: Security controls should be disabled when an error occurs

explanation: Fail-safe defaults are another of Saltzer and Schroeder’s fundamental design principles.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A side-channel attack extracts secret information by observing:

options.A: Only the mathematical description of the algorithm
options.B: Physical phenomena such as timing, power consumption, electromagnetic radiation or acoustic emanations that depend on the secret data
options.C: Only the ciphertext produced by a perfect implementation

explanation: Side channels exploit implementation characteristics rather than pure mathematical weaknesses.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A honeypot is a security mechanism whose primary purpose is to:

options.A: Replace the production firewall
options.B: Attract and observe attackers in a controlled environment so that their techniques can be studied and production systems better protected
options.C: Store all user passwords in cleartext

explanation: Honeypots are decoy systems that yield intelligence about adversary behaviour.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: Whaling is a form of social engineering that specifically targets:

options.A: Ordinary end users with generic messages
options.B: High-value individuals such as executives or senior officials, using highly personalised and often elaborate pretexts
options.C: Only automated systems with no human interaction
options.D: Public web servers with SQL injection

explanation: Whaling is spear phishing aimed at “big fish”.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A security control that prevents an action from occurring (as opposed to detecting it after the fact) is classified as:

options.A: A detective control
options.B: A preventive (or preventative) control
options.C: A corrective control only

explanation: Preventive, detective and corrective (or recovery) are the three classic temporal categories of controls.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A session-fixation attack aims to:

options.A: Force a user to choose a weak password
options.B: Cause a victim to adopt a session identifier that is already known to the attacker, so that after the victim authenticates the attacker can hijack the authenticated session
options.C: Encrypt all traffic with a weak cipher

explanation: Session fixation is prevented by regenerating the session identifier upon successful authentication.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The concept of an “air gap” in security architecture means that:

options.A: Two networks are connected by a high-speed fibre link
options.B: A system or network is physically isolated from other networks (especially the Internet), so that electronic data transfer is possible only by controlled, manual means
options.C: All systems share a single broadcast domain
options.D: Encryption is disabled to improve performance

explanation: Air-gapped systems are used for the highest-security environments, though they are not immune to all attack vectors (e.g., supply-chain or insider threats).

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A credential-stuffing attack exploits:

options.A: A novel zero-day vulnerability in the login form
options.B: The reuse of username/password pairs that have been leaked from other breaches; the attacker automates login attempts against many sites with those credentials
options.C: A pure physical theft of a hardware token
options.D: A misconfigured firewall rule that allows all traffic

explanation: Credential stuffing is a large-scale, automated form of credential reuse; MFA and breach monitoring are key defences.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: In a multilevel security system that implements the Bell–LaPadula model, the “no-read-up” rule states that:

options.A: A subject may read any object regardless of classification
options.B: A subject may not read an object whose security level is higher than the subject’s clearance
options.C: A subject may write to any higher level
options.D: There are no restrictions on reading

explanation: Simple Security Property (no-read-up) and the *-property (no-write-down) protect confidentiality.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A security information and event management (SIEM) system is primarily used to:

options.A: Replace the need for any firewalls
options.B: Aggregate, correlate and analyse security logs and events from many sources so that incidents can be detected and investigated
options.C: Store only user passwords in cleartext
options.D: Perform only vulnerability scanning of web applications

explanation: SIEMs provide centralised visibility and alerting across the enterprise.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A supply-chain attack targets:

options.A: Only the final end-user of a software product
options.B: An intermediate link (vendor, library, update mechanism, hardware manufacturer, etc.) so that the compromise is inherited by downstream customers
options.C: Only the physical locks on a data-centre door
options.D: A single misconfigured open port on a public server

explanation: Supply-chain compromises (e.g., tainted updates or malicious dependencies) can affect thousands of organisations at once.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The principle of open design (or “no security through obscurity”) asserts that:

options.A: The security of a system should rely on the secrecy of its design and source code
options.B: The design of a security mechanism should not be secret; security should depend only on the secrecy of keys or passwords, so that the mechanism can be scrutinised and improved
options.C: All source code must be kept permanently confidential
options.D: Cryptographic algorithms should never be published

explanation: Open design is a classic Saltzer-and-Schroeder principle; modern cryptography relies on it.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A business email compromise (BEC) attack typically involves:

options.A: A purely technical buffer-overflow exploit of the mail server
options.B: Social engineering (often impersonation of an executive or trusted partner) to persuade an employee to transfer funds or disclose sensitive information
options.C: A DDoS flood against the organisation’s website
options.D: The installation of a rootkit on every workstation

explanation: BEC is a high-value form of social engineering that has caused multi-million-dollar losses.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A vulnerability scanner is a tool that:

options.A: Actively exploits every discovered weakness to demonstrate impact
options.B: Probes systems for known security weaknesses (missing patches, misconfigurations, default credentials, etc.) and reports them for remediation
options.C: Replaces the need for any penetration testing

explanation: Scanners identify potential problems; exploitation is left to penetration tests or attackers.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: In the context of malware, a worm is distinguished from a virus by the fact that a worm:

options.A: Requires a host file and user action to propagate
options.B: Self-propagates across networks by exploiting vulnerabilities or weak configurations, without needing to attach to a host file or rely on user interaction
options.C: Is always a pure Trojan with no replication capability
options.D: Exists only as a boot-sector infection on removable media

explanation: Worms are standalone, self-replicating network programs; viruses need a host and usually user action.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A false positive in an intrusion-detection system is:

options.A: A genuine attack that the system correctly reports
options.B: An alert raised for benign activity that is incorrectly classified as malicious, consuming analyst time and potentially leading to alert fatigue
options.C: A complete failure to detect any attack

explanation: High false-positive rates degrade the usefulness of detection systems.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The practice of “patch management” is essential because:

options.A: Patches never fix security vulnerabilities
options.B: Vendors regularly release fixes for discovered vulnerabilities; timely application of those fixes closes the window of exposure to known exploits
options.C: Unpatched systems are always more secure
options.D: Patches are required only for cosmetic user-interface changes

explanation: Unpatched known vulnerabilities remain one of the most common routes to successful compromise.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A security control that restores a system to a secure state after an incident (for example, restoring from a clean backup) is classified as:

options.A: A preventive control
options.B: A detective control
options.C: A corrective (or recovery) control

explanation: Corrective controls remediate the effects of an incident that has already occurred.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: In a zero-trust security model the fundamental assumption is that:

options.A: Everything inside the organisational network can be implicitly trusted
options.B: No user or device is trusted by default, whether inside or outside the network perimeter; every access request must be authenticated, authorised and continuously validated
options.C: Firewalls are unnecessary

explanation: Zero trust replaces perimeter-centric trust with continuous, explicit verification.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: A race-condition vulnerability in concurrent software can be exploited when:

options.A: All shared resources are properly protected by locks or other synchronisation
options.B: The correctness of a security check depends on a temporal sequence of operations that an attacker can interleave, causing the check to pass while the subsequent use of a resource occurs under different conditions
options.C: The program is single-threaded and never accesses shared state
options.D: The operating system disables all interrupts permanently

explanation: Time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) races are a classic example of this class of flaw.

topic: 8.1 Cybersecurity
question: The fundamental reason that cybersecurity is treated as a continuous process rather than a one-time project is that:

options.A: Threats, vulnerabilities, technologies and business requirements constantly evolve; static defences become obsolete
options.B: Once a firewall is installed no further attention is ever required
options.C: Attackers never change their methods
options.D: Compliance frameworks never update their requirements

explanation: Security is a moving target; continuous monitoring, improvement and adaptation are essential.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Nepal’s National Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Policy, 2072 (2015) was issued by which ministry?

options.A: Ministry of Finance
options.B: Ministry of Information and Communication (now Ministry of Communication and Information Technology)
options.C: Ministry of Education

explanation: The ICT Policy 2072 was promulgated by the then Ministry of Information and Communication as the overarching national ICT policy framework.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, commercial banks are required to conduct Information System (IS) audits:

options.A: Only once at the time of licence issuance
options.B: Periodically (typically annually) to ensure the effectiveness of the control framework and the adequacy of the security plan
options.C: Only when a major fraud has already occurred

explanation: The Guidelines mandate periodic (commonly understood as annual) IS audits; external experts may be engaged if internal capacity is insufficient.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The NRB Cyber Resilience Guidelines, 2023 were issued pursuant to which policy commitment?

options.A: A purely voluntary industry code of conduct
options.B: NRB’s Monetary Policy of FY 2022/23 (policy number 128) stating that a Cyber and Information Security Guideline would be issued for institutions licensed to carry out payment-related transactions
options.C: An international treaty that Nepal has not ratified

explanation: The Guidelines explicitly reference Monetary Policy 2022/23 policy number 128 as their mandate.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, a bank’s Disaster Recovery Planning (DRP) and Business Continuity Planning (BCP) are expected to achieve:

options.A: Unlimited downtime after any incident
options.B: An efficient, effective and economic “fail-safe” system with minimum downtime, covering both natural and man-made disasters as well as security threats
options.C: No recovery capability at all

explanation: The Guidelines require board-approved BCP/DRP that prioritises critical functions and minimises downtime.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023 apply to:

options.A: Only government ministries
options.B: Licensed institutions under the Payment Systems Department, including Class A/B/C/D BFIs as well as Payment System Operators (PSOs) and Payment Service Providers (PSPs)
options.C: Only foreign banks operating outside Nepal

explanation: The Guidelines explicitly cover BFIs and payment-system entities supervised by NRB’s Payment Systems Department.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, electronic attacks and suspected electronic attacks must be:

options.A: Ignored if no financial loss is immediately visible
options.B: Identified, documented and reported to Nepal Rastra Bank (typically on a monthly basis)
options.C: Reported only to the bank’s own board and never to the regulator
options.D: Disclosed only in the annual report three years later

explanation: Fraud-management provisions require documentation and periodic reporting of electronic attacks to NRB.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The five core risk-management categories emphasised by the Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023 are:

options.A: Only Encryption and Firewalls
options.B: Governance, Identification, Protection, Detection, and Response & Recovery
options.C: Only Audit and Compliance
options.D: Marketing, Sales, HR, Finance and Legal

explanation: These five categories, together with the overarching components of Testing, Situational Awareness and Learning & Evolving, structure the entire guideline.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the Cyber Resilience Guidelines, the ultimate responsibility for cyber-risk management rests with:

options.A: Only the IT help-desk staff
options.B: The Board of Directors of the licensed institution, which must set risk tolerance, approve the cyber-resilience strategy and define roles and responsibilities
options.C: Only external consultants

explanation: Board-level accountability is a central governance requirement of the Guidelines.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The NRB IT Guidelines require that an Action Plan for implementation of the Guidelines be submitted to the Bank Supervision Department within:

options.A: Ten years of issuance
options.B: Six months of issuance
options.C: Only after a major incident has occurred

explanation: Banks were required to submit a time-bound Action Plan within six months and to achieve full compliance within two years of issuance.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the Cyber Resilience Guidelines the target objective for resumption of critical business operations after a cyber incident is stated as:

options.A: Thirty days
options.B: Two hours (as a target objective for safe and practicable resumption, possibly in reduced capacity)
options.C: One calendar year

explanation: The Guidelines set a two-hour resumption target for critical operations once it is safe and practicable to do so.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Which of the following is a key thematic area explicitly addressed by the ICT Policy 2072?

options.A: Only the regulation of foreign exchange
options.B: Human-resource development, ICT in education, e-governance, telecommunications infrastructure, ICT for agriculture, and access for rural/remote areas and persons with disabilities
options.C: Only the licensing of commercial banks
options.D: Only the setting of interest rates

explanation: The Policy covers a broad spectrum of ICT development themes ranging from human capital to sectoral applications and inclusive access.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, if a bank lacks sufficient internal expertise to conduct an IS audit it may:

options.A: Skip the audit entirely
options.B: Outsource the audit to an external professional provider, while the bank’s audit committee retains responsibility for planning, risk assessment and follow-up
options.C: Appoint any staff member regardless of competence
options.D: Rely solely on the vendor of the core banking system

explanation: Outsourcing is permitted provided the bank retains ultimate responsibility and the provider is competent.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines emphasise the establishment of continuous monitoring capability, which may be realised through:

options.A: A purely manual paper log reviewed once a year
options.B: A Security Operations Centre (SOC), Network Operations Centre or equivalent that collects, centralises and correlates event information from multiple sources
options.C: No monitoring at all
options.D: Only the physical security guards at the data-centre door

explanation: Continuous monitoring via SOC/SIEM-type capabilities is a core Detection requirement.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, a bank’s IT Governance framework is expected to ensure that IT resources are used in a manner that is:

options.A: Efficient, effective and economic, so that business requirements are met and IT-related risks are incorporated into the overall risk-management policy
options.B: Completely independent of any business strategy
options.C: Focused only on the newest technology regardless of cost or risk
options.D: Managed solely by external vendors with no board oversight

explanation: IT Governance is the first major section of the Guidelines and stresses alignment with business needs and risk management.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Material or systemic cyber incidents under the Cyber Resilience Guidelines must be:

options.A: Kept confidential from all authorities indefinitely
options.B: Immediately reported to the relevant oversight and regulatory authorities (NRB) in accordance with NRB’s reporting requirements
options.C: Reported only after a full year of investigation

explanation: Prompt regulatory notification of material/systemic incidents is a mandatory Response requirement.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072 identifies as a policy objective the promotion of:

options.A: Only traditional agriculture with no technology component
options.B: ICT industry development, e-commerce, convergence of telecommunications/ICT/broadcasting, and the use of ICT for government-service innovation and good governance
options.C: The complete prohibition of any private-sector ICT activity
options.D: Isolation of Nepal from all international ICT standards

explanation: The Policy explicitly lists these developmental and governance-oriented objectives.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, information-security requirements should be incorporated:

options.A: Only after a system has already gone live
options.B: At each stage of the software-development life cycle
options.C: Only in the user-training manual
options.D: Never; security is an optional afterthought

explanation: Security-by-design throughout the SDLC is an explicit expectation of the Guidelines.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines require licensed institutions to maintain testing programmes that include, among other activities:

options.A: Only informal conversations among staff
options.B: Vulnerability assessments, penetration testing and, where appropriate, red-team exercises to validate the cyber-resilience posture
options.C: No technical testing whatsoever
options.D: Only the testing of paper forms

explanation: Testing is one of the three overarching components that must permeate the entire cyber-resilience framework.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, audit trails of critical systems must be:

options.A: Deleted daily to save storage space
options.B: Detailed enough to serve as forensic evidence and must satisfy regulatory and legal requirements
options.C: Accessible to every customer of the bank
options.D: Written only on paper and never digitised

explanation: Robust, forensically usable audit trails are a core control expectation.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072 emphasises conformance, interoperability and standards in telecommunications/ICTs in order to:

options.A: Encourage proprietary lock-in and prevent any interconnection
options.B: Ensure that systems and services can work together reliably across organisational and national boundaries
options.C: Prohibit the use of any international standards
options.D: Limit ICT use exclusively to the Kathmandu Valley

explanation: Interoperability and standards are explicit policy themes intended to support a coherent national ICT ecosystem.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: A licensed institution under the Cyber Resilience Guidelines must have a cyber-incident response capability that covers:

options.A: Only the detection of incidents
options.B: Detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident activity
options.C: Only the issuance of a press release

explanation: A full incident-response lifecycle is required; cooperative arrangements with external response providers are also envisaged.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, a bank should develop and maintain a data-backup and recovery policy that supports:

options.A: The permanent loss of all customer data after any incident
options.B: The ability to restore data and systems in accordance with the institution’s recovery objectives and regulatory expectations
options.C: Backup only of marketing materials
options.D: No off-site copies of any kind

explanation: Backup and recovery policy is one of the twelve core points of the NRB IT Policy that the Guidelines elaborate.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines require that security controls be aligned with recognised standards such as:

options.A: Only internal undocumented practices
options.B: Internationally recognised frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001 is cited as an example of the type of standard expected)
options.C: No standards of any kind
options.D: Only proprietary vendor checklists that cannot be audited

explanation: Alignment with recognised standards is part of the Protection domain of the Guidelines.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, outsourcing of critical IT services requires:

options.A: No due diligence or contractual safeguards
options.B: Appropriate due diligence, contractual clauses covering security and confidentiality, and continued oversight by the bank, because the bank remains responsible for the outsourced functions
options.C: Complete transfer of all regulatory responsibility to the vendor

explanation: Outsourcing management is a dedicated section of the Guidelines; accountability cannot be delegated away.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072’s vision and mission orient national ICT development toward:

options.A: Isolation from global digital trends
options.B: Sustainable development, economic growth, good governance and inclusive access to ICT services
options.C: The exclusive benefit of a single private monopoly
options.D: The prohibition of any broadband infrastructure

explanation: The Policy’s stated vision and mission align ICT with broader national development goals.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the Cyber Resilience Guidelines, situational awareness includes the expectation that an institution will:

options.A: Ignore all external threat intelligence
options.B: Maintain awareness of the threat landscape, share relevant information where appropriate, and use that awareness to adjust its defences
options.C: Rely solely on a single antivirus product with no further monitoring
options.D: Disable all logging to reduce storage costs

explanation: Situational Awareness is one of the three overarching components that must run through the entire framework.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, customers should be made aware of:

options.A: Only the bank’s profit figures
options.B: Electronic frauds together with measures for fraud identification, avoidance and protection
options.C: Nothing related to security

explanation: Customer awareness is an explicit fraud-management requirement.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines require a responsible-disclosure policy so that:

options.A: All vulnerabilities are kept permanently secret from everyone
options.B: Potential vulnerabilities and risks can be disclosed in a controlled manner that helps participants and stakeholders mitigate their own risk and supports overall financial stability
options.C: Only the attacker is informed of the vulnerability
options.D: No disclosure of any kind is ever permitted

explanation: Responsible disclosure balances transparency with the need to avoid enabling further attacks.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, a bank adopting a new technology or system is expected to:

options.A: Deploy it immediately without any risk analysis
options.B: Carry out a detailed risk analysis before adoption, because new technology can introduce new risk exposures
options.C: Ignore all operational risks
options.D: Rely solely on the vendor’s marketing brochure

explanation: Risk analysis before technology adoption is a stated governance expectation.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072 treats access to telecommunications/ICTs for persons with disabilities and specific needs as:

options.A: An optional luxury
options.B: A policy concern that must be addressed so that ICT services are inclusive
options.C: A matter outside the scope of any national policy

explanation: Inclusive access, including for persons with disabilities, is an explicit theme of the Policy.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the Cyber Resilience Guidelines the “Learning and Evolving” component requires institutions to:

options.A: Never change their defences once implemented
options.B: Continuously improve their cyber-resilience posture on the basis of lessons learned from incidents, tests and changes in the threat landscape
options.C: Discard all historical incident data
options.D: Rely solely on static, never-updated policies

explanation: Learning & Evolving is the third overarching component and closes the continuous-improvement loop.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, multi-level security for information is expected to protect:

options.A: Only the physical building
options.B: The confidentiality, integrity and availability of information through layered technical, organisational and physical controls
options.C: Only the marketing website
options.D: Nothing; security is left entirely to end users

explanation: Multi-level information security is one of the twelve core points of the NRB IT Policy.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines expect an institution’s incident-response plan to identify:

options.A: Only the colour of the incident-response team’s uniforms
options.B: Internal and external stakeholders to be notified, decision-making authorities, and the information that must be shared and reported, together with timing
options.C: No stakeholders at all

explanation: Clear escalation, notification and information-sharing arrangements are mandatory elements of the response plan.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, source-code review of critical applications is:

options.A: Prohibited
options.B: Encouraged in order to identify loopholes, coding errors or malicious constructs before the system is implemented; discovered defects must be fixed prior to go-live
options.C: Required only after a successful breach

explanation: Source-code review is an explicit recommendation within the system-acquisition and development section.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072 positions ICT as a tool for:

options.A: Only entertainment
options.B: Sustainable development, economic growth, improved public-service delivery and good governance
options.C: The complete replacement of all human labour
options.D: Isolation of rural communities from digital services

explanation: The Policy’s background and objectives explicitly link ICT to national development and governance goals.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the Cyber Resilience Guidelines, protection of critical assets includes the expectation of:

options.A: No access controls of any kind
options.B: Strong security controls (access control, encryption, network security, etc.) commensurate with the classification and criticality of the assets
options.C: Public disclosure of all encryption keys

explanation: The Protection domain requires a defence-in-depth set of controls aligned with asset criticality.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, a bank’s BCP must include:

options.A: Only a list of employee birthdays
options.B: Prioritisation of critical business functions, incident-handling procedures, resource allocation, and assignment of knowledgeable personnel, and must be reviewed periodically
options.C: No consideration of outsourcing dependencies
options.D: A statement that recovery is impossible

explanation: Detailed, board-approved BCP with periodic review is mandatory.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines treat governance as the foundation that must:

options.A: Be left entirely to junior IT staff with no board involvement
options.B: Ensure that cyber risk is integrated into the overall risk-management framework, with clear roles, accountability and board-approved strategy and risk tolerance
options.C: Ignore all external regulatory expectations
options.D: Focus solely on marketing the institution’s digital channels

explanation: Governance is the first of the five core categories and underpins all other cyber-resilience activities.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, migration from an old system to a new system requires:

options.A: No documentation or testing
options.B: A documented migration policy and methodology that preserve data completeness, integrity, confidentiality and consistency, together with retention of the old system’s audit trail
options.C: Immediate deletion of all historical data
options.D: Reliance on verbal assurances from the vendor only

explanation: Migration controls and preservation of auditability are explicit expectations.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072’s treatment of cloud computing reflects an intention to:

options.A: Prohibit any use of cloud services
options.B: Recognise cloud computing as a relevant technology area within the broader ICT policy framework
options.C: Mandate that every citizen host a personal cloud server

explanation: Cloud computing appears among the policy themes, indicating forward-looking recognition of the technology.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the Cyber Resilience Guidelines, identification of risks includes the expectation that an institution will:

options.A: Assume that no cyber risks exist
options.B: Identify critical operations, assets, threats and vulnerabilities through regular risk assessments so that proportionate controls can be applied
options.C: Perform risk assessment only after a successful breach
options.D: Outsource all risk identification with no internal understanding

explanation: The Identification domain is the analytical foundation for subsequent Protection, Detection and Response activities.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, the board or audit committee must ensure that the IS-audit function has:

options.A: No resources at all
options.B: Sufficient resources and capability to evaluate IT controls with adequate coverage
options.C: Only a single junior staff member with no IT background
options.D: Resources drawn exclusively from the vendor of the core system

explanation: Resource adequacy for IS audit is an explicit board/audit-committee responsibility.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines complement which international guidance?

options.A: No international guidance whatsoever
options.B: The CPMI-IOSCO Guidance on Cyber Resilience for Financial Market Infrastructures (and the underlying PFMI principles)
options.C: Only domestic agricultural guidelines
options.D: A purely national standard with no international reference

explanation: The Guidelines are explicitly positioned as supplemental to the international CPMI-IOSCO cyber-resilience guidance.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the NRB IT Guidelines, information-security education is expected to cover:

options.A: Only the IT department
options.B: Staff (and, where relevant, customers) so that awareness of threats, secure behaviour and institutional policies is maintained
options.C: No one; security education is optional

explanation: Security education is a dedicated section of the Guidelines and supports the human layer of defence.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: In the event of indications of criminal intent (fraud, extortion, etc.) the Cyber Resilience Guidelines expect a licensed institution to:

options.A: Handle the matter solely internally and never involve law enforcement
options.B: Have procedures to escalate investigations to law-enforcement agencies
options.C: Ignore the criminal aspect completely
options.D: Publish all evidence on social media immediately

explanation: Escalation to law enforcement is an explicit expectation when criminality is indicated.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The ICT Policy 2072’s emphasis on ICT in agriculture, education and health reflects a strategy of:

options.A: Restricting ICT to urban financial services only
options.B: Sectoral mainstreaming of ICT so that key development sectors benefit from digital tools and services
options.C: Prohibiting any ICT use outside Kathmandu
options.D: Replacing all traditional knowledge with pure technology

explanation: Sectoral application of ICT is a recurring theme of the Policy’s objectives and strategies.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: According to the NRB IT Guidelines, a well-structured and secured physical IT infrastructure must be accompanied by:

options.A: No documentation of any kind
options.B: Proper documentation so that configuration, dependencies and recovery procedures are known and maintainable
options.C: Documentation written only in a private language unknown to the bank’s own staff
options.D: Documentation that is destroyed after every audit

explanation: Documentation is explicitly paired with physical-infrastructure security in the core policy points.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The Cyber Resilience Guidelines require that an institution’s cyber-resilience strategy and framework be:

options.A: Kept purely oral and never written down
options.B: Documented, approved at the appropriate governance level (board), and aligned with the institution’s overall risk appetite and with NRB’s expectations
options.C: Copied unchanged from a foreign bank without adaptation
options.D: Focused exclusively on marketing digital products

explanation: A board-approved, institution-specific strategy is the starting point of the Governance domain.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: Under the combined reading of the NRB IT Guidelines and the Cyber Resilience Guidelines, a bank’s disaster-recovery and cyber-recovery capabilities must together ensure:

options.A: That no recovery is ever attempted
options.B: That critical services can be resumed within the institution’s stated RTO/RPO objectives and, for cyber incidents affecting critical payment operations, within the two-hour resumption target where practicable
options.C: That recovery is possible only after several years
options.D: That only non-critical marketing systems are recovered

explanation: The two sets of guidelines together impose both general BCP/DRP obligations and specific cyber-resumption expectations.

topic: 9.1 Nepal-specific policies (ICT Policy 2072, NRB IT Guidelines, Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023)
question: The overarching policy intent that links the ICT Policy 2072, the NRB IT Guidelines and the Cyber Resilience Guidelines 2023 is to:

options.A: Discourage any use of information technology in Nepal
options.B: Promote the safe, secure, reliable and inclusive use of ICT and digital financial services so that national development and financial-system stability are strengthened
options.C: Create barriers that prevent ordinary citizens from accessing digital services
options.D: Transfer all cyber risk exclusively onto individual consumers with no institutional responsibility

explanation: All three instruments, despite different scopes, share the goal of enabling beneficial digital transformation while managing the associated risks.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Under the Electronic Transactions Act, 2063, an electronic record is given the same legal recognition as a paper document provided that:

options.A: It is printed on paper within 24 hours
options.B: It remains accessible and usable for subsequent reference
options.C: It is signed only with a wet-ink signature
options.D: It is stored exclusively on a foreign server

explanation: Section 3 of ETA 2063 accords legal validity to electronic records that can be retrieved for later reference.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A digital signature under ETA 2063 has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature when it is created using:

options.A: A simple scanned image of a signature
options.B: An asymmetric cryptosystem and is authenticated by a Digital Signature Certificate issued by a licensed Certifying Authority
options.C: Any username and password combination
options.D: A biometric fingerprint alone without any certificate

explanation: Section 4 requires an asymmetric cryptosystem and a certificate from a CA licensed by the Controller.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Office of the Controller of Certifying Authorities (OCCA) under ETA 2063 is responsible for:

options.A: Issuing every digital signature certificate directly to citizens
options.B: Licensing, supervising and regulating Certifying Authorities, and setting standards for the public-key infrastructure
options.C: Operating the core banking systems of all commercial banks
options.D: Hearing all cyber-crime trials as a court of first instance

explanation: The Controller (OCCA) sits at the apex of the PKI hierarchy and oversees licensed Certifying Authorities.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Unauthorised access to a computer system or computer material (commonly called hacking) under Section 45 of ETA 2063 is punishable by:

options.A: A maximum fine of NPR 10,000 only
options.B: Imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to NPR 200,000 or both
options.C: Only a written warning

explanation: Section 45 prescribes up to 3 years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of up to NPR 2 lakh.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Publication of illegal material in electronic form (content contrary to public morality, that spreads hatred, etc.) under Section 47 of ETA 2063 carries a maximum penalty of:

options.A: Six months’ imprisonment only
options.B: Up to five years’ imprisonment or a fine up to NPR 100,000 or both
options.C: Only a fine of NPR 5,000

explanation: Section 47 is one of the most frequently invoked provisions and carries the highest imprisonment term among the common cyber offences.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Individual Privacy Act, 2075 was enacted primarily to give effect to which constitutional right?

options.A: Right to free speech only
options.B: Right to privacy guaranteed by Article 28 of the Constitution of Nepal
options.C: Right to property exclusively

explanation: The Privacy Act operationalises the fundamental right to privacy recognised in Article 28.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Under the Privacy Act 2075, collection, storage, processing or sharing of an individual’s private information generally requires:

options.A: No consent of any kind
options.B: Prior informed consent of the individual (or legal authority where consent is not required by law)
options.C: Only the consent of the data controller’s shareholders
options.D: A court order in every single case

explanation: Consent (together with purpose limitation and security) is a core principle of the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A Certifying Authority under ETA 2063 is an entity that:

options.A: Issues digital signature certificates after being licensed by the Controller
options.B: Operates exclusively as a commercial bank
options.C: Has the power to arrest cyber-crime suspects
options.D: Sets the monetary policy of Nepal

explanation: CAs are licensed intermediaries that issue and manage digital-signature certificates under the Controller’s oversight.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Damage to a computer or information system under Section 46 of ETA 2063 is punishable by:

options.A: Only a civil suit for damages
options.B: Imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to NPR 200,000 or both
options.C: A maximum fine of NPR 1,000
options.D: No penalty if the damage is temporary

explanation: Section 46 covers intentional damage to computer systems or data and carries the standard 3-year / NPR 2-lakh ceiling.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Information Technology Tribunal established under ETA 2063 is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Licensing commercial banks
options.B: Adjudicating offences and disputes arising under the Electronic Transactions Act
options.C: Issuing digital signature certificates to the general public

explanation: Chapter 9 of the Act creates specialised tribunals (IT Tribunal and Appellate Tribunal) for cyber-related matters.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
