question: Under the Privacy Act 2075, an individual has the right to:

options.A: Demand that all personal data held by any organisation be permanently deleted without any procedure
options.B: Access personal data held about him or her and request correction of inaccurate data
options.C: Compel any private company to publish all of its internal algorithms
options.D: Prevent any government agency from ever collecting any data

explanation: Rights of access and rectification are explicitly recognised under the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Pirating, destroying or altering computer source code under Section 44 of ETA 2063 is punishable by:

options.A: A maximum of six months’ imprisonment
options.B: Imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to NPR 200,000 or both
options.C: Only a fine of NPR 5,000

explanation: Section 44 protects the integrity of source code with the same penalty ceiling as unauthorised access and system damage.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A subscriber under ETA 2063 is required to generate a key pair using:

options.A: A symmetric cipher only
options.B: A secure asymmetric cryptographic system
options.C: A simple password hash with no public key

explanation: The Act mandates the use of asymmetric cryptography for digital signatures.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Breach of confidentiality by a person who has access to confidential electronic information under Section 48 of ETA 2063 is punishable by:

options.A: Life imprisonment
options.B: Imprisonment up to two years or a fine (commonly cited up to NPR 100,000 / 10,000 depending on the exact text) or both
options.C: Only a civil penalty

explanation: Section 48 criminalises unauthorised disclosure of confidential information obtained in the course of duties.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Computer fraud under ETA 2063 (false digital signatures, fraudulent electronic transactions, etc.) is typically punishable by:

options.A: Only a warning letter
options.B: Imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to NPR 100,000 or both
options.C: A mandatory ten-year sentence

explanation: Fraudulent use of electronic means for wrongful gain is criminalised with a two-year / NPR 1-lakh ceiling in the commonly cited provisions.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Sensitive personal data under the Privacy Act 2075 (caste, ethnicity, religion, biometric data, health records, sexual orientation, etc.) generally requires:

options.A: No special protection beyond ordinary personal data
options.B: Heightened protection and, in most cases, explicit consent before processing
options.C: Mandatory public disclosure

explanation: The Act accords additional safeguards to categories of data that are inherently more privacy-sensitive.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: An offence committed outside Nepal that affects a computer system or network located in Nepal may, under ETA 2063:

options.A: Never be prosecuted in Nepal
options.B: Be prosecuted in Nepal if the Act’s extraterritorial provisions are attracted
options.C: Be prosecuted only by the foreign state
options.D: Result only in a diplomatic protest

explanation: The Act contains extraterritorial reach for offences that impact systems or data within Nepal.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The primary purpose of a Digital Signature Certificate issued by a licensed CA is to:

options.A: Serve as a national identity card
options.B: Bind a public key to the identity of the subscriber and thereby enable verification of digital signatures
options.C: Replace the need for any password
options.D: Grant the holder unrestricted access to all government databases

explanation: The certificate is the trust anchor that links a public key to a verified identity.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Under the Privacy Act 2075, an organisation that collects personal data must:

options.A: Use the data for any purpose it later decides
options.B: Inform the individual of the purpose, obtain consent where required, and use the data only for the stated purpose while keeping it secure
options.C: Share the data freely with any third party
options.D: Store the data in clear text on publicly accessible servers

explanation: Purpose limitation, consent and security are core obligations of data controllers under the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Abetment of a computer-related offence under ETA 2063 is generally punishable by:

options.A: The same maximum penalty as the principal offence in every case
options.B: A lighter penalty (commonly up to six months’ imprisonment or a fine up to NPR 50,000)
options.C: No penalty at all

explanation: Abetment carries a reduced but still criminal sanction under the Act’s penalty scheme.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: When a corporate body commits an offence under ETA 2063, liability typically attaches to:

options.A: Only the lowest-ranking employee
options.B: The person in charge of the organisation (and the body itself) unless that person can prove lack of knowledge or due diligence
options.C: Only the shareholders

explanation: Corporate-offence provisions hold the person responsible for the conduct of business of the body corporate accountable.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Privacy Act 2075 protects privacy in relation to which of the following domains?

options.A: Only financial transactions
options.B: Body, residence, property, documents, data, correspondence and character
options.C: Only political opinions
options.D: Only data stored on government servers

explanation: The Act elaborates the constitutional right to privacy across these seven classic domains.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A digital signature created without a certificate from a licensed Certifying Authority under ETA 2063:

options.A: Automatically has the same legal force as a handwritten signature
options.B: Does not enjoy the statutory equivalence to a handwritten signature conferred by Section 4
options.C: Is the only form of signature recognised by Nepali courts
options.D: Is prohibited from being used in any private contract

explanation: Statutory legal equivalence is conditioned on the use of a licensed CA certificate and asymmetric cryptography.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Devices used in the commission of an offence under ETA 2063 may be:

options.A: Returned to the offender immediately after arrest
options.B: Subject to confiscation by the competent authority
options.C: Sold by the offender to recover losses

explanation: The Act provides for confiscation of instrumentalities of cyber offences.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Unauthorised disclosure of private information under the Privacy Act 2075 can attract:

options.A: Only a civil claim for damages
options.B: Imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to NPR 30,000 or both (as commonly cited)
options.C: No sanction of any kind

explanation: The Act contains criminal penalties for serious breaches of privacy obligations.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Controller under ETA 2063 may, in special circumstances, order a subscriber to:

options.A: Destroy all public keys permanently
options.B: Deposit the private key with the Controller when required for investigation or other legally authorised purposes
options.C: Publish the private key on a public website
options.D: Never use a digital signature again

explanation: Limited key-escrow powers exist for the Controller under defined conditions.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: False information given to obtain a digital-signature certificate or licence under ETA 2063 is an offence punishable by:

options.A: Only a civil fine
options.B: Imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to NPR 100,000 or both
options.C: No penalty if the certificate is later revoked

explanation: Providing false particulars in the certificate-issuance process is itself criminalised.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The legal recognition of electronic records and digital signatures under ETA 2063 is intended primarily to:

options.A: Discourage all electronic commerce
options.B: Provide a statutory foundation for e-commerce, e-governance and secure electronic transactions
options.C: Replace the entire Civil Code

explanation: The Act’s core policy goal is to enable trustworthy electronic transactions and e-government services.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Under the Privacy Act 2075, personal information includes data relating to:

options.A: Only a person’s bank balance
options.B: Caste, ethnicity, religion, education, biometric identifiers, financial details, health, and other identifying attributes
options.C: Only publicly available news articles
options.D: Only data that the individual has already posted on social media

explanation: The Act adopts a broad definition of personal information covering both ordinary and sensitive categories.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Submission or display of a false licence or digital-signature certificate under ETA 2063 is punishable by:

options.A: Only a verbal reprimand
options.B: Imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to NPR 100,000 or both
options.C: No criminal consequence

explanation: Forgery or misuse of certificates and licences is specifically criminalised.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The asymmetric cryptosystem required for a statutory digital signature under ETA 2063 relies on:

options.A: A single shared secret key for both signing and verification
options.B: A mathematically related public-key / private-key pair, where the private key creates the signature and the public key verifies it
options.C: Only a password hash

explanation: Asymmetric (public-key) cryptography is the technical foundation of the digital-signature scheme recognised by the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: An organisation that processes personal data under the Privacy Act 2075 must store that data:

options.A: In clear text on any publicly reachable server
options.B: Securely, with appropriate technical and organisational measures to prevent unauthorised access, alteration or disclosure
options.C: Only on paper and never electronically
options.D: Without any retention limit or purpose limitation

explanation: Security of personal data is an explicit obligation of entities that collect and process such data.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Information Technology Appellate Tribunal under ETA 2063 hears:

options.A: All civil property disputes in Nepal
options.B: Appeals against decisions of the Information Technology Tribunal and certain regulatory decisions under the Act
options.C: Only tax appeals

explanation: The Appellate Tribunal provides a specialised second tier of adjudication for ETA matters.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Repeat offences under ETA 2063 generally attract:

options.A: A lighter penalty than the first offence
options.B: An enhanced penalty (commonly one-and-a-half times the original maximum)
options.C: No additional consequence

explanation: The Act provides for aggravated punishment on subsequent convictions.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Privacy Act 2075 permits collection of personal data by an authorised body only after:

options.A: The data have already been published on social media
options.B: Informing the individual of the purpose and obtaining consent (or relying on another lawful ground where consent is not required)
options.C: A majority vote of the organisation’s board without any notice to the individual
options.D: The individual has left the country

explanation: Transparency and consent (or equivalent lawful basis) are prerequisites for legitimate processing.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A digital signature under ETA 2063 serves which two primary security functions?

options.A: Confidentiality and availability only
options.B: Authentication of the signatory and integrity of the signed record
options.C: Only non-repudiation without any integrity check
options.D: Only encryption of the entire message

explanation: A properly created digital signature proves who signed and that the content has not been altered.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Non-submission of prescribed statements or documents required under ETA 2063 can result in:

options.A: A fine (commonly up to NPR 50,000)
options.B: Automatic acquittal of all other charges
options.C: A mandatory prison term of ten years

explanation: Procedural non-compliance itself carries a monetary penalty under the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Privacy Act 2075’s protection of correspondence includes:

options.A: Only letters sent by post
options.B: Communications transmitted by electronic or other means, so that unauthorised interception or disclosure is restricted
options.C: Only face-to-face conversations

explanation: The Act’s concept of correspondence privacy extends to electronic communications.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Licensing of a Certifying Authority under ETA 2063 is performed by:

options.A: Any commercial bank
options.B: The Controller of Certifying Authorities
options.C: The Supreme Court of Nepal
options.D: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority exclusively for all CAs

explanation: The Controller is the statutory licensing and supervisory authority for CAs.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: An offence against a government computer system under ETA 2063 may attract:

options.A: A reduced penalty compared with offences against private systems
options.B: An enhanced penalty (commonly an additional 50 % of the ordinary maximum)
options.C: No penalty at all
options.D: Only a civil fine paid to the government

explanation: Offences involving government systems are treated as aggravated under the Act.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Privacy Act 2075 does not create a dedicated independent Data Protection Authority; enforcement is primarily through:

options.A: A specialised privacy tribunal with exclusive jurisdiction
options.B: Ordinary courts (District Courts) and other competent authorities under the Act
options.C: Only the Office of the Controller of Certifying Authorities
options.D: Self-regulation by private companies with no state involvement

explanation: Nepal’s privacy regime currently relies on the ordinary court system rather than a specialised DPA.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A subscriber who loses control of the private key corresponding to a digital-signature certificate should:

options.A: Continue using the certificate indefinitely
options.B: Promptly request suspension or revocation of the certificate from the issuing Certifying Authority
options.C: Publish the private key so that others can use it
options.D: Ignore the loss because private keys cannot be compromised

explanation: Compromise of the private key undermines the security of all signatures; revocation is the prescribed remedy.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The combined effect of ETA 2063 and the Privacy Act 2075 on a bank that processes customer data electronically is that the bank must:

options.A: Ignore both statutes because banking is regulated only by NRB
options.B: Ensure legal validity of electronic records and signatures while also respecting consent, purpose limitation and security obligations for personal data
options.C: Store all customer data in clear text for regulatory inspection
options.D: Refuse to use any electronic channel

explanation: Banks operate under both the electronic-transactions regime and the privacy regime (in addition to NRB directives).

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Publication of material that spreads hatred against any caste, community, religion or nationality in electronic form is criminalised under:

options.A: Only the Copyright Act
options.B: Section 47 of the Electronic Transactions Act 2063 (among other possible overlapping provisions)
options.C: Only the Civil Code

explanation: Section 47 explicitly covers electronic publication of content that spreads hatred or is otherwise illegal.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The statutory digital signature recognised by ETA 2063 provides non-repudiation because:

options.A: The private key is known to everyone
options.B: Only the holder of the corresponding private key could have created the signature, and the certificate links that key to an identified subscriber
options.C: The signature can be forged by anyone with the public key

explanation: Non-repudiation rests on the secrecy of the private key and the trustworthy binding of the public key to identity via the certificate.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: Under the Privacy Act 2075, a public body that holds personal data must, upon a lawful request by the data subject:

options.A: Refuse all access requests as a matter of policy
options.B: Provide access to the personal data (subject to any statutory exceptions) and correct inaccurate data when the request is properly supported
options.C: Charge an unlimited fee for every access request
options.D: Delete the data without any verification

explanation: Access and correction rights are enforceable against entities that hold personal data.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Electronic Transactions Act 2063 contains how many chapters?

options.A: Five
options.B: Twelve (with approximately 80 sections)
options.C: Three

explanation: ETA 2063 is structured in 12 chapters covering validity, certification, offences, tribunals and related matters.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: A bank that issues a digital-signature certificate without being licensed as a Certifying Authority under ETA 2063 would be:

options.A: Acting fully within the law
options.B: Committing an offence (operating without the required licence)
options.C: Exempt because it is a bank
options.D: Regulated only by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority for this purpose

explanation: Only entities licensed by the Controller may lawfully act as Certifying Authorities.

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The Privacy Act 2075 and ETA 2063 together imply that a financial institution’s electronic customer records must be:

options.A: Publicly downloadable by anyone
options.B: Kept confidential, processed only for lawful purposes with appropriate consent or authority, and protected by security measures consistent with both privacy and electronic-transactions obligations
options.C: Deleted every 24 hours regardless of regulatory retention requirements

explanation: Banks must satisfy both the privacy obligations of the Privacy Act and the integrity/security expectations of the electronic-transactions regime (and NRB directives).

topic: 9.2 Electronic Transactions Act, Digital Signatures, Privacy Act & Cyber Law
question: The fundamental policy objective that unites the Electronic Transactions Act 2063 and the Privacy Act 2075 is to:

options.A: Prohibit all electronic activity in Nepal
options.B: Enable trustworthy electronic transactions and digital services while protecting the privacy and security of individuals’ personal information
options.C: Transfer all responsibility for data protection solely onto end users
options.D: Eliminate the need for any regulatory oversight of digital systems

explanation: Both statutes aim to support digital transformation while establishing legal safeguards for authenticity, integrity and privacy.
